News.title: ‘Attacker who rammed Aussie MP with car is identified’ as politician still fights for life in hospital & could lose legs
News.content:
Next

THE man who allegedly rammed an Australian politician with his car in a horror “deliberate” attack has been identified, reports say.

Independent MP Helen Haines, 65, was struck by the Toyota Land Cruiser “at least three times” and pinned underneath on Monday outside her regional Victoria office.



The man allegedly behind the wheel was Brendan Nugent, 43, according to The Age newspaper.

Nugent is from Tarrawingee – a short 15-minute drive from Wangaratta where the attack unfolded – and has a history of activism in the area.



His social media includes a number of anti-Israel and anti-logging posts.

One source told the paper he strayed into “darker” things after once protesting logging in the local forest.

The horrific attack is being probed by counter-terror cops and Aussie spies – ASIO.

Haines was taking items out of her car boot near her office when she was hit by the Toyota Landcruiser at 3.30pm local time, according to police.



Cody Lepoidevin was working across the road from Haines’ Wangaratta office at the time of the attack when he heard screams.

Lepoidevin said he saw the Land Cruiser drive into Haines at least three times before the attacker tried to flee.

He told The Age: “I was there to restrain him against the wall, but yeah, more or less they got him out of the car.

“He was quite delirious, I suspect pretty riddled with drugs, but yeah, from there on it was pretty much just blur. We did what we could.”

Australian prime minister Anthony Albanese described the incident as an “attack” and said counter-terrorism units were investigating the ordeal.



He said: “This wasn’t an accident. There was a deliberate act it would appear.”

Witnesses said the driver passed her in a car park before doing a U-turn and ramming the mum-of-three politician.

A local barber told 7News he pulled the driver from the car and allegedly wrestled him to the ground after finding a flick knife in his pocket.



The MP was airlifted to a Melbourne hospital with “severe” lower body injuries and underwent surgery on Monday night.

Reports say she could lose both her legs as a result of the critical injuries.

They added: “A knife was located by police and seized from inside the Toyota.



“It is not known yet if the parties are known to each other.”

The suspect is due to be quizzed by investigators tonight at Wangaratta Police Station.

Haines’ family thanked the “swift assistance” of bystanders, police and medical workers for responding to the suspected attack.

They said on Monday night: “Our family and Helen’s staff will be making no further comment at this time and ask that their privacy be respected by the public and the media.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Haines, a former health professional before her political career, was first elected as the Independent Federal Member for Indi in 2019.



Albanese also said Haines was “fiercely intelligent, but most importantly… a thoroughly decent human being, full of integrity and respected right across the Parliament and by everyone who comes into contact with her”.

News.title: Graffiti pranksters mocking celebs like Susanna Reid & Alan Carr on subway walls vow to beat killjoy council’s whitewash
News.content:
Next

GRAFFITI artists who have been skewering celebs in a subway art campaign say they plan to stay a step ahead of council workmen determined to whitewash them out of existence.

The Mellow Birds have caused hilarity with suburban scrawling that pokes fun at family TV favourites like Susanna Reid, Denise Welch, Olly Murs and Stacey Dooley.



Residents of the Newcastle upon Tyne suburb of West Denton have been kept chuckling for weeks by the bizarre messages which started to appear in subways – however the local council isn’t laughing.

They sent workmen out to cover over messages such as: “Ross Kemp dabs Zoflora behind his ears,” and “Alan Carr sprays Joop in the air and shimmies through it”.





Other messages wrote “Mel B has potato smilies at least three times a week,” and “Jamelia spells swear words with the lettered candles in Card Factory.”

Although locals lapped up the inoffensive graffiti, councillors have condemned it and a whitewash was ordered.



However, within days, the mystery artists – suspected to be female – struck again in the dead of night with another slew of whacky observations.

And despite a man being arrested on suspicion of criminal damage last week, a further slew of scrawlings have appeared today, with Traitors host Claudia Winkleman, Hollywood star Tom Hardy and Joey Essex among the latest celebs featured.

The Sun tracked down the mystery artists who would only speak anonymously via messenger.

They confirmed themselves as people “of a certain age” who were enjoying giving the people of Newcastle and thousands following on social media a good laugh.



However, they hit back at the council for failing to see the humour in their work, adding: “This is bringing communities together in a way that nothing of late has and by jove we need to have a laugh in these trying times, you know?”

Many locals have jumped to defend the mystery artists, branding their work the “modern day Bayeux Tapestry”.

Alan and Susan Todd stopped to laugh at their latest piece of work: “Susanna Reid eats Pukka pies in bed.”

One local, Alan, 66, said: “Whenever we come this way we stop to read the latest bits of graffiti, to be honest it’s given us a really good laugh.



“The council have been down and whitewashed over it but whoever these people are they’ve been pretty quick to come back and start again.

“I can’t see a problem with it, it’s all pretty clean, harmless fun.”

Susan, also 66, said: “I know you’re not supposed to go around scrawling graffiti, everyone knows that, but these subways have always had it and at least this is giving everyone a laugh.

“It’s better than kids writing horrible stuff about each other and in one of the local subways the council brought in an artist to decorate it. I can’t see that this is much different.”



Carly Best, 37, said: “I always like to stop and have a laugh at the latest messages from these guys.

“I hope the council don’t come and paint over it again – I’m sure they’ll be back if that happens though.”

Californian Jay Nabonne, 61, moved to Newcastle 13 years ago and he has also been bemused by the graffiti.

He laughed: “I have to say I’ve never seen anything like it before.



“I think this is the North East sense of humour showing itself, it’s not really offensive.”

Elizabeth Orrell, 63, was on her way back from the gym and stopped to read the latest Mellow Birds handiwork.

She said: “It’s taken the attention away from kids who write horrible stuff in the subways and it’s putting a smile on people’s faces.

“The people they reference are all of a certain age and appeal to a certain audience. I think the people responsible are older and possibly women.”



Philip Coghill, 31, stopped on his way to the local McDonald’s.

He said: “I’ve never seen this before, it’s really strange but it’s a good laugh and it isn’t offending anyone.

“It’s so ridiculous that I don’t think it would even upset the celebrities who are being written about.”

The graffiti started to appear around three weeks ago and was initially intended as fan art for the London-based singer/songwriter Rose Gray, who has had a string of minor club hits.



The Mellow Birds are fans and began writing messages about Rose in the hope of spreading the word about her work.

That spiralled into a stream of graffiti about unconnected celebs and the feedback on social media prompted them to continue adding to their subway scrawling.

The Mellow Birds – who would not confirm their age, gender or how many of them are involved – said: “The work itself started rather innocently, you walk through these communal areas and see the usual tags, people’s street names or gangs ya ya and you think, well I could do better than that.

“And then eventually, what started as a perfectly innocent joke to promote the latest Rose Gray single became almost a cultural event, bigger than us.



“We must stress, however, that neither Rose Gray, or her label, have any involvement.

“It’s never lost on anyone, involved or not, that it comes at a cost to remove, however again I’d love to see some comical response from the council and have them acknowledge the reception it has had, and genuinely collaborate with it.

“The response has been out of this world, none of it is meant with any malice.

“The abysmal and entirely banal suggestions are what give them legs, we feel anyway.



“But I would like to take a genuine opportunity to address the officials involved in this saga.

“To confirm, we nor anyone else involved in this are the enemy, we appreciate that this is a crime, of course we do.

“And it’s abundantly clear that the council do not enjoy the efforts or see the humour in it, from a procedural perspective at the very least.

“But I’d stress again that this is bringing communities together in a way that nothing of late has, and by jove we need to have a laugh in these trying times, you know?



“So I do extend an olive branch to Newcastle City Council.”

Councillor Peter Lovatt, Newcastle City Council’s Cabinet Member for Neighbourhoods and Local Services, has urged anyone who knows who is responsible to report them to police.

He said: “We are aware of the graffiti in West Denton and have taken immediate action to ensure it is removed as quickly as possible.

“This type of graffiti is unacceptable. It damages public spaces, blights our communities and creates an unnecessary cost to taxpayers through the resources required to remove it.



“It is a form of criminal damage and a recordable offence. Anyone responsible for vandalising property could face police action, including arrest and prosecution.

“We would urge anyone with information about those responsible to report it to Northumbria Police.

“The council has a zero-tolerance approach to offensive graffiti and will always act swiftly to remove it.”

Cllr Peter Lovatt, Cabinet Member for Neighbourhoods and Local Services, Newcastle City Council: “We understand that many people have found the graffiti funny but we would ask you to consider the impact on those living in the community.

“Some of the graffiti was over the top of artwork produced by children in the community, and other bits of graffiti are on the side of people’s homes.



“We would ask that the person responsible considers the impact on those children whose art was destroyed, or the residents having to call us out to clean their homes, or the Newcastle council tax payers ultimately footing the bill for our call outs.

“West Denton is a proud community and nobody should be the butt of a joke for the benefit of those who have never stepped foot there.

“That isn’t a lack of humour, that’s showing respect to the people we are here to serve.”

He added: “This type of graffiti is unacceptable. It damages public spaces, blights our communities and creates an unnecessary cost to taxpayers through the resources required to remove it. It is a form of criminal damage and a recordable offence.”

A Northumbria Police spokesman said: “On Monday we arrested a man on suspicion of criminal damage in relation to graffiti in the West Denton area of Newcastle.



“In interview the man, aged 33, admitted carrying out the vandalism and he has now been referred for an out of court disposal.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Police have also condemned his behaviour.

The spokesman added: “Anti-social behaviour of this nature is completely unacceptable and alongside our partners we will always look to take action when we are made aware of it.”

News.title: ‘Loving father’ who was ‘murdered’ at popular UK caravan park is pictured as family pay tribute
News.content:
'DEEPLY MISSED' ‘Loving father’ who was ‘murdered’ at popular UK caravan park is pictured as family pay tribute







Next

A MAN allegedly murdered at a holiday caravan park has been named, as tributes pour in for the “loving father”.

Lee Jackson, 40, died last week after the incident at Valley Farm Holiday Park in Clacton, Essex.



Emergency services scrambled to the park on the evening of October 14.

Tragically, the dad-of-four was discovered with fatal injuries and could not be saved.



Lee has been remembered as bringing “happiness to everyone around him”.

In a statement released yesterday, his family said: “Lee Andrew Jackson was a loving father of four who brought laughter, joy, and happiness to everyone around him.



“Our son will be deeply missed by his family and friends.”

Over the weekend, Daniel Fox was charged in connection with Lee’s alleged murder.



The 40-year-old was also charged with three counts of assaulting an emergency worker, two counts of making threats to kill, and one count of burglary.

Detective Inspector Tim Coyles, who’s leading the investigation, said: “Specialist officers continue to support the victim’s family.

“I want to thank my team for their work enabling us to get to this stage swiftly.

“I know this incident has caused a great deal of shock within the community around the holiday park and I want to thank the public for their support and understanding.”

Essex Police have urged anyone with information relating to the incident to contact them immediately.

News.title: Mass illegal immigration, an eye-watering welfare bill, war in Europe but Burnham is talking about noise on the Tube
News.content:
Next

YOU know those small annoyances in life that drive everyone completely mad? Andy Burnham is here to help.

Yesterday he promised to stop headphone-dodging passengers blaring out music on trains and buses.



Today he is pledging to prevent jobsworth parking wardens handing out petty fines for minor infractions.

He is also banning thousands of serious offenders detained in mental hospitals claiming benefits while their living costs are met by the NHS.



The PM reckons these “everyday fixes” of mind-bending problems will win him the support of exasperated voters.

There is no doubt these common-sense solutions will be welcomed by many, but to what effect?



There is a danger that these tweaks are dismissed as small beer to Brits impatient for change on the real issues confronting the country.

Mass illegal immigration, an eye-watering welfare bill, war in Europe… and you’re talking about noise on the Tube, Prime Minister?

Kemi Badenoch will today try to increase the pressure on Mr Burnham over one of those problems he is facing: our huge national debt.

At a press conference in London, she will say: “Problems have caught up with us that we can no longer afford to run away from. First and foremost, that means living within our means.”



In short, the Tory leader is demanding massive cuts to public spending to start to bring down our crippling debts.

But that currently looks impossible given the resistance that will be put up by Mr Burnham’s Labour MPs.

The PM’s left-wing backbenchers have already flexed their muscles to force climbdowns on other issues like immigration.

Yet if Mr Burnham thinks he can duck hard decisions to fix the economy, he risks the wrath of the electorate.

And he only needs to look across the Channel to see the perils of letting the economy teeter on the edge of breaking point…

News.title: Matthew McConaughey flirts with possible presidential run as actor slams two-party system ahead of midterms
News.content:
Next

INTERSTELLAR star Matthew McConaughey is rumoured to be considering running for the US presidency.

It comes after the True Detective actor, 56, released a six-minute video backing independent candidates ahead of the midterm elections.



The Oscar winner argued that voters needed alternatives to the Democrats and Republicans, especially as frustration with the two-party system grows.

He said: “I am not here today to endorse a candidate or a party.



“I am here endorsing two things: fairness and reality.

“Independent does not mean you’re middle of the road. Independent is the original road. Before there was ever a Republican or Democrat, there was an American.”

He added that a fair fight required representation beyond the same two parties competing repeatedly.

Polling figures added context to his argument.



A CNN poll released in June found that 47 per cent of voters identified with neither major party.

A Gallup poll cited in coverage of his remarks found that 45 per cent of Americans identified as independents, compared with 27 per cent each for Democrats and Republicans.

McConaughey, who lives in Austin, Texas, with his wife and children, previously considered a run for Texas governor in 2021 but later decided he wasn’t ready.



Several political commentators interpreted the actor’s comments as him laying the groundwork to make a run as an independent candidate in 2028.

Adam Wren of Politico’s Playbook Podcast said: “The fact that he is talking about independent candidates leads a lot of people to think perhaps he wants to stage an independent run in 2028 and beyond.”

Link Lauren, a conservative political influencer, was critical of McConaughey’s intentions.

He said: “Now he seems to be laying a foundation to run as an independent in 2028, acting like he’s the first to do it.

“He will get eaten alive if he runs for president. He can’t take the heat.”



McConaughey flirted with the idea of a presidential run in 2022, saying if he ended up on the ballot it would be because the path “chose him”.

He continued: “We get pulled into things… It’s inevitable. I didn’t choose it, it chose me.”

McConaughey also claimed he was on a “learning tour” while visiting the National Governors Association summer meeting in July 2024.

News.title: Cabinet row erupts after Energy Sec SLAMS Shabana Mahmood’s plans to make foreigners wait longer for permanent residency
News.content:
Next

A CABINET row over immigration reforms intensified after Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh attacked plans to make foreigners wait longer for permanent residency.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood had wanted to double the time migrants must live in the UK before being eligible for indefinite leave to remain from five to ten years — and apply it retrospectively to those already here.



But Ms Fahnbulleh warned extending the wait was a threat to “building cohesion” and said Labour must “challenge divisive rhetoric”.

She said Labour must “raise the level of debate” and “challenge divisive rhetoric” over immigration.



Ms Mahmood had already been expected to water down her plans after a backlash from senior Labour MPs.

Deputy Prime Minister Angela Rayner had already criticised the policy as “un-British” before Ms Fahnbulleh threw her weight behind the immigration rebellion.



In a letter to her constituents in Peckham, South East London, Ms Fahnbulleh said: “If we continually prolong the time people have to wait for settlement, we can also prolong the process of building cohesion.”

Allies of Ms Fahnbulleh said the statement was poorly-worded and would be changed on her constituency website.



Tory Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp last night said: “Labour’s Cabinet members are openly campaigning against their own government’s supposed immigration policy.

“Miattah Fahnbulleh says she opposes a longer time for immigrants to get permanent settlement – the opposite of Shabana Mahmood’s claimed policy.

“Shabana Mahmood has already delayed implementing her own policy, allowing two hundred thousand immigrants to stay permanently and claim benefits.

“Instead of being tough as she said she would be, she is running scared of Angela Rayner and the Labour left.”

News.title: Shakespeare’s plays set to be turned into video games in drive to get more kids reading the Bard’s works
News.content:
Next

THE works of William Shakespeare are set to be turned into video games – in a drive to get kids reading the Bard’s plays.

University boffins have been awarded £590,000 to investigate whether games can make the writer’s series of tragedies, comedies and romances more accessible for young audiences.



The project, called The Shakespeare Arcade, is to be the first large-scale study of how video games can support the teaching of his works.

Professor Erin Sullivan, of the Shakespeare Institute at the University of Birmingham, said: “Shakespeare and video games might at first seem like strange bedfellows, but the truth is there is a long and rich tradition of adapting Shakespeare’s plays to new media.



“The Shakespeare Arcade will introduce the public to the world of Shakespeare-inspired video games and highlight how game developers might use classic texts in the future.”

Several games have already gone on the market with their plots based on Shakespeare plays.



These include This Way Madness Lies, a role-playing video game where players control a group of girls who help Shakespeare’s Romeo fight off monsters.

Another game, Elsinore, follows the character of Ophelia from Hamlet.

An adventure video game, called The Book of Watermarks, was strongly influenced by the Bard’s 1611 play The Tempest.

Dr Sarah Olive, senior lecturer in communication and culture at Aston University, said: “Educators have always drawn on the latest technologies to engage students and facilitate learning, from cinefilm to chatbots.



“The Shakespeare Arcade is an exciting opportunity to expand existing resources and pedagogies for teaching his works and literary classics more widely.”

In 2021, Shakespeare’s plays were turned into virtual reality experiences where fans could experience the settings of his plays by wearing an interactive headset.

News.title: Shocking moment Jewish lady punched in face as man, 33, arrested over ‘antisemitic hate crime’ after ‘attacking’ three
News.content:
Next

THIS is the shocking moment a Jewish lady appears to be punched in the face, as cops arrest a man over an alleged antisemitic hate crime, after three were apparently attacked.

All the women were allegedly assaulted in the Clapton Common area of Hackney, east London, this afternoon, October 19.



One of the women contacted Shomrim, the volunteer Jewish security organisation, who arrived within 30 seconds and witnessed a second alleged assault on another Jewish lady.

The organisation then detained the man and alerted the Met Police, who arrived at 1.40pm.



The cops have confirmed that at least three women were assaulted.

One of the women was pushing her young baby in a pram at the time of the attack.



All the women are believed to have suffered minor injuries.

Cops arrested a 33-year-old man on suspicion of racially-aggravated common assault.



The Met Police is treating the incident as a suspected antisemitic hate crime and officers are keen to hear from any other people who may have been assaulted.

The suspect was subsequently further arrested on suspicion of causing grievous bodily harm, in connection with an unrelated assault on a woman, who is believed to be known to him, in the Islington area on October 16.

He remains in police custody.

Chief Inspector Erica Crawshaw of the Metropolitan Police said: “This was an alarming and distressing incident and we are grateful to our partners in the Shomrim for detaining a suspect prior to the arrival of officers.

“We have launched an investigation and would ask that anyone with information that could help police, or any victims who have not yet come forward, contact us as soon as possible.



“Antisemitic behaviour and hate crime of any kind will not be tolerated.

“We recognise the concern that this incident will have caused the Jewish community here in Hackney.

“We have increased patrols in the area and we are speaking to community leaders to provide further reassurance.”

Anyone with information about the incidents in Clapton Common that could assist police is asked to call 101, quoting reference 3400/19OCT26 or Crimestoppers, anonymously, on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget
News.content:
Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey has dismissed calls from some Labour MPs to increase Capital Gains Tax (CGT) when he hands down his first Budget.

Cabinet ministers Wes Streeting and Louise Haigh both previously voiced support for raising CGT before Andy Burnham became prime minister in July.

Ahead of next week's Budget, Healey ruled out lifting CGT - which is imposed on the profit people make when they sell an asset that has increased in value, such as shares in a company or properties which are not primary residences.

The move followed warnings that it could end up costing the government money if wealthy people leave the country or defer selling off assets, the Times newspaper reported.

The chancellor has previously indicated he wanted the UK to be a country of wealth creation, saying government policies should lift confidence, investment and profit.

Burnham has faced warnings against lifting CGT. His former adviser and Goldman Sachs Chief Economist Lord Jim O'Neill suggested it would send "the wrong message to business".

But, influential Labour figures had pushed for equalising CGT and income tax, with the former generally attracting a lower tax rate.

Louise Haigh, a key ally of the prime minister, had suggested capital gains should go up to be closer to income tax, before she became Burnham's first secretary of state.

Defence secretary Wes Streeting called for a "wealth tax that works" in May, shortly after resigning as a minister in former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer's government.

Healey already ruled out levelling the two tax rates, according to the Financial Times, external.

In a pre-Budget speech on Tuesday, Tory leader Kemi Badenoch is expected to urge the government to drop its spending plans and reduce its borrowing.

News.title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules
News.content:
Drivers will be given the right to challenge "rip off" private parking charges and more grace when using private providers under new rules set out by Andy Burnham.

The Prime Minister announced the changes after drivers repeatedly raised concerns penalties issued by private providers were too harsh and left motorists unfairly penalised.

In one case, a woman was taken to court in a Â£1,906 claim after taking longer than five minutes to pay at a car park in Derby. The charge was eventually dropped.

Private car parks already have an industry code of practice, but the RAC motoring group said the government's changes would protect drivers from the "poor practices of some private parking companies".

Burnham, the prime minister, said: "Being a few minutes late back to your car or typing one digit of your numberplate wrong shouldn't end with a hefty fine landing on your doormat.

"These charges leave people feeling ripped off and out of pocket, so I'm putting a stop to them."

The new rules will give drivers:

a guaranteed 5 minute period to decide whether to park

A 10 minute window to leave without facing a penalty

Cancellation of charges for issues drivers can't control, like vehicle breakdowns in car parks

Cancellation of charges for honest mistakes such as stopping to check directions, as well as for medical emergencies or broken ticket machines

Maximum charges of Â£20 on appeal for slip-ups like forgetting a parking permit, entering the wrong vehicle registration, or forgetting to confirm the registration in the machine when parking

A freeze on the maximum parking charge at Â£100, which is the same limit as the current private parking Code of Practice

Operators who do not comply risk losing access to DVLA data, making it far more difficult to pursue the car's owner even if they do issue a charge.

Private car parks are different to council-owned car parks and streets. RAC analysis of government data showed a record 17 million private parking tickets were issued in 2025/2026 - a 17% increase from a year earlier.

With each charge worth up to Â£100, the data, analysed by the Press Association and the RAC Foundation, suggests drivers could collectively face private parking charges worth more than Â£4.6m each day.

The yellow and black envelope of a Penalty Charge Notice, or PCN, is a dreaded sight for motorists returning to their car.

The AA has warned some drivers pay up even if they have done nothing wrong, just to avoid the hassle. It said people felt they would not get a fair hearing if they appealed fines, with many saying they feared legal action.

The current private parking industry Code of Practice, created by the British Parking Association and the International Parking Community, was introduced in 2024.

But the culture of motorists feeling they have been harshly penalised has spurred the government to present a formalised code to Parliament.

The British Parking Association told the BBC it welcomed the changes, but said "many of the principles within the new framework are already reflected in the existing voluntary Code of Practice".

The new Code will apply in England, Scotland and Wales after motorists said they wanted independent oversight of the private parking industry.

Jack Cousens, head of roads policy at the AA, said drivers "finally have something which could offer them better protections against the worst private parking operators". He said in the past they have "aggressively attacked drivers to the point where many simply pay up".

But the RAC's head of policy Simon Williams said it wasn't the leap his firm had been campaigning for. He called for the banning of debt recovery fees being added on top of PCNs and said the current industry-run appeals bodies should be replaced by a single independent one.

The government said it will be consulting on the issue of debt recovery fees, as well as other recommendation from the Competition and Markets Authority.

News.title: Woman says she 'closed eyes and tried not to be there' during alleged Russell Brand rape
News.content:
Warning - this report contains graphic content

A woman who alleges she was raped by Russell Brand at a bar told the police "I just closed my eyes and tried not to be there" while the attack was taking place.

In a 2023 video interview with an officer shown to the jury at his trial, the woman said she had been speaking to Brand about him hosting the Channel 4 show Big Brother's Big Mouth when he allegedly sexually assaulted her.

Brand, 51, has pleaded not guilty to all seven charges in the trial - three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one of indecent assault.

The allegations, made by six female complainants, span a 10-year period between 1999 and 2009.

The woman told the Southwark Crown Court jury the "lad culture" of the 2000s stopped her from reporting the TV star.

She has accused Brand of grabbing her breasts at the bar in Soho in London in 2004 before dragging her into a toilet and allegedly raping her.

The pair had been attending a birthday party when the alleged incidents happened.

She said she waited two decades to come forward to the police because the thought of doing so "terrified" her.

She said his celebrity status meant "it would be his word against mine".

"I would be ostracised in my work environment or friends."

The complainant worked for MTV at the time and said she was often surrounded by famous people.

From behind a blue screen in the witness box she said times had changed.

In those days - she said - "you weren't believed as a woman and it was a lad culture of 'you wearing this, so you were asking for it' and all that rubbish you were told back then".

The complainant recalled Brand's "big weird grin" which she compared to the face of a clown as he allegedly launched forward and grabbed hold of her.

Brand's barrister, Ian Winter KC, suggested during cross examination that Brand and the woman went to the toilet consensually for a "kiss and a cuddle", but they abandoned the attempt to have a sexual encounter because of the filthy state of the flooded toilet.

The woman, who became tearful while giving evidence, has rejected this version of events.

She said she felt "dazed" after the alleged attack.

Pressed on her claim of being dragged into the toilets against her will, the defendant's barrister suggested it would have been "perfectly easy" for her to have struggled or asked for help.

She said she did not agree because he had been holding her quite strongly, saying "part of me was saying just get it over with so you can get out of here".

She described feeling numb and ashamed afterwards.

She told the jury she had later confided in a friend, telling them Brand had "tried to do it" - but held back from saying he had "succeeded" in raping her.

The woman told the prosecution barrister that she didn't even know at the time that the alleged oral attack would be legally considered as rape.

Earlier on Monday, the jury was shown a 2023 video interview with an officer in which the woman said she had been speaking to Brand about him hosting the Channel 4 show Big Brother's Big Mouth when he allegedly sexually assaulted her.

In her recorded interview with police, the woman said "he literally just grabbed my boobs out of nowhere in the middle of the conversation, just in the middle of a conversation and I just remember this weird maniacal grin, looming in front of me as he just grabbed my boobs".

A short while later, she said he "dragged me in the toilets" where the floor was flooded, before "he unzipped himself" and allegedly orally raped her.

She said the alleged rape was "swift", and left her "in disbelief and shock".

"The toilets were behind where he stood. It was literally just grab and pull. He was holding me quite strongly on the arm and pulled me in that direction," she said.

"Part of me was saying just get it over with so you can get out of here".

"I just closed my eyes and tried not to be there. I just remember it felt like a force. I definitely said I don't want to do this," she added.

After the alleged rape, the woman, who was in her 20s at the time, said Brand "turned to me and said 'oh I guess we should swap numbers now', like it was just all normal, like he hadn't just forced me to do that."

Brand denies all the charges he faces.

He has said that any sexual contact if it happened, would have been consensual.

The trial continues and is expected to last for six weeks.

News.title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits
News.content:
Killers and serious sex offenders detained in hospital are among the criminals who will no longer receive benefits under proposals called for by victims' families.

Regulations due to be laid in Parliament on Tuesday seek to end the "double provision" and prevent serious criminals receiving up to Â£800 a month in universal credit over several years while already having their bed and board funded through the NHS while receiving psychiatric treatment.

The government said closing the loophole would save an estimated tens of millions of pounds annually.

The parents of Barnaby Webber and Grace O'Malley Kumar, who were killed by Valdo Calocane in Nottingham in 2023, welcomed the announcement.

The new regulations are expected to come into force early next year, subject to parliamentary approval.

News.title: US church on frontline of battle against drug known as 'tranq'
News.content:
America has been fighting the War on Drugs for decades, but the drug cartels, the suppliers and the dealers appear to be always one step ahead of the authorities.

President Trump has declared the cartels, "terrorists" and labelled fentanyl, the powerful synthetic opioid, a "weapon of mass destruction".

But the drug supply is changing, with other deadly synthetics being added to the mix, including strong animal tranquillisers, known on the streets as "tranq".

While overdose deaths are falling, the potency of the new drugs has recovery workers worried. For some the answer might lie in reducing demand, giving users support and helping them end their addiction.

BBC international correspondent Quentin Sommerville and camera journalist Darren Conway travelled to Columbus, Ohio to find out more.

Read more on this story: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis.

News.title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps
News.content:
Checking in at a dating event in a bar in Guildford, Olivia Miller-Davis is understandably apprehensive.

Even bringing a friend with her doesn't remove the awkwardness at the start of the night.

"It's always nerve-wracking when you're meeting new people," the 28-year-old admits before downloading an app that will match her to other daters based on their star signs.

This is speed dating 2026-style and Olivia, like many people we speak to, is here because she's fed up of "endlessly swiping" or as some describe it "app fatigue".

She says she hates judging people with "really limited information and just a couple of pictures" because she doesn't feel she can "really fully commit" with so little to go on.

According to a recent study from online regulator Ofcom 11% of adults use dating sites but it suggests the time we spend on them is dropping, from a peak of almost four hours a month in 2023, down to three hours last year.

News.title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about
News.content:
This report contains detailed descriptions of medical symptoms.

Monica Thomas was in her teens when she started experiencing intimate itching and soreness, but despite numerous trips to the doctors it was dismissed as thrush.

Her symptoms got worse, with sores and blisters leaving her in constant pain.

"I was bed bound for quite a long time because I couldn't walk," she says.

Monica says she was examined 28 times in six months before being offered a biopsy.

She says "we don't really talk about" gynaecological health as a society so there is a taboo around speaking about symptoms.

"Even when we go to the doctors, for me, the embarrassment of having to get undressed...with these doctors looking it is embarrassing," she says.

"But equally when you're in pain or it's itching and you've got discomfort, living with it is just as bad."

The 34-year-old from Suffolk was eventually diagnosed with a condition called lichen sclerosus.

News.title: Four arrested after police officer injured in shooting
News.content:
Four people have been arrested - including a woman on suspicion of causing grievous bodily harm and possessing a firearm - after a police officer was shot in Nottingham city centre.

Nottinghamshire Police said the officer had approached two suspects at a bus stop in Angel Row shortly before 04:50 BST on Sunday.

The male officer remains in hospital and is in a stable condition, the force added.

Two women, 27 and 25, and a 24-year-old man were arrested after police stopped a vehicle in the Radford area of Nottingham on Sunday evening, while a 30-year-old man was arrested in Bedfordshire in the early hours of Monday.

The 27-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of causing grievous bodily harm with intent, and possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life.

The 24-year-old man and 25-year-old woman were also arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender.

Separately, after stopping a vehicle in Bedfordshire, the 30-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender.

News.title: Troubles legacy bill is not an amnesty for soldiers - NI secretary
News.content:
The secretary of state for Northern Ireland has rejected claims that planned changes to the government's Troubles legacy bill amount to an "amnesty" for former soldiers.

Sir Chris Bryant said it was "completely wrong" to suggest a requirement for the attorney general to consent to serious Troubles-related prosecutions was designed to pardon veterans.

The proposal is among a series of government amendments being debated by MPs on Monday after the long-awaited legislation returned to the House of Commons.

Speaking to BBC News NI, Bryant said it was a "sensible measure" to ensure there was "more consistency" in how decisions are made.

The legislation seeks to deal with the unresolved legacy of the decades-long violent conflict in Northern Ireland, which cost the lives of more than 3,500 people.

It was first introduced to Parliament last year following agreement on a joint framework with the Irish government.

News.title: Man accused of mass train stabbing admits wounding
News.content:
A man accused of a mass stabbing on a train in Cambridgeshire last year has pleaded guilty to 12 counts of wounding with intent.

Passengers and staff were injured on the 18:25 Doncaster-London service on Saturday, 1 November after it left Peterborough, causing it to make an unscheduled stop at Huntingdon railway station.

Anthony Williams, 33, has denied 14 counts of attempted murder, relating to the train and to incidents in London and Peterborough, and is due to stand trial next week.

Appearing at a pre-trial review at Cambridge Crown Court, Williams, of Langford Road in Peterborough, pleaded guilty to the lesser wounding charges and several other offences.

He appeared via video link from Rampton Hospital in Nottinghamshire.

At an earlier hearing, Williams pleaded not guilty to attempting to murder Jonathan Gjoshe, Sachin Balakrishnan, David Presland, Scott Bletcher, Scott Green, Kevin Deely, Stephen Crean, Raza Aslam, Michael Paffett, and Samir Zitouni on the train near Huntingdon on 1 November.

In front of Mr Justice Calver this Monday, Williams pleaded guilty to 12 counts of wounding with intent and two of attempting to wound with intent in relation to incidents on the train, and earlier in Peterborough and London.

News.title: Man held after three Jewish women report assaults
News.content:
A man has been arrested after three Jewish women, one of whom was pushing a baby in a pram, reported being assaulted in north-east London.

Police were called to the Clapton Common area of Hackney at about 13:40 BST on Monday after a man had been detained by members of Shomrim, a Jewish neighbourhood watch group.

Officers arrested a 33-year-old man on suspicion of racially aggravated common assault. The women are believed to have suffered minor injuries.

The Metropolitan Police said it was treating the incident as a suspected antisemitic hate crime and had increased patrols in the area.

The man has since been further arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm in connection with a separate incident in Islington on Friday, the force said. He remains in custody.

Ch Insp Erica Crawshaw said it had been "an alarming and distressing incident" and thanked Shomrim volunteers for detaining a suspect before officers arrived.

"We recognise the concern that this incident will have caused the Jewish community here in Hackney," she said.

"We have increased patrols in the area and we are speaking to community leaders to provide further reassurance."

The Met has appealed for anyone with information, or anyone else who believes they may have been assaulted, to come forward.
