Guéhi was among the players who opted not to take a knee at the weekend as part of the Premier League’s “No Room For Racism” campaign. “I haven’t been taking the knee for a while now,” he said. “I’d always clap just because of what that actually signifies.” He wants greater action to combat racism in sport. “I hope we can do a bit more but we will just see. Hopefully the message is still getting out there, which is important.”

Sports.title: Konsa bullish about Arsenal’s Champions League hopes as Bayern clash looms
Sports.content:
For Ezri Konsa, it was just a wonderfully satisfying challenge. The Nottingham Forest striker Liam Delap had stolen in behind him up the inside left channel on Sunday. There were 93 minutes gone, Arsenal were 1-0 up and it was now or never for Forest. Konsa decreed that it would be never, curving his covering run back, matching Delap for pace and stretching into the perfect block tackle.

So, another win for Arsenal: their 10th in 11 matches this season. Another clean sheet. And for Konsa, a continuation of what has been a dreamlike couple of months. Do points-saving last-minute challenges mean more when the defender is actually a fan of the club, too? Basically, yes.

“I’ve been asked this a lot,” Konsa says with a smile, when the subject of his boyhood allegiance is raised. “And, yes, I was [an Arsenal supporter]. I had a lot of Arsenal kits when I was younger. You dream of playing for big clubs like this. When you’re a kid, you see the likes of Arsenal, growing up, and the amount of quality players they’ve had throughout the years and to be here – and not only to be here but to be here with close friends – makes it even more special.”

Konsa is talking about Eberechi Eze, in particular; another boyhood Arsenal fan, with whom he is especially tight. Many supporters have seen the clip of Eze greeting Konsa at the training ground after the latter had completed his £51m move from Aston Villa and how they crack up with laughter before embracing. It is infectious. But Konsa knows a clutch of other Arsenal players from England duty – Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka, Noni Madueke, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Ben White – and he credits them with helping him to settle in.

The 28-year-old’s adaptation has been quick and it has needed to be with William Saliba injured. After making his Arsenal debut as a substitute at Villa – Konsa’s scriptwriters have been hard at work – he has played in every minute of the club’s Premier League and Champions League matches. The victory at Forest, where Arsenal had drawn 0-0 in each of the previous two seasons, was significant. It was not a performance of any attacking pace or spark. Perhaps it made the points feel more precious.

“We hadn’t won here in two seasons, the boss was going on about it,” Konsa says. “It’s something we wanted to change as players and these are the games you have to win. If you want to win titles, you have to come away to tough places like this and get three points.”

View image in fullscreen Ezri Konsa does battle with Liam Delap during Arsenal’s 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Things are about to get even more interesting for Konsa and Arsenal because on Wednesday they face Bayern Munich at the Allianz Arena in the Champions League. “It’s against my international teammate as well,” Konsa says, and he is straight into an appreciation of Harry Kane, the England captain, who has been on fire since joining Bayern from Tottenham in 2023. Kane’s scoring record for the club bears repeating: 155 goals in 157 appearances.

Konsa has a good record against Kane, having faced him seven times, six of them for Villa against Spurs. The seventh and most recent came in October 2024 when Konsa was in the Villa team that beat Kane’s Bayern 1-0 at Villa Park in the Champions League. It was Villa’s first home match in the competition for 41 years. The defender has four wins against Kane’s teams and three losses. Kane has only scored twice against him, both from penalties.

“The Villa-Bayern game … to beat them at home and keep a clean sheet … it was very special for the players and the fans,” Konsa says. “I don’t really look much at those kind of stats [against individual players] but I am relishing the challenge.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The dynamics against Bayern appear different for Konsa this time. It was a famous victory for Villa that night, in part because of the tie’s history; the club beat Bayern 1-0 in the 1982 European Cup final. Villa were underdogs as they felt their way back into Europe’s elite competition. Arsenal will kick off as Bayern’s equals and among the favourites to win the tournament, having lost on penalties to Paris Saint-Germain in last season’s final.

Konsa won the first trophy of his career a week before that when he was in the Villa team that defeated Freiburg in the Europa League final. He says he has felt the determination of the Arsenal squad to go one step further in Europe.

“One hundred per cent,” Konsa says. “As players, the standards we have, the goals we have … we want to win everything – the Champions League, the Prem. Whatever trophies are in front of us. When I came to Arsenal, I wanted to win. I was hungry to win. Last season I got my hands on the Europa League and this season I want more.”

Sports.title: Arsenal and Liverpool backed to take advantage of Barcelona’s mad decision to sell best defender
Sports.content:
Arsenal and Liverpool backed to take advantage of Barcelona’s mad decision to sell best defender

France defender Jules Kounde has been tipped to move to the Premier League if Barcelona choose to cash in on him.

The LaLiga giants have been warned it would be a 'mad' decision to offload Kounde anytime soon, though.

5 Kounde has been with Barcelona since 2022 Credit: Getty

That is according to European football journalist Andy Brassell, who has named the two Premier League clubs the right-back could join.

Kounde has made 196 appearances for Barca since signing from Sevilla in 2022.

He has also won three LaLiga titles in four years, with another potentially on the cards this term.

Hansi Flick's side are already five points clear at the top of the table having won each of their opening nine matches.

Kounde has helped contribute with a goal and an assist in their last two victories.

However, Brassell believes Barca may chose to sell the 27-year-old sooner rather than later despite handing him a new five-year deal as recently as August last year.

Could Kounde leave Barcelona?

Speaking exclusively to talkSPORT.com, he explained: "I do get the feeling that Barcelona are going to sell Jules Kounde at some point in the near future, which I think is a bit mad.

"Obviously they're going to have to sell someone of value at some point in the medium term. It looks like they're limbering up for it to be him.

"He's an underrated right-back and a really underrated centre-back because he doesn't get to play there that often anymore."

Kounde has shown his versatility for club and country at both right-back and in central defence.

5 Barca have been warned selling Kounde would be a 'mad' decision Credit: Getty

As well as his title triumphs with Barcelona, the former Sevilla and Bordeaux man has won 58 caps for France.

He was part of the side which reached the 2022 World Cup final having won the Nations League the previous year.

Kounde made five starts during the tournament in Qatar, including the final defeat to Argentina.

Didier Deschamps later included him in his squad for both Euro 2024 and last summer's World Cup in North America.

Arsenal and Liverpool told to sign Kounde

As for which clubs Brassell believes Kounde could join, he continued: "I think he'd be brilliant for Arsenal, for example. I think he'd be really good there.

"You could argue that maybe that's the place that Arsenal don't need to spend £50-60million on a player because they've got so many accomplished defenders.

5 Kounde was handed a new five-year deal by Barca last summer Credit: AFP

"I think he'd be good for Liverpool as well because he can be an attacking full-back but he's an authentic defender as well."

Arsenal currently have just two senior right-backs in their squad in the form of Jurrien Timber and Ben White.

However, the latter is currently out of contract at the end of next season.

As for Liverpool, the Reds' centre-back options could see them move for Kounde next summer.

Both Virgil van Dijk and Joe Gomez's deal will expire at the end of the current campaign.

Their exits would leave Andoni Iraola with only three recognised centre-backs, provided Ronald Araujo's loan from Barca is made permanent.

5 Arsenal have an embarrassment of riches in defence but Arteta surely wouldn't say no to Kounde Credit: Getty

5 Van Dijk's potential departure from Liverpool in the summer leaves a hole in their defence Credit: Getty

Kounde's ability to play both centrally and at right-back would also provide a boost, with Araujo deputising in the role in recent weeks.

It comes amid Conor Bradley's injury lay-off, with a return not expected before December for the long-term absentee.

Sports.title: Furious Jamie O’Hara demands Tottenham sell £52m summer signing in expletive-laden rant
Sports.content:
Tottenham finally got their first Premier League win of the season against Coventry, but it wasn't a stress-free watch for Jamie O'Hara.

At the seventh time of asking, Spurs got themselves up and running with a 3-1 home victory against Frank Lampard's newly-promoted side.



5 Ben Davies was the unlikely man that sealed the points for Tottenham Credit: AFP

5 Omar Marmoush had set Spurs on their way as he restored their lead in the second half Credit: Getty

Roberto De Zerbi's side headed into Monday night's clash as the only team in England's top five divisions yet to win a league fixture this season.

But Spurs finally shed their unwanted tag on home turf with a first three points that moved them out of the Premier League's bottom three.



Coventry youth product James Maddison opened the scoring with a stunning curled effort after just 14 minutes - marking his first Tottenham start in 18 months with a goal.

Despite a dominant first-half, Spurs' lead was then wiped away on 49 minutes when Jack Rudoni's initial shot rebounded into his path and he found the net at the second attempt to equalise.



But De Zerbi's men restored their lead ten minutes later, as Omar Marmoush curled home to ease their nerves, before Ben Davies sealed the points with a stoppage-time effort.

Van Hecke leaves O'Hara fuming

While Tottenham megafan and former player O'Hara was delighted to see his club finally deliver the goods, he was left raging at Jan Paul van Hecke when his mistake helped Coventry find their equaliser.



The £52million defender gave the ball away further up the pitch in the build-up, before failing to recover to stop Rudoni from scoring.

With O'Hara taking part in a special live watchalong of the game alongside Jason Cundy on 'Sports Bar: The Lock In', he did not hold back in his assessment of Van Hecke's role in the goal.

In an X-rated outburst, he ex-Spurs midfielder exclaimed: "What the f*** is Van Hecke doing? He is s***. He is absolute toilet.

"It is toilet, it is so Spurs. What is [Antonin] Kinsky doing? Van Hecke, I'm sick of it, get him out of here. We sold (Luka) Vuskovic for that pile of c***."



5 Van Hecke endured a hairy moment as Spurs were briefly pegged back by Coventry Credit: AFP

5 Rudoni equalised for Coventry minutes into the second half Credit: Getty

With Chelsea man Cundy earning a reputation for winding up O'Hara over Spurs' struggles, he made sure to deliver while his co-host raged.

Repeating his favourite catch phrase in recent months, Cundy gleefully taunted him: "You're going down!"



"F*** off," came the response from a furious O'Hara.

Despite a much-needed three points for Spurs, the talkSPORT host wasn't done with slating Van Hecke after the match either.

O'Hara continued to question why promising young defender Luka Vuskovic was allowed to be sold to Brighton, while Van Hecke moved in the opposite direction.

He said on the Sports Bar: "He's running through treacle, people say he's good on the ball but he is a problem for us.

5 Jan Paul van Hecke was one the first of Spurs' big-money arrivals this summer when he joined in a £52m deal Credit: Getty



"Brighton got Vuskovic out of the deal, they've got a better player."

Thankfully for O'Hara, Van Hecke's moment to forget was unable to prevent Spurs from getting their all-important win.

This isn't the first time the Dutcham has come in for criticism since reuniting with former Brighton boss De Zerbi in north London this summer.

In Spurs' 3-2 defeat to Aston Villa in September, Stuart Pearce questioned his £52m price tag after he struggled against Nicolas Jackson.

The England great said of Van Hecke on air: "Was that £52million worth of central defending?"



While Van Hecke's struggles came under scrutiny again against Coventry, O'Hara and Spurs fans up and down the country will simply be relieved to see their team get their first three points.

The victory lifts them out of the Premier League relegation zone and into 16th place, with six points from their first seven games.

Sports.title: UEFA piles pressure on FIFA demanding more from Gianni Infantino in damning letter
Sports.content:
UEFA piles pressure on FIFA demanding more from Gianni Infantino in damning letter

UEFA has sent FIFA a letter demanding answers to 42 questions surrounding Gianni Infantino's presidency, including his relationship with Donald Trump.

The letter, seen by talkSPORT, is addressed to General Secretary Mattias Grafstrom, and seeks answers by November 2.

3 Gianni Infantino has faced mounting scrutiny over his presidency in recent months Credit: Getty

It follows FIFA President Infantino telling FIFA Council members in a meeting in Zurich last Thursday to put their questions in writing.

UEFA is seeking further clarity on a number of concerns raised in the meeting, including Infantino's relationship with US President Donald Trump.

The letter also questions how Folarin Balogun’s red card came to be suspended at the World Cup, which allowed him to play against Belgium despite being sent off in the round before against Bosnia-Herzegovina.

UEFA want details as to how the FIFA Peace Prize was founded, and given to Trump at the 2026 World Cup draw in Washington DC.

Among their other grievances, European football's governing body ask for more transparency FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), the failed plan to part-privatise FIFA.

UEFA's letter to FIFA

“We formally request a substantive written response to each question, together with all supporting documentation by Monday, November 2,” the UEFA letter reads.

“Any refusal to disclose information or documents should be justified individually, with a clear explanation of the specific grounds relied upon.

“These questions require answers now. They cannot be deferred until the next meeting of the FIFA Council — nor can future governance reforms substitute for scrutiny of decisions already taken and accountability for them.”

Senior UEFA executives are still spearheading a move to find a candidate to run against Infantino at the next election.

The deadline to put forward a name is November 18.

3 Aleksander Ceferin heads up UEFA, who have long questioned Infantino's suitability for his role as FIFA president Credit: Getty

Infantino has vowed to fight on, but there remain several unanswered questions despite the FIFA President apologising for FFE in Zurich last week.

UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin and his CONCACAF counterpart Victor Montagliani have both called for Infantino to resign, as has UEFA vice-president Laura McAllister and English FA chair Debbie Hewitt.

Among the major issues over which UEFA are seeking answers are the origins of FFE, where Infantino planned to sell off stakes in the world football governing body's competitions to private investors

FIFA are asked by UEFA, "When was the idea of FFE first explored, by whom and with what objective?"

FIFA are also tasked with explaining why Josh Kushner's Thrive Capital were granted exclusivity as an investor without consultation. Kusher is the younger brother of Jared Kushner, the son-in-law of U.S. president Donald Trump.

UEFA also ask whether Infantino had a financial interest in FFE.

3 infantino's decisions throughout the summer have put him under serious pressure to keep his job Credit: AFP

The letter goes on to demand further information on "a series of decisions, transactions and interventions involving the FIFA President, the President of the United States [Trump] and individuals associated with him".

These are outlined in detail as follows:

UEFA's question on Infantino-Trump dealings " • The FIFA Peace Prize, which was not submitted to the FIFA Council for approval; - The reported seven-year, approximately USD 4 million lease of office premises in Trump Tower, New York, involving Eric Trump, for premises reportedly unused for much of the year; - The proposed agreement with Thrive Capital, led by Mr Joshua Kushner, a member of the US President’s family; - The US President’s telephone call to the FIFA President requesting intervention in the Balogun disciplinary case; - Reported advanced discussions involving the US President and individuals associated with him concerning a FIFA cryptocurrency; - The World Cup sponsorship arrangement with Kalshi, a company reportedly advised and partly owned by Donald Trump Jr., including reports that Kalshi received extensive advertising exposure without providing financial consideration to FIFA; - The last-minute relocation of the World Cup draw, reportedly at significant additional cost to FIFA, to the JFK/Donald Trump Center in Washington, D.C., instead of Las Vegas; - The involvement of the US President’s daughter and grandson in the Club World Cup draw; - The announcement of a USD 75 million investment in Palestine during the US President’s Board of Peace meeting, apparently without prior information being provided to, or approval sought from, the FIFA Finance Committee or Council; - Public statements by White House representatives, including Andrew Giuliani and the US President himself, defending the FIFA President, supporting his continued presidency and criticising those questioning his leadership."

UEFA want all documents relating to Balogun's red card against Bosnia in the World Cup round of 32 to be shared.

The US striker saw his automatic one-game ban suspended following a call from President Trump to Infantino to review the matter, as talkSPORT exclusively revealed.

Infantino has always claimed he had no involvement in the decision to suspend Balogun’s red stressing FIFA's disciplinary committee, which is independent, took the call.

The lack of clarity as to why the decision was made has led Infantino’s critics to question whether Infantino directly influenced the decision despite his denial.

And there are questions about Infantino's use of a private jet, and the hosting of celebrities at World Cup final, and whether any FIFA costs were incurred in doing so.

Sports.title: Ex-Premier League star opens up on unemployment struggle as he targets manager role
Sports.content:
Ex-Premier League star opens up on unemployment struggle as he targets manager role

Steven Caulker has provided an update on his search for coaching opportunities following a viral social media post.

The former defender took to LinkedIn on Sunday to share details of a 'stressful' spell away from football.



3 Caulker's phone has 'not stopped ringing' since his viral LinkedIn post Credit: Getty

Caulker has been without a job since leaving his role as assistant manager at Turkish side Konyaspor last month.

The 34-year-old spent eight months with the club, joining their coaching staff in February.

It followed his decision to retire from football in November 2025 after a spell in Iceland with Stjarnan.



Caulker had juggled playing with a role as assistant manager during his time at the Scandinavian club.

Meanwhile, he was previously a player-coach for Spanish outfit Malaga Juniors back in 2024.



Since leaving Turkey, though, Caulker has been unable to secure a role in England despite his experience and coaching badges.

The former Sierra Leone international joined Hawksbee and Jacobs on Monday to provide an update on his employment search.



Asked about the response to his LinkedIn post, he revealed: "Do you know what? I wrote that post yesterday morning and I think my phone has not stopped ringing."

Caulker continued: "It’s a good thing. I’m just in a situation where I wanted to leave Turkey.

"I wanted to come back and look to develop my coaching in the UK or maybe Europe, but I felt that it was time to come back closer to home.

3 Caulker made 123 Premier League appearances as a player Credit: Getty



"I spent a long time on the road and I’ve come back and I’ve been applying for jobs, I’m doing all the networking. It’s just a case of waiting for the right opportunity to appear.

"The difficult thing when you’re in a situation like this, or what I’m finding difficult, is to then say no to jobs that don’t align with my vision.

"Ultimately, I want to be a Premier League manager and I know that I’ve got a lot of work to get there, but I want to make sure that I’m on the right path, learning from the right people and making the right decisions along the way."

Caulker made 123 Premier League appearances as a player for Cardiff City, QPR, Swansea City, Tottenham Hotspur, Liverpool and Southampton.



He also represented Wigan Athletic in the EFL and had a brief spell in Scotland with Dundee.

As well as winning 18 caps for Sierra Leone, the centre-back was capped once by England in 2012.

3 Caulker has coached in Spain, Iceland and Turkey already in his career Credit: Getty

It followed his inclusion in the Team GB squad at the London Olympics earlier that year.



Alongside his coaching career, Caulker founded his own wellbeing consultancy firm last November following his retirement.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford’s lack of form has created dressing room headache for Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford doesn't seem to have the trust of Michael Carrick and his current form is causing an issue for the under-pressure Manchester United boss.

That's the view of talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook, who has shared his thoughts on the forward after he was an unused substitute in United's 1-1 draw with Leeds.

4 Rashford's goalless start to the season saw him left on the bench against Leeds Credit: Getty

The Red Devils' worst ever start to a Premier League season continued on Sunday, as their winless run extended to six games.

It piles the pressure on boss Carrick, whose side have won just once in the league - a 5-2 victory against Ipswich in their second game - and sit just two points above the bottom three in 13th.

As for Rashford, he has struggled to have a positive impact since returning to Old Trafford following his loan spell at Barcelona.

Rashford has been struggling with a hip injury suffered during the World Cup, meaning he needs regular treatment to ensure he is available for selection.

The England forward is yet to register a goal contribution this term, having made eight appearances across all competitions.

That's despite starting on six occasions, and he wasn't called upon at the weekend as United went in search of a winner at Elland Road.

Rashford return questioned

With Rashford having little influence as United continue to struggle, United fan Crook has claimed his return is only proving a hindrance.

An academy graduate, Rashford quickly established himself as one of England's brightest young talents after bursting onto the scene as an 18-year-old.

He remained a key player for United in the years that followed, and signed a five-year deal worth in excess of £325,000-per-week in 2023 after a 30-goal season, which he remains under contract now.

However, after two loan spells away at Aston Villa and Barcelona, Crook told talkSPORT Breakfast: "I think he's probably peaked.

4 Rashford has scored 138 goals for United, but wasn't called upon against Leeds Credit: AFP

4 The 28-year-old has failed to pick up where he left off last season at Barcelona Credit: Getty

"That season, when he scored so many goals under Erik ten Hag [30 in 2022/23 term], that convinced them to give him this huge, big-money contract, which has been a real problem, I think, for the football club.

"And since he came back in, I was hoping that maybe his spell away at Barcelona would have sparked a new lease of life out of Marcus Rashford, but we haven't seen it, in all honesty.

"And I think Michael Carrick was absolutely right to put him on the bench yesterday, and the fact he didn't bring him on at the end of the game when United are short of goals and chasing a winner probably tells you he doesn't trust him at this moment in time."

United finished an impressive third in the Premier League last season, with Bryan Mbeumo, Benjamin Sesko and Matheus Cunha all hitting double figures in league goals.

Rashford's return was expected to boost their attacking threat having registered 14 goals and 15 assists on loan at Barcelona in 2025/26.

However, with United's forward line struggling to deliver the goods this term, Crook believes Rashford's return has upset the squad -particularly Cunha, who has scored just once so far.

4 Matheus Cunha hit 10 Premier League goals in his debut season for United last term Credit: Getty

He continued: "I think his return has been a problem, I think there's probably some unhappy players in that dressing room that he's earning so much money.

"I think it's been an issue for Matheus Cunha, because it's his place that he took and you can see that Cunha is sulking a little bit.

"And there was such a good balance at the top end of the pitch last season with Cunha and Mbeumo and Bruno Fernandes, Amad Diallo, Sesko when he was fit.

"But Marcus Rashford, I think, not on a personal level, but just because those players feel aggrieved, I think he's upset the balance of the attack and isn't putting the numbers on the board at the moment to justify that huge salary."

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo gets meaningless ban and receives miniscule fine for Portugal walkout
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has been given a 30-day suspension after leaving his country's international camp last month.

The 41-year-old stormed out of the national team camp following a dispute over playing time with head coach Jorge Jesus.



4 Ronaldo will be unavailable for Portugal for a 30-day period Credit: Getty

Ronaldo was angered after being left on the bench for the entire match during Portugal's 2-1 Nations League win over Norway.

He later issued a lengthy statement apologising to his teammates but conceding that his actions deserved punishment, and was then provisionally suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation.

And the Al Nassr forward has now learned his fate, with reporter Fabrizio Romano confirming the country's FA have now suspended him for 30 days, and handed out a €255 (£214) fine.



The ban is effective from the date he left Portugal's camp - September 30.

This means he has already served 19 days of the 30-day suspension and will be available for the upcoming November international break.



Portugal face Denmark on November 14 in the Nations League, before returning to action three days later against Wales.

Portugal statement on Ronaldo

Ronaldo's punishment was announced in a statement by the Portuguese Federation's Disciplinary Council.



A statement read: “In these terms and with the grounds set forth, the Disciplinary Council – Non-Professional Section – of the Portuguese Football Federation decides, in these proceedings, to find the accusation fully justified.

“Consequently, to condemn the Defendant Cristiano Ronaldo dos Santos Aveiro for the commission, on one occasion and intentionally, of the disciplinary infraction foreseen and sanctioned by paragraph 1 of article 160 of the RDFPF.

“Applying to him, consequently, the sanction of suspension for 30 (thirty) days and, additionally, the sanction of a fine which is set at 2.5 UC, that is, €255.00 (two hundred and fifty-five euros).”

4 Against Norway in September, Ronaldo was an unused substitute for the first time in 18 years Credit: Getty



4 Jorge Jesus was previously Ronaldo's manager at Al Nassr, but the pair clashed recently on Portugal duty Credit: Getty

It's fair to say Ronaldo's miniscule fine isn't likely to hit him too hard.

The Man United and Real Madrid great earns an estimated £225.5million-per-year with his wages and commercial deals.

This means it will take him just 30 seconds to earn back the £215 he owes Portugal in fine money.



Ronaldo's Portugal saga

The incident which led to Ronaldo's suspension happened on September 30, the day before Portugal were due to play Denmark.

He clashed with manager Jesus after the player felt he was misled over his expected playing time in the autumn international break.

Ronaldo and Jesus agreed that he would play in the first and last of their four matches but on the morning of the second match against Norway, the latter said he would play him for 30 minutes.

4 Cristiano Ronaldo is enduring a rough patch in his storied international career Credit: Getty



In a statement, the Portugal captain also claimed his manager had told him to warm up against Norway, only to leave him on the bench.

Ronaldo wrote: "I warmed up from half-time, watched the minutes go by, and was not called. The coach had broken his word to me."

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner apologised for his actions though, adding: “I also owe an apology to my national team teammates for having left the camp.

"Despite the absolute breach of trust in the coach’s word, as those who witnessed these conversations can attest, I should not have done it."



It remains to be seen if Jesus will recall Ronaldo for Portugal's November internationals, where the forward will be looking to make headway in his bid to reach 1,000 career goals.

Of his current 981 tally, he has scored 146 goals in 234 appearances for his country, making him both the all-time top goalscorer and the most capped player in men's international football history.

Sports.title: ‘Dangerous’ – Police launch investigation after rugby ball booted into Premier League stadium during match
Sports.content:
Brentford has confirmed they are working with the police after footage of a rugby ball being kicked into their stadium went viral.

The Bees were beaten 2-1 by Liverpool at the Gtech Community Stadium on Saturday, with a video taken during the game since circulating online.



3 A ball was kicked onto the Gtech pitch from a high-rise flat during Brentford's defeat to Liverpool Credit: Getty

A clip appears to show an individual kicking a rugby ball from a high-rise flat into the ground while the match was unfolding.

The ball initially seemed to hit the roof of the Gtech’s East Stand, but footage later emerged of a coach inside the ground removing it from inside the ground.

This suggests it had bounced down to the pitch, and Brentford has since commented after the video went viral following the defeat.



Bees condemn 'dangerous' incident

In a statement, Brentford condemned the recent footage, calling the individual's actions 'dangerous and potentially very harmful'.

The Bees also revealed that they are now working with the police to identify those involved in the incident.



The club wrote: "Brentford Football Club is aware of an incident involving an item being kicked from a height towards the field of play during Saturday’s match against Liverpool.

"Such behaviour is dangerous and potentially very harmful.

"The matter has been referred to the police and the club is supporting the relevant authorities in their investigation to help identify those responsible and take appropriate action, which may result in criminal prosecution.



"The matchday safety of fans, staff, players and officials is of utmost importance, and the club will support all efforts to ensure action is taken."

The Gtech Community Stadium has hosted Brentford since 2020, after they moved across town from former home Griffin Park.

3 Alexander Isak was the difference on the pitch against Brentford on Saturday Credit: Getty

With a capacity of 17,250, the west London ground is the second-smallest in size in the Premier League, only ahead of Bournemouth's Vitality Stadium.



It is part of a wider development project in the local area, and is surrounded by blocks of flats and other commercial buildings, where the footage of the rugby ball incident appears to take place.

What happened in Brentford vs Liverpool?

Brentford are also left picking up the pieces from their display on the pitch on Saturday, after Liverpool came from behind to beat them.

Keane Lewis-Potter put the Bees in front on the stroke of half-time, before further drama unfolded.

Yehor Yarmolyuk was shown a red card in first-half stoppage time for violent conduct, after a VAR review showed him to caught Jeremy Jacquet with a 'headbutting action'.



This proved a turning point in the game, with summer signing Victor Munoz grabbing the equaliser before Alexander Isak struck on 70 minutes to seal three points for the Reds.

3 Keith Andrews' Brentford are sixth in the Premier League after defeat to Liverpool in an eventful afternoon Credit: Getty

Brentford then saw out the final minutes with nine men, as Vitaly Janelt was shown a second yellow card for bringing down Rio Ngumoha on the edge of the Brentford penalty area.

The result saw the Bees fall to their first defeat of the season, while Liverpool moved above them into fifth in the table with victory.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace hit with unusual kick-off time double-whammy as Manchester United and Arsenal games rearranged
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace hit with unusual kick-off time double-whammy as Manchester United and Arsenal games rearranged

Add us as preferred source

The Premier League has announced the fixture amendments for the first three weeks of December.

Clubs have now learned the dates and kick-off times for their matches throughout the month and into January.



3 Palace have seen multiple matches rearranged by the Premier League Credit: Getty

It follows the confirmation of UK TV broadcast selections between December 26 and January 7.

Matches have also been moved in line with existing fixtures in European competitions.

Fixture dates and kick-off times for the remainder of January are set to be announced the week commencing November 30.



Palace matches rescheduled

The latest selections see Crystal Palace facing a pair of unusual kick-off times for their home matches against Manchester United and Arsenal.

Both fixtures will kick-off at 7pm on a Sunday night in a rarely-seen decision.



Palace's clash with United will now be played on Sunday, December 13.

The move comes after the fixture was selected for live coverage by TNT Sports.

However, it could not be played in the broadcaster's usual 12:30pm Saturday slot due to Palace's Europa League commitments.



Pierre Sage's side face Polish outfit Jagiellonia Bialystok away from home on Thursday, December 10.

Meanwhile, Sky Sports has chosen to broadcast Arsenal's trip to Selhurst Park.

3 Palace will host United at 7pm on Sunday, December 13 Credit: Getty

As a result, the match has been moved from Boxing Day to Sunday, December 27.



Palace's matches against Chelsea, Sunderland and Bournemouth in December will also be broadcast live on UK TV.

The trip to face the Black Cats has been rescheduled to 2pm on Sunday, December 20 due to being chosen for Sky Sports coverage.

Their return fixture against Chelsea in January will also be covered by the broadcaster.

Premier League fixture amendments

Elsewhere, Brighton and Bournemouth have also seen fixtures moved to the Sunday 2pm slot due to their European schedules.



The two clubs are competing in the Conference League and Europa League, respectively, this season.

3 Arsenal's trip to Selhurst Park has also been moved to a Sunday night Credit: Getty

Crystal Palace's Festive Fixtures Matches between December 1 and January 7 Chelsea vs Crystal Palace - 7:30pm on Wednesday, December 2 (Live on Sky Sports) Aston Villa vs Crystal Palace - 3pm on Saturday, December 5 Crystal Palace vs Manchester United - 7pm on Sunday, December 13 (Live on TNT Sports) Sunderland vs Crystal Palace - 2pm on Sunday, December 20 (Live on Sky Sports) Crystal Palace vs Arsenal - 7pm on Sunday, December 27 (Live on Sky Sports) Crystal Palace vs Bournemouth - 7.30pm on Wednesday, December 30 (Live on Sky Sports) Brentford vs Crystal Palace - 3pm on Saturday, December 2 Crystal Palace vs Chelsea - 7:30pm on Wednesday, December 6 (Live on Sky Sports)

Meanwhile, Everton are now set to host Fulham on Sunday, December 6 due to the Cottagers facing Tottenham Hotspur on Thursday, December 3.

Other notable changes include the north London derby at 4:30pm on Sunday, December 6 and Manchester City vs Chelsea on Saturday, December 12 at 5:30pm.



The Blues have provisionally had their home clash with Aston Villa rescheduled to Monday, December 21 on Sky Sports.

However, the match could instead take place at 8pm on Saturday, December 19 depending on whether either club remains in the Carabao Cup.

Sports.title: 'Reckless on a catastrophic level': Medical expert's damning verdict on the Eagles' decision to play Jalen Hurts with a blood clot that could have killed him… now their NFL reputation and his career lie in tatters as 'fall guy' hunt begins
Sports.content:
Jalen Hurts was at risk of dying in the days before multiple blood clots were found in his lungs, an expert claims, as the Philadelphia Eagles face growing questions over their handling of the star quarterback's health.

Hurts is set to miss the rest of the NFL season after doctors made the terrifying discovery on Wednesday - three days after he played against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London before flying home to Philadelphia and 10 days after a cleat to the calf against the Los Angeles Rams that sparked the problem.

An ultrasound initially found a blood clot after the team arrived in London to face the Jaguars, with Hurts placed on the injury report with a calf injury on Friday. According to reports, Hurts barely slept the night before the game after being evaluated in a London hospital. But the quarterback was nevertheless allowed to take the field.

Now, sports medicine specialist Dr. Jesse Morse - who has not personally treated Hurts - has told the Daily Mail that the 'fact they let him play in the game is the craziest decision that I can fathom,' as he outlined the terrifying risks he faced then and in the days that followed.

The Daily Mail has contacted Hurts' representatives and the Philadelphia Eagles for comment.

Morse claimed that even Hurts' tiredness put him in danger, noting that lack of sleep 'significantly reduces reaction time', and in an NFL game 'you're at very high risk for suffering concussion or possible injury if your reaction times are slow.'

Jalen Hurts is set to miss the rest of the NFL season due to multiple blood clots in his lungs

The Eagles have faced questions over the handling of Hurts' situation after his diagnosis

ESPN initially reported that Hurts was up all night before the Jaguars game, due to the risk that the clot could move. But the quarterback's agent, Nicole Lynn, has since claimed that he was able to sleep after rejoining the team. Lynn said the Eagles set aside a room for him at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

After returning to the United States following Philadelphia's loss to the Jaguars, Hurts said he had faced a 'very unique' situation when he practiced. It was not until Wednesday, October 14 that the Eagles said a follow-up ultrasound revealed the clot had moved. The Eagles have not responded to comment to confirm whether or not he had any more ultrasounds between the Jaguars game and that finding.

The fact he played the game in London indicates he had not started taking blood thinning medication before the game, as that would have prevented him from being able to take to the field due to extremely high risks from being hit.

Morse said: 'Rather than being smart and putting him on the blood thinner to prevent that blood clot from moving, they decided to say, you know what, we're just going to let him play.

'The crazy part, after that, is them saying, you know what? He just played a stressful game, which is very stressful in the body and increases the risk for further clotting, but not only that, could have caused it to move. Then they decided to send him back internationally from London to Philly.

'So he was at risk of having a blood clot, going through his lungs, his brain or his heart and potentially killing him, from the date of that diagnosis. So probably from last Friday, through the game, through the international flight, and then each of the days afterwards until he was put on a blood thinner.'

Morse believes allowing Hurts to play in the game and subsequent details of his treatment could amount to a 'fireable offense' and told the Daily Mail: 'There has to be a fall guy, probably, multiple fall guys. But this is reckless on a catastrophic level.

'Whether this is the coach, the GM, the doctor, the medical team... somebody, several people have to be the fall guy, because this isn't just a random, one off, small player, that like, "we could just sit him, it's not a big deal."

'This is the quarterback of the team. This is the leader. So everybody is in the know about what's going on with this situation. This is not, you know, we're going to keep this hush hush.

'Everyone was in on this decision, but this is on the medical staff to say, "hey, I am not medically clearing you to play in that game. I don't care if you want to play in that game. I know you're going to want to play."

'Players want to play. But it is my medical judgment that is not worth the risk. For you to play in that game and potentially this blood clot from the blood vessel, go into your lungs, cause a saddle embolus and die.'

Hurts threw for over 200 yards against the Jaguars in London in a narrow 19-17 loss

Hurts later told reporters he had faced a 'very unique' situation before the Jaguars game

Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni insisted Monday he has 'full trust and full faith' in the team's medical staff and added: 'We always put our players health first and foremost in every situation.'

Attention is now turning to whether Hurts will be able to return at all, with concerns the situation could end his career. He will need to be cleared after months on blood thinners, which Morse says is far from guaranteed now he faces increased risk of blood clots after a 'unique' sequence of events.

'It could be (career-ending),' Morse said. 'At the minimum, this is three months. And we've had several players suffer blood costs and come back. But to my knowledge, and I studied this stuff really well, I don't think we've ever had an NFL player get confirmed multiple blood clots in his lungs. Which means this is not the first time, and this was not only one.

'The only way you could potentially prevent a new blood clot from forming is to be on a blood thinner. You cannot be on a blood thinner and a play contact sport. You will bleed out and you can't stop the hose when the faucet is turned on, which is what a blood thinner does. You can't turn it off until like 34 days later. So it's not worth the risk.

'Unless they decide to make this a unique exception to the rule, this could be career ending. At the minimum it is season ending, but this is a very unique situation.

'Just the fact that this was a trauma-induced clot. That was probably worsened by the international flight each way. Diagnosed, acknowledged that it existed, recommended not to sleep, because if he slept, the immobility could potentially cause the blood clot to move into his lungs, yet you allowed him to play in an NFL game? And then flew him back on a flight for 6 to 7 hours? I don't know how they could medically clear him, safely.'

Morse also points to increased risk, albeit a rare one, of suffering blood clots after getting a COVID-19 vaccine. In 2021, it was found that around 4 in one million people who got the Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine later got a blood clot syndrome. The vaccine is no longer available in the United States and medical experts say the benefits of getting a COVID-19 vaccine generally outweigh the risks.

Hurts is set to remain with the team while he is ruled out of football due to his health condition

Hurts initially suffered the injury when he took a cleat to the calf against the Los Angeles Rams

'They're calling this provoked versus unprovoked, is usually the term we use. So this would be a provoked blood clot, meaning it was a trauma which led to it.

'The trauma that caused it could potentially cause a new one. So if this was an unprovoked blood clot, meaning he just developed blood cloth out of the blue, he wasn't doing anything, he didn't get hit, then that is permanent career-ending. No questions.

'That's what happened to Chris Bosh for the for the Miami Heat. But at the same time, knowing the sport that he plays, how can you justify the risk?'

Sports.title: Graeme Souness labels Bukayo Saka a CHEAT: Liverpool legend claims Arsenal star 'dives all over the place' - leaving Piers Morgan in shock
Sports.content:
Graeme Souness has accused Bukayo Saka of being a 'cheat' who 'dives all over the place'. And the Liverpool legend believes Arsenal have a strategy of ganging up on referees to convince them that a 'screaming' Saka has been fouled. It is an accusation commonly levelled at the England man, 25, who is often among the most-fouled players in a given Premier League season. Fans may remember the controversy that erupted in the Champions League quarter-finals in 2024 when he tried to buy a last-minute penalty against Manuel Neuer in a tie which Arsenal eventually lost. And Souness dug into the winger on Piers Morgan's Football Uncensored show, leaving his host outraged. 'Your man Saka dives all over the place. I don't want to hear about him. The minute he looks like losing possession, he's down,' he said. Graeme Souness has accused Bukayo Saka of being a 'cheat' who 'dives all over the place' Fans may remember his 'dive' against Bayern Munich in the Champions League in 2024 Souness says that Saka 'screams' when he goes down and that Arsenal's players work to convince the referee 'He simulates a foul. Anyone who simulates a foul in my book would be a cheat. 'He dives when he should be staying on his feet. He's not alone. So Saka gets tackled, he screams as he's going down. 'The referee thinks there's nothing in that but wait a minute, he's stayed down. And then worse than that, everyone in the immediate area - all Arsenal players - put their hands up and scream foul. 'The referee at that point panics and blows his whistle when it wasn't a foul - his first instinct was the right one. 'But he blows a foul because he's thinking, wait a minute, something I'm not understanding here. 'Simulation is a form of cheating, yes. But it's all over football today. 'If you asked 100 people what is it you dislike about the modern game, 50 per cent would say simulation, another 50 per cent would say VAR.' With the game moving at such speed, it is difficult to always know exactly how hard a player has felt contact, or how a tiny amount of contact may genuinely throw them off. Piers Morgan was unhappy with Souness' suggestion, saying: 'I wouldn't call him a cheat Saka's notoriety for diving has lasted for years, but he is far from the only player to have that criticism levelled at him. The incident with Bayern in 2024 attracted a lot of attention and debate. It initially looked as if the goalkeeper had brought him down, and the winger had got to the ball first. However, replays showed Saka moving his leg in Neuer's direction to collide with him to try and buy a penalty - a move which backfired. Some pundits came down on him with disapproval, with Paola Di Canio telling Sky Sports Italia: 'He moves blatantly the leg towards Neuer, it’s never a penalty. 'He didn’t behave as an experienced player. He behaved like a baby with no experience.' But Rio Ferdinand took Saka's side, saying: 'I can’t believe that’s not been given! That is a penalty, I’m in disbelief.'

Sports.title: Zlatan Ibrahimovic's acrobatic brilliance against England, Jamie Vardy's volley and a belter at Blackpool... after Diego Gomez's halfway-line stunner for Brighton, our experts pick their favourite goal
Sports.content:
Zlatan Ibrahimovic's acrobatic brilliance against England, Jamie Vardy's volley and a belter at Blackpool... after Diego Gomez's halfway-line stunner for Brighton, our experts pick their favourite goal

Diego Gomez's incredible strike from the halfway line was the highlight of Brighton's 5-0 demolition of Crystal Palace on Sunday - and a contender for goal of the season.

On the back of that, we asked our experts for their favourite goal they have ever witnessed live...

MATT BARLOW: Zlatan Ibrahimovic (Sweden 4-2 England, 2012)

Zlatan's overhead kick from about 35 yards for Sweden against England. Simply the most Zlatan moment you could imagine. The opening of a new stadium in Stockholm came with a general feeling of underappreciation in the media for Zlatan's enduring qualities. Me included to be honest.

He had rarely turned it on against English opposition in the Champions League, but this was the night he scored four in a 4-2 win as the England choir serenaded him with a song comparing him unfavourably to Andy Carroll.

His fourth was an outrageous acrobatic finish not only from distance but also off centre, wide on the right with Joe Hart marooned out of his goal. Off came the shirt.

Asked by a gaggle of English reporters to rate his own career out of 10 after the game, Zlatan thought carefully for a moment or two and said, "10". Nobody argued. Still makes me smile.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic's amazing strike towards the end of the match sealed Sweden's 4-2 win

JACK GAUGHAN: Phil Clarkson (Blackpool 2-1 Northampton, 1998)

A header has popped up in the direction of Clarkson. Six yards out, back to goal and with a defender touch tight. A goal down, Blackpool’s No 8 takes the knock down with the instep of his right foot, passing over to his left and then uses his left to impishly volley a backheel with proper force into the corner.

Remarkably he watches the ball all the way and follows it into the net, pirouetting and almost breaking into an Eric Cantona celebration.

It’s Division Two (League One these days) - a moment of genius so far removed from its surroundings that it sticks in your mind for decades to come. Sat on a wall level with that penalty area, there was a seven-year-old going crazy who’d had a perfect view of the magic unfolding.

Hopefully in his second career, Clarkson delivers the post to the people of the Fylde Coast with the same panache.

JAMES SHARPE: Jamie Vardy (West Brom 1-4 Leicester, 2018)

As someone who has watched - and cheered - many a Jamie Vardy goal for Leicester over the years, you might think my pick of the bunch would be his glorious 30-yard volley against Liverpool in the title-winning season. Or the one to break Ruud van Nistelrooy’s record by scoring in 11 consecutive games. Or…never mind.

Belters, of course, but not the best nor my favourite. That one is saved for his ridiculous over-the-shoulder volley against West Brom in 2018, a strike that would be crowned Carling goal of the month and Leicester’s goal of the season.

Riyad Mahrez’s floating ball over the top, dropping over Vardy’s shoulder as he runs in behind and never breaks stride as he hooks it first-time - with his weaker left foot - straight into the bottom corner. I make a noise every time I watch it back. He makes it look ridiculously easy.

All from a man who Michael Owen once described as ‘not a natural finisher’.

Jamie Vardy's volley levelled the game against West Brom and Leicester went on to win 4-1

IAN HERBERT: Paul Mullin (Wrexham 2-0 Stockport, 2022)

A 90th-minute goal which sent Paul Mullin running onto a ball sent from his own half into the left channel. He’d taken nine strides and was just outside the area when, with a defender approaching, he looked up, saw the goalkeeper moving out and dug out looping a left foot shot over him, into the net.

It was the goal which co-owner Ryan Reynolds always said had switched him on to the beauty of football and, for what it’s worth, the film star’s tweet of it generated 2.1 million views.

For we Wrexham fans, though, it was the most graphic evidence we’d seen that we really did have the talent to end our non-League exile. The club had gambled on paying Mullin big wages. This proved his value.

And another vote from NATHAN SALT...

A goal that I felt I was watching in slow motion when witnessing it in real time. The game had ticked over into stoppage time, Stockport were breaking and an inch-perfect Liam McAlinden tackle stopped them in their tracks.

From there it was poetry in motion as Jordan Davies, a local lad who grew up a stone’s throw from the ground, sent Mullin clear and he chipped the goalkeeper from best part of 30 yards to send us to Wembley.

I lost my voice, picked up a few bruises in the celebrations, and can still picture it as vividly now as I did at the time. Technique, context, euphoria, the goal had it all.

Paul Mullin scored 110 goals for Wrexham in a stellar spell at the club

LEWIS STEELE: Nick Powell (Cheltenham 0-2 Crewe, 2012)

Nick Powell for Crewe Alexandra against Cheltenham in the League Two play-off final, 2012. What do you mean, dear reader, when you say you've never seen it?

The technique is outstanding and, to this day, I think he would have made it at Manchester United had Sir Alex Ferguson not left - the subsequent managers were under pressure so could not give youth players a chance.

Honourable mentions for Alejandro Garnacho for United at Everton and several Rodri goals for Manchester City. I also once saw someone back-heel a ball into their own goal from near the halfway line in Sunday League but I suppose that doesn’t count.

Nick Powell earned a move from Crewe to Manchester United in the summer of 2012 at the age of 18, just a month after his play-off final strike

WILL PICKWORTH: Dean Campbell (Aston Villa 1-2 Stevenage, 2023)

I can still vividly picture every part; David Amoo winning the corner, Jake Reeves taking it quickly, Ollie Watkins' half-hearted attempt to close Dean Campbell down, the ball squirming under Robin Olsen's arms, and the incredible away-end scenes.

As a Stevenage fan, I have never felt emotions quite like those provided by the 90th-minute winner to knock out Unai Emery's Aston Villa in the FA Cup in January 2023.

The fact it was scored by Campbell, an OK but unspectacular loanee with just seven career goals in 247 games only adds to its allure, and ensures that Boro fans will never, ever, forget the Scottish midfielder.

Sports.title: James Maddison gives Tottenham lift off: First Premier League goal in 610 days helps fire Roberto De Zerbi's men off the bottom of the table in 3-1 win over Coventry - as Dejan Kulusevski makes long-awaited return
Sports.content:
They came to salute the return of Dejan Kulusevski, and they rose to applaud James Maddison as he fired in the goal to finally give Tottenham lift off in this Premier League season. Two creative forces back in Spurs colours offering hope that things can only get better. Kulusevski came off the bench in the 87th minute to make his first appearance for close to 18 months after a serious knee injury which for a time threatened to end his career. Maddison had not started a game for even longer, with his own recovery from cruciate knee damage complicated by a setback, a hip niggle in the summer and then a shoulder injury after coming on as a sub in the first game of the season at Brentford. Roberto De Zerbi threw Maddison back into the team against Coventry, a club where his career began before leaving for Norwich more than a decade ago, and whose fans made the mistake of jeering his early touches. Maddison repaid the Spurs boss and silenced the those in the away end with a wonderful goal to give his team the lead in the 14th minute and settle a few of the jitters. James Maddison scored his first Premier League goal in 610 days to give Tottenham lift-off Dejan Kulusevski made his first outing since May 2025 and received a rapturous reception Roberto De Zerbi's side finally have a win - and the rocking Tottenham faithful loved it It swerved from his right boot just outside the penalty box and traced through an elegant arc into the top corner of the net, his first Premier League goal for 610 days. By the time he left the pitch exhausted to a standing ovation in the 69th minute, his team were 2-1 up. Jack Rudoni had equalised for Coventry before Omar Marmoush scored his first since arriving from Manchester City to restore the lead and Ben Davies added a third in the sixth minute of stoppage time. Coventry goalkeeper Carl Rushworth should have saved the effort from Davies but the home fans did not care, Finally, they could celebrate their first victory of the Premier League win of the season and with it climb off the foot of the table. It was a positive return from a training break last week on the Costa del Sol even if Spurs were far from emphatic. They were untidy at times in possession and vulnerable at the back. There are injury problems piling up. Tosin Adarabioyo, Andy Robertson and Marmoush all limped off in a nervous closing spell. On top of injuries to Pedro Porro, Savio, Lucas Bergvall, Mykhailo Mudryk and Destiny Udogie, the casualty list is lengthening once again. Nor will this performance cause sleepless nights across London at Chelsea, the opponents for Spurs on Saturday and yet this was a night De Zerbi desperately needed. First for the win to release the pressure and instil belief that they can win at home, and then to have Maddison making them tick, always looking to move the ball at a slick tempo and Kulusevski back in the picture. Ben Davies netted late on to make it a comfortable finish for Spurs, who climb to 16th De Zerbi deployed a lopsided tactical shape with three centre halves, and Jan Paul van Hecke on the right of the trio sliding across to play at times as a right back. MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS TOTTENHAM (3-1-4-2): Kinsky 6; Adarabioyo 7 (Fernandes 71min, 6), Van Hecke 6, Van de Ven 6; Tonali 6; Kudus 7 (Tel 87), Gray 6, MADDISON 8 (Gallagher 69, 6), Robertson 6 (Davies 69, 6); Solanke 6, Marmoush 7 (Kulusevski 87) Scorers: Maddison 14, Marmoush 58, Davies 90+6. Booked: Solanke. Manager: Roberto De Zerbi 7 COVENTRY CITY (4-2-3-1): Rushworth 5; Van Ewijk 6, Thomas 6, Pinnock 6, Dasilva 6; Yirenkyi 7 (Onyeka 60, 6), Grimes 6; Sakamoto 6 (Hamer 78), Rudoni 7 (Kesler-Hayden 87), Thomas-Asante 6 (Mason-Clark 78); Cherif 6 (Awoniyi 60, 5) Scorer: Rudoni 49. Booked: Dasilva, Yirenkyi, Rudoni Manager: Frank Lampard 6 Referee: Andy Madley 6 Attendance: 60,913 Toni Kinsky saved at the feet of Rudoni inside 15 seconds. Van Hecke deflected a shot from Tatsuhiro Sakamoto and Bobby Thomas went close with a header from the corner. All of this within the first 15 minutes. Mohamed Kudus proved difficult to pick up in the first half in his role as a wing back seemingly devoid of defensive duties and was involved in Maddison's opener, carrying the ball forward after Tosin won it in the air and Archie Gray moved it wide. The goal though was all about Maddison's exquisite finish, swept first time beyond the dive of Rushworth who is struggling with quality of long-range shooting in the Premier League. Brighton's Lewis Dunk and Newcastle's Sven Botman have both crashed screamers past him and there was more pain from distance for him in the second half. Spurs dominated possession, although Maddison's goal was their only shot on target in the first half and they wobbled against a Coventry team quick on the turnover and threatening from set pieces. Tosin's presence helped Spurs to cope with their aerial strength. The Van de Ven afterburners were required towards the end of the first half when Brandon Thomas-Asante darted clear of Van Hecke. Van de Ven was alert to the danger and quick on the cover with a sliding tackle. Frank Lampard's Coventry have lost their two-match winning streak but remain above the relegation zone DE ZERBI HAILS SPAIN TRAINING BREAK AND SUMMIT FOR CHANGING THE MOOD AT SPURS Roberto De Zerbi hailed the impact of a training break in Spain and a summit meeting with his players for transforming the mood inside the Tottenham dressing room. Spurs claimed their first win of the Premier League season at the seventh attempt, beating Coventry 3-1 after returning from a trip to Marbella. But De Zerbi detected a change of attitude among his players before the previous game, the fight back to draw with 10 men at Manchester United. The Spurs boss said: 'The day before Old Trafford, we had a big meeting, and we spoke about the situation and said we can't move on if we don't accept responsibility. 'Then we spent time together and want to be not a family but like a family, because during the game if you have a problem and there is a tough situation you have to play for your friend and your brother, not like robots on the pitch. 'Life is like this. If we don't react together in tough moments we have to change and play golf or another sport.' James Maddison scored the opener on his first start for almost 18 months and Dejan Kulusevski came on as a late substitute for his first appearance in just as long. 'With them in the dressing room there is another atmosphere,' said De Zerbi, who eased fears about Tosin Adarabioyo, Andy Robertson and Omar Marmoush, who all limped off before the end. 'Not injuries, nothing important.' Coventry boss Frank Lampard disputed the second Spurs goal because goalscorer Marmoush caught Milan van Ewijk in the face with an arm as he rolled clear but chose his words carefully. 'I did think that,' said Lampard. 'If you roll and elbows are that high and he connects with Milan I thought VAR would cancel it, I did. 'Have to be careful, there's no point after the event to get too deep into it.' By Matt Barlow Coventry started the season with four defeats but kicked into life with a win at Nottingham Forest before thumping four past Newcastle on their previous outing. They travelled to London with the look of a team who knew the plan and were level early in the second half. Van Hecke lost the ball dribbling out into midfield and was punished by Rudoni who linked up well with Caleb Yirenkyi and then forced a shot past Kinsky when his initial cross rebounded his way. Spurs have seldom responded well to setbacks in recent months, especially not at home in the Premier League and the fact they did will encourage De Zerbi. They went forward with purpose after the equaliser. Sandro Tonali fizzed shots over and wide before Marmoush struck. Coventry disputed the goal. They thought there was a foul by the Spurs goalscorer as he rolled out of a challenge and threw out an elbow and catching Milan van Ewijk flush in the face, but the goal would stand. Then on came Kulusevski to a rapturous ovation. And in went the third. Spurs have lift off.
