Sports.title: Russell and Leclerc are the joint ‘sprint race champions’ of 2026 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli can clinch the drivers’ championship at the next round – but three of his rivals out-scored him over the course of Formula 1’s six sprint races this year.

Singapore played host to F1’s sixth and final sprint race of 2026 last weekend. The sprint races were won by four different drivers: George Russell won three (Shanghai, Montreal and Zandvoort), while his team mate Andrea Kimi Antonelli triumphed at Silverstone, Lando Norris won in Miami and it was Max Verstappen’s turn in Singapore.

Russell could have beaten Verstappen last weekend, of course, having taken the lead off him at the start. But his crash at the end of lap one ended his chances of winning a fourth sprint race.

It also meant he ended the year with as many sprint race points as a driver who didn’t win any of these races. Charles Leclerc collected 34 points from sprint races, the same as Russell. This was made possible by the single-point gaps between finishing positions in sprint races, which are much closer than those used in grands prix.

After Russell’s retirement, Norris was on course to end the year as the top sprint race points-scorer. But his last-lap tangle with his team mate cost him three points and left him third.

As points are only awarded to the top eight finishers in sprint races, the drivers from the top four teams tended to monopolise them, with one exception: Isack Hadjar did not score a single point in a sprint race.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Liam Lawson scored points for both Red Bull (while substituting for Hadjar at Zandvoort) and Racing Bulls in sprint races. His regular team mate Arvid Lindblad also took sprint race points, as did Alpine’s Pierre Gasly and Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg.

But for almost half the grid, the sprint races offered nothing. The addition of four more sprint races next year could further increase the gap between the leading teams and the midfield.

Sports.title: On this day: Wheldon killed in IndyCar horror crash at Las Vegas finale | Briefs
Sports.content:
IndyCar champion and Indianapolis 500 winner Dan Wheldon lost his life in a horrific crash in the season finale at Las Vegas 15 years ago today.

Running in the middle of a 34-car pack on the Las Vegas Motor Speedway, Wheldon was caught up in a multi-car accident and launched into the fencing on the outside of the oval. IndyCar has not returned to the speedway since.

Wheldon’s wife Susie gave birth to their second son earlier that year. Both their sons went into racing and the eldest, Sebastian, will compete in Formula 3 next year.

Dan Wheldon’s victories included the 2005 IndyCar championship plus two wins in the Indianapolis 500. The second came earlier in 2011, in one of the most astonishing finishes ever seen at the Brickyard:

Sports.title: Singapore victory leaves Verstappen one win away from a full set – but not for long | 2026 Singapore Grand Prix stats and facts
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen’s 73rd career victory was surely one of the most overdue of his career. At his 10th attempt, the Red Bull driver finally won the Singapore Grand Prix.

He’d come close several times before. Verstappen had started second four times and converted three of those into second-place finishes. On the other occasion he was wiped out by the Ferrari drivers as they sprinted to turn one.

But after finally claiming his first pole position at the Marina Bay circuit, Verstappen never let go of his advantage, leading every lap of the race. However with other drivers switching to the preferred soft tyres over the final stint, Verstappen did not set the fastest lap, so he did not collect his seventh ‘grand slam’.

He has now won at 27 different circuits, a feat only bettered by Lewis Hamilton on 31. Verstappen has won on every track on the calendar with a single exception: the Madring, which held its first grand prix this year.

However in order to complete a clean sweep of victories at every track on the calendar, Verstappen will have to win at three new rounds next year. Two venues where he has raced in F1, but not previously won at, will return on the 2027 F1 calendar.

What’s more, another driver will be in the same position as Verstappen. This is Hamilton, the last driver to have achieved a clean sweep:

Track Verstappen’s best result Hamilton’s best result Bahrain International Circuit 1st 1st Jeddah Corniche Circuit 1st 1st Albert Park 1st 1st Suzuka 1st 1st Shanghai International Circuit 1st 1st Miami International Autodrome 1st 6th Circuit Gilles Villeneuve 1st 1st Monaco 1st 1st Autodromo do Algarve 2nd 1st Silverstone 1st 1st Red Bull Ring 1st 1st Spa-Francorchamps 1st 1st Hungaroring 1st 1st Monza 1st 1st Madring 2nd DNF Baku City Circuit 1st 1st Istanbul Park 2nd 1st Singapore 1st 1st Circuit of the Americas 1st 1st Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez 1st 1st Interlagos 1st 1st Las Vegas Strip Circuit 1st 2nd Losail International Circuit 1st 1st Yas Marina 1st 1st

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Hamilton last achieved a clean sweep when he won the French Grand Prix in 2018. He kept up the achievement over the next two seasons – even as the Covid-19 pandemic added new races to the schedule in 2020 – but his run ended when he failed to win at Zandvoort in 2021.

Achieving a clean sweep next year would arguably be a greater feat for either driver. There were 21 circuits on the calendar when Hamilton achieved it in 2018, but there are 24 on next year’s schedule.

Verstappen became the fifth driver to achieve 50 pole positions last weekend. He did so in his 250th race start and joins Ayrton Senna, who took 108 races to do the same, Hamilton (168), Michael Schumacher (177) and Sebastian Vettel (196).

This was the fourth year in a row the Singapore Grand Prix has been won from pole position. Verstappen led every lap on his way to victory, which is the fourth ‘lights-to-flag’ victory at the circuit in the last five years, along with Sergio Perez’s win in 2022 (from second on the grid), Carlos Sainz Jnr’s in 2023 and Lando Norris’s from 2024.

Red Bull was only one win behind Mercedes when the season began. However Mercedes has enjoyed such a strong season that Red Bull’s victories in the last two rounds means its is now 10 behind. However Red Bull did end Mercedes’ streak of leading at least one lap in every race this year.

Racing Bulls reached 100 points, which is more than they scored last year and their best score since 2021, when they competed as AlphaTauri.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

But Alpine’s season has decidedly hit the skids as they failed to score for the third round in a row. It was a particularly frustrating weekend for Pierre Gasly, who finished one place outside the points in both the sprint race and grand prix.

Williams left Singapore point-less, too. Carlos Sainz Jnr got his car into the top 10 early on in his 250th appearance in a grand prix weekend, but slipped to 14th at the flag.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Wanted $15 Million Per Fight From Zuffa
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson wanted $15 million per fight from Zuffa Boxing regardless of who stood across from him, according to reporter Sean Zittel. The reported figures explain why Stevenson parted ways with the promotion without stepping into their ring.

Zittel reports that Zuffa explored a January date against Jose ‘Rayo’ Valenzuela in Newark that would have paid Stevenson roughly $7 million, with an alternative December slot against an undetermined opponent carrying similar money. Stevenson turned both options down, holding out for top-tier compensation. Zittel added that Stevenson initially accepted $15 million to fight Haney before raising his demands even higher. The reporter did not disclose the final dollar amount Stevenson sought after moving the goalposts.

“He wanted $15 million no matter who was going to be put in front of him,” Zittel said on his channel about Shakur’s purse expectations.

Zittel clarified that the $15 million target was originally connected to a potential showdown with Devin Haney. Instead of treating that number as an opponent-specific purse, Stevenson reportedly wanted that guarantee for every outing. Zittel noted that while he reached out without receiving a response from Stevenson or his team, his sourcing did not come from Bill Haney or anyone in the Haney camp.

He described the split between Shakur and Zuffa as mutual, with the fighter unhappy about the available money and the company unwilling to meet his price. Walking away leaves Stevenson searching for a backer willing to exceed that $7 million mark. While launching his own promotional company grants him control over his schedule, another outfit or broadcaster still must step up to fund those purses.

High-profile opponents demand substantial guarantees of their own, quickly inflating the total cost of staging an event.

Shakur earned a defining victory over Teofimo Lopez in January, yet his tenure with Zuffa concluded without another appearance. Turning down the Valenzuela bout kept him on the sidelines during prime earning months.

Unless a network or deep-pocketed backer agrees to meet that 15 million asking price, Stevenson will struggle to balance his self-valuation with what the sport is willing to pay him. Standing firm on an inflated number risks keeping him on the shelf while the rest of the division continues to move forward without him.

Sports.title: Carlos Adames Zuffa Debut Draws Fan Criticism
Sports.content:
Carlos Adames’ reported Zuffa Boxing debut against Gerome Warburton is drawing criticism from fans who see the Welsh fighter as an underwhelming opponent for the WBC middleweight champion.

According to Dan Rafael, Adames will face Warburton in the November 14 main event in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The bout will take place above 160 pounds, with Adames’ WBC title not at stake.

For Zuffa, signing Adames brings an established champion into its middleweight roster. However, introducing him against Warburton gives fans little opportunity to judge him against one of the division’s leading contenders. It looks like an opportunity for Adames to collect a win and make an impression before moving toward a bigger fight.

Warburton, 31, has an 18-2-2 record with two knockouts. That limited knockout total helps explain the reaction to his selection. Adames is accustomed to facing world-level opposition, and Warburton has yet to prove he belongs in that company.

His fourth-round stoppage loss to Kieron Conway in May 2025 is another reason fans are questioning the matchmaking. Conway beat him at British and Commonwealth level. Now Warburton is being brought in to headline against a reigning world champion.

There is some recent form in Warburton’s favor. He has won three consecutive fights since that defeat, including victories over Nathan Heaney in March and September this year. Those results deserve recognition when discussing how he landed this opportunity.

Nonetheless, beating Heaney twice does not establish Warburton as one of the best middleweights available. Adames represents a much higher level, and the pressure will be on the champion to produce a performance that reflects that difference.

A quick stoppage would give Zuffa a highlight to promote. A long, competitive fight could bring more criticism of Adames and raise questions about what this debut achieved.

The matchup gives Warburton a major opportunity. Adames has considerably less to gain.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Leaves Zuffa After Three Months
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson says Zuffa Boxing granted his release over the weekend, ending his three-month stay without a fight. The unbeaten four-division champion plans to start his own promotional company and pursue opponents at lightweight and light welterweight.

Stevenson announced the split in a video posted on his YouTube channel and shared on X. He described spending eight weeks in camp preparing for fights that never materialized.

“I requested to be released from Zuffa Boxing. Now over the weekend, my request has been granted, and now I am officially a free agent,” Stevenson said.

The 29-year-old signed with the Dana White-led company in July. He hasn’t fought since defeating Teofimo Lopez on January 31 at Madison Square Garden to win the WBO and Ring light welterweight titles.

Negotiations for a Devin Haney fight failed to produce an agreement amid disagreements over weight and rehydration conditions. Talks involving WBA light welterweight champion Gary Antuanne Russell also failed to produce a fight.

Stevenson insisted he wasn’t looking to blame anyone for his inactivity.

“This is the business of boxing. I’m not mad at anyone. I’m not pointing no fingers.”

Nevertheless, leaving so soon after signing shows how quickly his plans with Zuffa unraveled. The company secured a prominent unbeaten champion, but the relationship ended before he appeared on one of its cards. Zuffa declined immediate comment to The Ring.

Stevenson now wants control over how his next fights are arranged.

“I am now taking my career in my own hands and I’m starting my own promotional company,” he said.

He added that he is willing to work with other promoters and networks, opening the possibility of partnerships rather than another exclusive promotional deal. Shakur calling himself a promoter sounds empowering on social media, but acting as an actual bank is an entirely different business.

Starting a promotional banner without self-funding just means running an LLC to collect an extra operational fee while someone else assumes all the downside risk. If Stevenson expects a guaranteed purse in the multi-million-dollar range, that check has to clear through site fees, network licensing rights, ticket gates, and pay-per-view buys.

When an elite fighter possesses a purely defensive, safety-first ring style, the math turns hostile very quickly. Traditional promoters like Matchroom, Top Rank, or Queensberry understand what it takes to make an event profitable.

If external backers refuse to absorb those deficits, Stevenson will eventually face two stark paths: either accept realistic purses based on actual revenue generation, or find a wealthy benefactor willing to burn capital regardless of the balance sheet.

The moment Shakur put pen to paper with Zuffa and immediately waved off Jose “Rayo” Valenzuela, the whole premise of the deal fell apart. Dana White’s business model has always run on control, matching his roster internally, and fighters taking the bouts handed to them. Shakur treated the setup like a traditional boxing boutique where he could dictate terms, pick who makes financial sense, and snub the promoter’s own in-house assets.

Cutting bait after just three months was simply accepting the obvious. Shakur’s approach to the sport is completely incompatible with Dana White’s playbook.

“Give it maybe a year or two, we will get to 147 where everybody is pressing me to just be a 147-pounder,” Stevenson said. “I will get there, but on my term and not on nobody else’s.”

Sports.title: Jaime Munguia Wants Melikuziev Fight Next Year
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguia intends to put his ordered title defense against Bektemir Melikuziev on hold until next year, insisting he requires a dedicated training camp while gearing up to face Nikita Zon on October 31.

The WBA super middleweight champion remains focused on competing on the Canelo Alvarez vs. Christian Mbilli undercard in Riyadh. Still, wanting to delay Melikuziev until 2027 raises major concerns regarding whether sanctioning officials will let him keep the belt while taking an unapproved interim contest.

The WBA previously noted that the Munguia vs. Zon matchup had not received sanctioning approval, adding that officials would review the matter while keeping Melikuziev in position as the mandatory challenger. Munguia gave no indication during the interview that he secured an exemption or official sign-off to delay the mandatory.

Instead, the titlist pointed to the compressed schedule as the reason he cannot face Melikuziev right away.

“Proper training camp and other things. But we have a short time for that fight,” Munguia told The Ring. “I think next year it’s going to be a good fight.”

Wanting a complete camp for an opponent like Melikuziev makes sense on paper. Shifting focus from one challenger to a heavy-handed mandatory creates complications, especially on shortened notice.

Still, personal preference does not erase championship duties. Melikuziev locked in his mandatory status through official channels. Forcing him to sit on the sidelines while Munguia takes another bout requires formal sanctioning body consent, not just the champion deciding a later date suits him better.

When the interviewer floated a schedule featuring Melikuziev in May and Hamzah Sheeraz in September, Munguia welcomed the Sheeraz option. Neither date, however, represents a signed agreement.

For now, Munguia is guaranteeing an explosive finish against Zon.

“It’s going to be a good fight, and it’s going to be a knockout,” Munguia said.

A stoppage win in Riyadh could generate a highlight reel moment on a major international stage. It will not resolve the uncertainty surrounding his strap. Until the WBA formally rules on the matter, Munguia is laying out a calendar he desires rather than one he is authorized to carry out.

Sports.title: Alberto Puello Plans To Mark Up Dalton Smith
Sports.content:
Alberto Puello plans to test Dalton Smith’s accuracy and cut-prone skin on Saturday, when the WBC light welterweight champion makes his first defense at Sheffield’s Utilita Arena. Smith could have a difficult night if he cannot consistently find the skilled southpaw.

Puello (25-1, 11 KOs) brings a different style than Subriel Matias, whom Smith stopped in five rounds in January. Matias gave Smith opportunities to plant his feet and fire during their shootout. Puello is unlikely to offer the same opportunities.

“With the big head he has, I’m not going to miss a blow. It’s going to be very easy to mark him up,” Puello told The Ring.

That threat has some substance behind it. Smith has suffered cuts around his eyes during his career, including against Matias. Puello’s ability to land accurately could become an issue even without the punching power normally associated with a knockout threat.

The Eddie Hearn-promoted Smith (19-0, 14 KOs) needs to avoid spending rounds following Puello without getting his punches off. Coming through boxing in the Dominican Republic, Puello has been exposed to different styles, and he has the professional experience to change his approach when something stops working.

Against Matias, Smith was dealing with a one-track pressure fighter whose instinct is to walk in behind high earmuff defense and trade at point-blank range. That allowed Smith to tie him up on the inside, rough him up, lean on him, and time his short hooks in the clinch. Matias basically walked straight into Smith’s traps because he has zero interest in back-foot boxing.

Puello is the polar opposite. He is not going to march into Smith’s chest to give him free clinches or let Smith wrap him up. He fights behind a long, tricky southpaw jab, controls distance, and steps off to the sides the second an opponent tries to close the gap.

Hearn has matched Smith against guys who come forward, allowing him to use his heavy-handed throwback fighting style to bludgeon them. Against a pure mover with an awkward southpaw stance like Puello, that exact style can make a fighter look flat-footed, crude, and completely out of ideas over twelve rounds. Style-wise, Puello is a nightmare for him.

Puello lost his WBC 140-lb title to Matias by a controversial 12-round majority decision in July 2025. He now travels to the champion’s hometown intending to leave less room for debate.

“The way I do it is to win clearly and never deviate from that plan that I have,” Puello said.

Sports.title: Daniel Dubois Targets February With Agit Kabayel Possible
Sports.content:
Daniel Dubois wants to be back in the ring this February. Frank Warren is eyeing Agit Kabayel to set up a massive heavyweight unification clash.

Dubois retained his WBO title by stopping Fabio Wardley in two rounds on Saturday at London’s O2 Arena, leaving him ready to pursue another champion without the need for a third fight with Wardley.

“He’ll fight in February, we are going to see what happens,” Warren told talkSPORT.

Warren is keeping a close eye on Kabayel’s November 28 defense against Nelson Hysa in Germany. He reported approximately 43,000 to 44,000 tickets sold for that event.

“Let’s see the outcome because that would be a fantastic unification scrap,” Warren said.

Kabayel offers a different challenge than Wardley. The German works the body with relentless pressure. He aims to drag opponents into deep waters rather than trade quick bombs. Dubois packs enough power to crack him coming forward, so it would get violent immediately.

If Kabayel drags him into rounds five, six, and seven while ripping hooks into his ribs, Dubois will be forced to answer the exact mental questions he has struggled with throughout his career.

The calendar could be tricky, though, to make a Dubois vs. Kabayel unification fight. Going from late November to February leaves barely two months to recover. If Hysa pushes Kabayel hard, that turnaround shrinks fast. Right now Warren is floating an option, not closing a contract.

Filip Hrgovic is also hovering around the picture. The IBF champ sat ringside Saturday night, looking for revenge against the only man who beat him as a pro.

“He wanted a rematch since Daniel holds a win over him,” Warren said.

Dubois holds plenty of leverage while his destruction of Wardley is fresh in everyone’s minds. Snatching another belt cements his status. Taking on Kabayel gives him a fresh face after crushing Wardley back-to-back.

Warren made it clear his fighter is chasing giant paydays, too.

“He wants big fights because he tells me he wants to make huge money,” Warren said.

February stays circled on the calendar. Once Kabayel gets past November, Dubois will know if he has a chance to make this fight happen.

Sports.title: Oscar Collazo Faces Mandatory Order After Flyweight Setback
Sports.content:
The WBO is not doing Oscar Collazo any favors. Just as the Puerto Rican minimumweight champion was preparing to walk away from 105 pounds, the sanctioning body stepped in to complicate matters, ordering him to defend his strap against interim titleholder Ryusei Matsumoto within a 15-day negotiating window.

The timing could hardly be worse for Collazo. He had already set his sights on bigger game, skipping right past light flyweight to challenge Ricardo Sandoval for two flyweight belts on October 10 in Chicago.

That two-division title run was ruined when a painful rib injury in training camp knocked him off the card. Instead of resting up and rescheduling his run at 112, Collazo now finds the WBO knocking on his door, insisting he settle business at the minimumweight limit.

WBO representative Gustavo Olivieri laid down the law on social media, making it clear that both camps have two weeks to hammer out terms or the fight goes straight to purse bids. The organization is leaning on its rule of keeping only one champion per division, which puts an end to Matsumoto’s interim status one way or another.

The order simply covers the paperwork, not a fight date. Nobody expects Collazo in the ring tomorrow, especially with bruised or broken ribs needing time to heal. The real issue is the weight. Making 105 pounds is brutal for any fighter growing into his prime, and Collazo had already mentally and physically started the transition to flyweight. Asking his body to drop back down for Matsumoto is a grueling chore that risks stalling his career.

Collazo holds the cards, but neither option is simple. Walking away from the belt leaves him empty-handed with nothing guaranteed at 112, while taking the Matsumoto fight delays his move up for several months.

Matsumoto’s team is in a great position, knowing they either get a shot at the real belt or pick it up by default. Collazo has to decide if keeping the hardware is worth the torture of making 105 one more time.

For Collazo, the risk-to-reward ratio is completely upside down. If he wins, what does he get? A small purse and the privilege of holding a belt that does not move the needle commercially. If he enters the ring drained from making weight and gets caught or looks sluggish against Matsumoto, his entire stock drops before he ever gets to cash in at flyweight.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Still Has Plenty Of Paydays Available
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley can still bag massive paydays below elite title level. Calls for him to hang up the gloves after getting stopped by Daniel Dubois completely miss that reality. Falling short against Dubois does not strip him of his ability to top domestic bills.

Derek Chisora wrote the playbook here. Chisora never had to conquer top-tier heavyweights to fill arenas or generate huge paychecks. British fans recognize him, know the entertainment they are paying for, and show up. Wardley can mirror that blueprint without wasting years fruitlessly chasing a rematch with Dubois.

Domestic dust-ups against Dave Allen, Johnny Fisher, or Chisora himself offer immediate box-office appeal. Efe Ajagba or Tony Yoka provide solid international flavor. None of those are walkovers, but none require beating a pound-for-pound monster to pack out a venue.

The draw remains unchanged. Fans know Wardley hits like a truck, and they know he can get hurt in return. Put Wardley in the ring with Fisher, and nobody cares if a world belt is on the line; they are tuning in because someone is going to sleep.

That leaves Queensberry holding plenty of cards. A routine bounce-back victory followed by a massive domestic main event puts him right back in the money without pretending he solved the Dubois riddle.

Down the line, reaching the end of his Queensberry deal might even open up a fresh bidding war. Zuffa could easily see value in an action-heavy British brawler. While nothing is on the table right now, it highlights how many avenues exist beyond this single loss.

Wardley’s physical condition must always come first. From a purely business perspective, the path is clear. Chisora proved you can remain a massive ticket seller without beating the division’s champions.

Wardley does not need another belt around his waist to get paid. Pick the right matchups, and he can laugh all the way to the bank for years to come.

Ghana News.title: Sexual abuse: Stop putting the burden on girls; teach boys respect — Advocate
Ghana News.content:
Amtu Akumfi-Ameyaw

A survivor of sexual abuse has called for a shift in how society tackles sexual violence, urging families to teach boys and men to respect others rather than placing the burden of preventing abuse largely on girls.

Amtu Akumfi-Ameyaw, co-founder of On This Side, said persistent warnings to girls about their clothing, movements and social interactions would do little to address sexual abuse if equal attention was not given to educating boys about boundaries, respect and responsible behaviour.

She made the call on Joy News’ PM Express on Monday, October 19, while reacting to developments in the allegations of sexual abuse involving female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS).

The allegations are the subject of Manasseh Azure Awuni’s documentary, Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow. It examines alleged sexual abuse involving female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School.

Click here to Watch the documentary.

“We continue to ask and dictate how girls should keep themselves. Oh, don't do this. Don't go here. Don't engage with this person. Don't wear these clothes,” she said.

“And we forget that we also have to socialise our men and our boys to be better and responsible human beings of society.”

Her comments come amid public concern over allegations involving the school’s headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai. The allegations have prompted renewed discussion about how sexual abuse is prevented, reported and addressed, particularly in institutions entrusted with the care of young people.

Rethink the responsibility

Ms Akumfi-Ameyaw said society needed to examine why girls were routinely told to take precautions against abuse while comparatively less emphasis was placed on ensuring that boys understood the importance of respecting other people’s boundaries.

She argued that the approach risked placing responsibility on potential victims while failing to confront the conduct of those who perpetrate abuse.

For her, efforts to prevent sexual violence must go beyond instructing girls on how to protect themselves and include deliberate efforts by families and communities to raise boys who understand consent, personal boundaries and accountability.

She said the persistence of abuse despite repeated warnings to girls raised questions about whether enough was being done to address the behaviour of perpetrators.

Respect starts at home

The advocate also challenged families that placed considerable importance on having male children to carry on the family name or serve as heirs, but did not give equal attention to teaching them respect for others.

“We have to take it seriously,” she said. “We can't be having families desire to have male kids to become heirs, but we don't care about teaching them basic things of respect.”

She said the prevention of sexual abuse required a broader change in attitudes, with parents, schools and communities taking responsibility for instilling appropriate values in boys from an early age.

Ms Akumfi-Ameyaw acknowledged that men and boys could also be victims of abuse, although she noted that women were disproportionately affected, according to data from around the world.

She said the experiences of all survivors needed to be recognised, while prevention efforts must respond to the patterns of abuse reflected in the available evidence.

Ms Akumfi-Ameyaw said survivors often faced difficult emotions, including guilt and disappointment, and could struggle to speak about their experiences when they feared they would not be believed or supported.

She called for society to take sexual abuse seriously rather than trivialising allegations or placing the responsibility for preventing abuse solely on those who may become victims.

Ghana News.title: ‘We all know an abuser, but choose to protect them’ – Sexual abuse survivor
Ghana News.content:
Amtu Akumfi-Ameyaw

A survivor of sexual abuse has accused society of turning a blind eye to perpetrators, saying people often protect those they know or respect while questioning the experiences of victims.

Amtu Akumfi-Ameyaw, co-founder of On This Side, said the tendency to defend alleged abusers, dismiss complaints and treat sexual abuse as a joke discouraged survivors from speaking out and reinforced the guilt and emotional distress they already experienced.

Reacting to developments in the alleged sexual abuse of female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), she said the response to such cases reflected a wider social problem in which people were quick to demand that girls protect themselves but paid less attention to teaching boys to respect others.

The allegations are the subject of Manasseh Azure Awuni’s documentary, Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow. It examines alleged sexual abuse involving female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School.

Click here to Watch the documentary.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Monday, October 19, she said people often pretended not to know sexual abusers, even when they were within their families, friendship circles or communities.

“I kid you not; each and every one of us knows an abuser. Each and every one of us,” she said.

“Sometimes we cover it because we care too much about other people, because they are loved ones, they are people we respect, and things like that.”

Silence and misplaced loyalty

Ms Akumfi-Ameyaw said the instinct to protect people who were loved or respected could lead families and communities to minimise allegations of abuse rather than confront them.

She likened the practice to selective opposition to corruption, arguing that people tended to condemn wrongdoing until someone close to them was implicated.

“If it hasn't happened to you or somebody you love, it looks like a joke,” she said. “And then also, if somebody you love or you care about is the abuser, you tend to take an entrenched position of defending them, of making it look like it's okay.”

She said such attitudes made it easier for communities to sweep allegations under the carpet, leaving survivors to contend with the consequences while those accused received protection.

Her comments followed public discussion surrounding a video related to the Obuasi SHTS allegations, in which a remark about an alleged incident being “a kiss on the cheek” had drawn attention.

Ms Akumfi-Ameyaw said the reaction illustrated how sexual abuse could be trivialised, particularly when people were unwilling to acknowledge wrongdoing by someone they knew.

Why survivors sometimes remain silent

The advocate said survivors often struggled with intense emotions, including disappointment and guilt, after their boundaries had been violated.

They could also blame themselves for failing to prevent the abuse, she said, and those feelings could deepen when trusted adults failed to provide the support they expected.

She cited housemistresses, senior housemistresses and teachers as examples of people students might turn to for help, but whose failure to respond appropriately could reinforce a survivor’s sense of helplessness.

When victims then heard people laughing about or dismissing their experiences, she said, they could conclude that what had happened to them did not matter.

That, she explained, could help account for why some survivors initially disclosed their experiences but later withdrew their accounts.

“They are dealing with their own battles,” she said, adding that survivors had to contend with significant emotional burdens even before deciding whether to speak publicly.

Ms Akumfi-Ameyaw also addressed the increase in the number of students reported to have come forward in connection with the Obuasi SHTS case.

She suggested that some students might have felt more able to speak when they realised that others had experienced similar situations and that support might be available.

“Because now they feel that they belong. They feel that they identify. They feel that maybe some level of help could get to them,” she said.

She urged the public not to interpret delayed disclosures as a reason to dismiss survivors’ accounts, saying the decision to speak could be shaped by fear, shame, isolation and uncertainty about whether anyone would help.

Teach boys to respect others

Ms Akumfi-Ameyaw said public discussions of sexual abuse often placed the responsibility for prevention on girls, with warnings about where they went, whom they interacted with and what they wore.

She argued that equal attention must be given to educating boys and men about respect, boundaries and responsible behaviour.

“We continue to ask and dictate how girls should keep themselves. Oh, don't do this. Don't go here. Don't engage with this person. Don't wear these clothes,” she said.

“And we forget that we also have to socialise our men and our boys to be better and responsible human beings of society.”

She acknowledged that boys and men could also experience abuse, although she said women were disproportionately affected according to data from around the world.

For her, the continued focus on telling potential victims how to avoid abuse raised questions about whether enough was being done to address the behaviour of perpetrators.

“We have to take it seriously,” she said. “We can't be having families desire to have male kids to become heirs, but we don't care about teaching them basic things of respect.”

Ghana News.title: Survivors feel a sense of guilt for failing to protect themselves from sexual abuse – Advocate
Ghana News.content:
Amtu Akumfi-Ameyaw

Survivors of sexual abuse often grapple with guilt and emotional distress, sometimes blaming themselves for failing to prevent the abuse, a survivor advocate, Amtu Akumfi-Ameyaw, has said.

She said those feelings could become more painful when trusted adults, including teachers and housemistresses expected to offer protection, failed to provide the support survivors needed.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Monday, October 19, Ms Akumfi-Ameyaw, co-founder of On This Side, a survivor-focused initiative, said the allegations of sexual abuse involving female students of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) had brought back memories of why it took her so long to speak about her own experience.

The allegations are the subject of investogative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni’s documentary, Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow. It examines alleged sexual abuse involving female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School.

Click here to Watch the documentary.

“I don't know if I should cry. I don't know if I should scream. I'm having, like, mixed feelings,” she said, describing her reaction to the developments.

She explained that survivors could feel disappointed in themselves after someone violated their personal boundaries, believing they should have been able to protect themselves.

“So there's a certain level of supposed guilt that you have that you couldn't protect yourself from abuse," she said.

Ms Akumfi-Ameyaw said the situation could become even more distressing when people survivors trusted to help them were unable to offer the necessary support.

When trusted adults fail

The advocate identified teachers, housemistresses and other school authorities as people students might naturally turn to when they experienced abuse.

However, she said the failure of such trusted figures to respond appropriately could reinforce survivors’ feelings of guilt and leave them questioning whether their experiences mattered.

She said hearing people laugh about or trivialise alleged abuse could deepen that emotional burden.

The response survivors received after disclosing their experiences was therefore critical, she suggested, because it could affect their willingness to continue speaking out.

Ms Akumfi-Ameyaw said some survivors who initially disclosed their experiences might later withdraw their accounts because of the personal struggles they faced.

“And it's the reason why you would actually even have some people come out to say their stories and eventually change their mind and say that you know what, everything was a lie. It never happened,” she said.

She added that survivors were often dealing with difficult emotions that others might not fully appreciate.

Ghana News.title: Billionaires fund Nigerian artists – Sarkodie
Ghana News.content:
Rapper Sarkodie has stated that Nigerian artists receive substantial financial support from billionaires and business executives in the country, unlike their Ghanaian counterparts.

In a recent episode of the When We Sit podcast, the Azonto crooner said Ghanaian artists often make music on their own, without any financial assistance from fellow Ghanaians.

He said Nigerian businessmen love to support and invest in talent, giving Nigerian artists a financial advantage in Africa.

"What Ghanaian artists do is organic. I give a business plan; even with that, it is hard to get some people to come in. But in Nigeria, I think they take a lot of risks; most rich people take a lot of risks to put their people on. If I break down what it takes to do the O2 Arena, you will freak out, but then we still have to do it," he said.

He recalled meeting Nigerian billionaire Tony Elumelu and being shocked by the amount he told him he was investing in a Nigerian artist, whom he believes is the future of Afrobeats.

Sarkodie urged Ghanaian business executives and rich folks to emulate Nigerian business leaders by financially supporting their artists.

Ghana News.title: Obuasi SHTS head saying GES exonerated him is the biggest insult to victims – Manasseh
Ghana News.content:
Investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni has challenged reports that the Ashanti Regional office of the Ghana Education Service (GES) has exonerated the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), Zakaria Abdulai, over allegations of sexual abuse involving female students.

He has questioned the regional education authorities’ capacity to determine allegations involving rape, arguing that the matter requires a criminal investigation by the police.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Monday, October 19, Mr Azure said any claim that the headmaster had been cleared by the regional office was deeply troubling, particularly given reports that complaints had previously been made to school authorities.

“I think it's the biggest insult to the victims and Ghanaians to say that the GES exonerated him,” he said. “This GES is within the enclave. These are the people who should have acted when reports upon reports went out."

The journalist said the committee that reportedly examined the matter was chaired by the Obuasi East Director of Education, raising questions about the process and its ability to address allegations of a criminal nature.

He also referred to concerns he said had been expressed by people in the Obuasi area about the response of school management and regional education authorities to the alleged incidents.

“Obuasi East and Obuasi West are so close. And if you go to that enclave, there are people who say that from the school's management to the regional GES looked away when these things happened,” he said.

Mr Azure questioned whether the committee had the expertise and mandate to investigate allegations of rape, insisting that such claims should be handled through the criminal justice system.

“So if those same people come out to say they have cleared him, they have exonerated him, these are allegations of rape,” he said.

“Which of them on that committee is equipped to investigate rape? This is a police, a criminal matter.”

Call for criminal investigation

The allegations are the subject of Manasseh Azure Awuni’s documentary, Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow. It examines alleged sexual abuse involving female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School.

Click here to Watch the documentary.

Mr Azure’s comments come amid public concern over reports that female students had made allegations of rape, sexual harassment, sexual assault and other forms of abuse involving the headmaster.

The allegations, which have attracted attention following the report by Mr Azure, have also prompted calls for the affected students to be protected from intimidation and for their complaints to be investigated independently.

A GES administrative inquiry and a police criminal investigation serve different purposes. Any determination of criminal responsibility must follow the applicable legal process.

The claims against Mr Abdulai remain allegations and must be established through a fair and credible investigation.

The matter has raised broader questions about how schools handle complaints of sexual abuse, the protection available to students who report alleged misconduct and the accountability of education authorities when concerns are brought to their attention.

Ghana News.title: SA High Commission admits errors in evacuation records, says future birth dates were passport expiry dates
Ghana News.content:
Ghana’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Benjamin Quashie

Ghana’s High Commission in South Africa has accepted responsibility for errors in the records of 15 evacuees. It says dates flagged in a JoyNews analysis as future birth dates were actually passport expiry dates.

The clarification follows JoyNews reports suggesting that the government, through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, paid reintegration and transportation allowances to people whose recorded birth dates were in the future.

In a statement issued on Monday, the mission in Pretoria described the discrepancies as minor clerical errors. It said they affected 15 of the 1,964 Ghanaians evacuated from South Africa.

“Our verification of the records indicates that the dates interpreted as dates of birth were, in fact, passport expiry dates.”

The High Commission acknowledged that its officials may have made errors while transcribing passport details. It attributed the mistakes to the emergency circumstances surrounding the evacuation of distressed Ghanaians.

It maintained that all evacuees completed the required identification, data-processing and departure procedures before leaving South Africa.

“However, these minor clerical errors do not invalidate the identities of the evacuees, their participation in the evacuation exercise, or the fact that they received the approved reintegration and transportation allowances.”

The mission supplied birth dates and passport expiry dates for several people referenced in the reports. These included James Akoto Baffour, Precious Sekyiwaa, Philip Oduro and Victoria Eduaquah.

It also clarified that six members of the Jibril family, comprising a mother and five children, travelled on Emergency Travel Certificates.

The High Commission said corrected information on the 15 individuals had been provided in an amended list to enable records to be updated.

It said it respected the media’s role in promoting transparency and accountability. It encouraged verification with official sources when discrepancies emerge in administrative records.

The mission urged the media and the public to rely on the corrected records.

“Fundamentally, we are proud of our efforts and sacrifices to save the lives of Ghanaians and bring them home safely.”

Ghana News.title: Obama blasts federal probe of Congresswoman Ilhan Omar as ‘so appalling’
Ghana News.content:
Barack Obama has said Congresswoman Ilhan Omar is under federal criminal investigation simply because she's an outspoken critic of President Donald Trump.

"The full weight of the federal government is being brought down on a law-abiding elected official because she has dared to criticise the president," the former US president wrote on X, calling the probe "so appalling".

The White House defended the inquiry, saying the Justice Department was "focused on restoring law and order".

Last week, Homeland Security agents searched the Minnesota Democrat's Washington, D.C., home as part of an investigation into her immigration status. Born in Somalia, Omar moved to the US with her family as a child.

US media outlets have reported that the probe is tied to her American citizenship and whether she lied about her age when she arrived in the US in 1995.

Questions have been raised about whether the age listed on Omar's citizenship application differed from her actual birth date.

Obama said in his X post on Sunday that her father became a naturalised citizen when she was 17, and not yet legally an adult, which then gave her citizenship.

"Now the Administration is actively trying to deport Congresswoman Omar, seemingly based solely on the unsubstantiated theory that she was actually 18 when her father was naturalised, and therefore is not a citizen," he wrote.

"If this becomes the new normal," he added, "there's no reason to believe it will stop with her - or that future presidents, in either party, won't do the same."

According to the US Citizenship and Immigration Services, a child born outside of the US automatically becomes a citizen when he or she has at least one parent who is a citizen by birth or naturalisation, or he or she is under the age of 18 and is a lawful permanent resident living in the custody of a citizen parent.

White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis denied the investigation was politically motivated.

"Unlike Joe Biden, President Trump has not weaponised the Department of Justice against his political foes," she said in an emailed statement to the BBC.

"The Department is focused on restoring law and order and keeping Americans safe."

Trump has often argued that federal criminal investigations against him as he campaigned for re-election were politically motivated.

The investigation into Omar could lead to the Justice Department seeking to "denaturalise" her, or revoke her citizenship. It would have to prove there were material lies in the naturalisation process.

In 2023, Republicans removed Omar from the House Foreign Affairs Committee for comments and tweets she made about Israel, which drew bipartisan criticism.

Omar has said that Trump has targeted her for years with "baseless lies and smear campaigns" and called the investigation "the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation".

But Trump has said the investigation had "nothing to do" with him, while describing Omar as a "terrible person" and a "complainer".

Federal agents reportedly seized her phone, computers, notebooks and passport in the raid a week ago.

Her lawyers have demanded that the government return her belongings, CBS News, the BBC's US partner, has reported, arguing in a letter sent on Friday that the seizure of property had violated restrictions imposed by a judge to protect her work as a federal lawmaker.

The lawyers also alleged that agents did not duly notify Omar or the House of Representatives' general counsel that a search would take place and kept her from contacting her attorney for more than an hour, according to CBS.

Democrats characterised the raid as the president attempting to interfere with the legislative branch of government. Republicans, meanwhile, have said Omar should be treated the same as anyone else under the law.

When Obama first ran for president, and throughout his two terms in the White House, Trump repeatedly raised questions about his citizenship, asserting he was not born on American soil and was disqualified from serving in office.

Obama released two records proving that he was born in Hawaii. Obama did not mention that history in his X post on Sunday.

Ghana News.title: We have stabilised the present; we must now secure the future’ — Ato Forson
Ghana News.content:
Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson

Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has called for a decisive break with the economic patterns that have held Ghana back, saying the country must now build on stabilisation to secure lasting prosperity.

Speaking during his New Economy engagement with faculty and students at the University of Ghana, Dr Forson said Ghana had reached a moment when public policy must confront the underlying causes of its economic challenges.

“We have stabilised the present. Now we must secure the future,” he declared.

The Finance Minister framed the next phase of Ghana’s economic journey as a test of the country’s willingness to make decisions that would shape the prospects of future generations.

“History does not wait for countries that are afraid to decide,” he said.

“There are moments when a nation must make a clear break with old patterns. There are moments when public policy must stop managing symptoms and start changing structures. This is such a moment for Ghana.”

His remarks placed structural transformation at the centre of the New Economy agenda, with economic stability serving as the foundation for a more productive economy that creates decent jobs and raises incomes.

The challenge, he indicated, is to move beyond addressing immediate pressures and change the conditions that allow those pressures to recur.

That ambition, to him, means producing more at home, adding value to what Ghana grows and mines, and expanding opportunities for businesses and workers.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Saudi Arabia cancels 2026 ‘Davos in the Desert’ amid Houthi attacks
World.content:
Saudi Arabia’s Future Investment Initiative (FII) conference has been postponed until next year, according to a statement on the official website, as deadly strikes by the Iran-backed Houthis against the kingdom continue.

The annual event was due to start next week on October 26 and run through October 29, with a date next year to be announced “very soon”, the statement released on Tuesday said.

FII Institute chief executive officer Dr Maha Bint Mishari Al Saud said the decision “comes from a deep commitment to our partners, members, speakers and delegates”.

“Because this is our landmark tenth edition, we want to ensure it delivers the full scale, extraordinary quality, and unforgettable impact that our community has come to expect and truly deserves,” she said.

Informally dubbed “Davos in the Desert”, a nod to the World Economic Forum’s annual meeting in Switzerland, the state-backed conference showcases the kingdom’s ambitious investment plans in a bid to attract billions of dollars needed to fund its economic transformation away from hydrocarbons towards tourism, sport and technology.

Expected speakers included: Alphabet & Google’s president and chief information officer, Ruth Porat; Goldman Sachs Group chairman and CEO David Solomon; and BlackRock chairman and CEO Laurence Fink, according to the FII website.

Fighting between a Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen’s internationally recognised government and the Iran-aligned Houthis has escalated in recent weeks.



The Houthis, also known as Ansar Allah, have hit military, energy and civilian infrastructure across Saudi Arabia, including Riyadh’s international airport, killing at least 18 people and injuring hundreds more.

Government staff to work from home

Government agencies in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, have told employees to work from home, one worker and two consultants told the AFP news agency, as the city comes under repeated attack from the Houthis.

The Kingdom Centre, a 99‑storey tower in downtown Riyadh that houses the International Monetary Fund’s regional office, also requested workers stay away until further notice.

On Sunday, an employee of a government agency in the capital received a message saying, “It has been decided to implement remote work from Monday to Thursday this week”. The message added: “We ask everyone to continue their activities as normal.”

Companies based in the King Abdullah Financial District, which hosts offices of major United States firms, have also asked employees to work from home, according to other sources.
