World.title: Rashida Tlaib demands arrest of Israeli soldier linked to Hind Rajab death
World.content:
US lawmaker says that government must arrest Israeli commander allegedly responsible for attack while he is in the US.

United States Representative Rashida Tlaib has called for her government to arrest the commander of an Israeli military unit believed to be responsible for the killing of five-year-old Palestinian girl Hind Rajab in Gaza.

In a social media post on Monday, Tlaib pointed to reports that Israeli soldier Sean Glass was present in the US. She emphasised that the US had a legal responsibility to probe his involvement in Rajab’s death.

“As a party to the Genocide Convention and the Geneva Conventions, our government is obligated to arrest and investigate him for these war crimes and acts of genocide,” she wrote.

As part of her post, Tlaib shared a report from the Hind Rajab Foundation (HRF), which tracks Israeli soldiers suspected of war crimes in Gaza.

The group said it has filed an emergency request for the US Department of Justice to arrest Glass.

“Sean Glass commanded the ‘Vampire Empire’ Company implicated in the killing of five-year-old Hind Rajab, members of her family, and the medics sent to rescue them. HRF’s investigation places him and his troops in the direct vicinity of Hind’s vehicle during the killing,” the group said in a statement.

“Today, Glass walks free in the United States. HRF demands that the US authorities arrest him and bring him to justice.”

The five-year-old’s killing on January 29, 2024, triggered global outrage and became a symbol of Israel’s targeting of Palestinian civilians and children during its genocidal war on Gaza.

Rajab and her family were attempting to leave Gaza City when their vehicle came under Israeli fire.



Her family was killed in the gunfire. Rajab called emergency services, appealing to rescuers, “I’m so scared. Please come!”

Recordings of her telephone call made international news. But both Rajab and the rescue team that tried to reach her were ultimately killed by Israeli forces.

The car Rajab was in was riddled with 335 bullet holes, which Israeli authorities initially blamed on a firefight with Palestinian fighters.

An investigation by the group Forensic Architecture found no evidence of an exchange of fire and concluded that only Israeli forces had been present in the area at the time of the incident.

Israel has opened a probe into the killings, but such investigations are seen by Palestinians as a means of dodging accountability and buying time until outrage over an incident dissipates.

Experts at the United Nations and other human rights watchdogs have declared Israel’s assault on Gaza to be a genocide. At least 74,000 Palestinians have been killed, including at least 21,000 children.

The US has continued to bolster Israel with diplomatic, military and economic assistance despite evidence of routine war crimes by Israeli forces in Gaza and elsewhere.

It has also denounced the International Criminal Court (ICC) for seeking the arrest of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Defence Minister Yoav Gallant on charges of war crimes.

World.title: Hegseth meets Netanyahu in unannounced Israel visit
World.content:
Hegseth has travelled to Israel to meet Netanyahu ahead of a closely contested election, Axios reported, citing sources.

US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has met with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during an undisclosed visit to Israel, according to Axios.

The meeting between the hawkish ally of US President Donald Trump and the veteran Israeli premier facing a knife-edge election occurred on Monday, Axios reported, citing two sources with knowledge of the matter.

The Reuters news agency could not immediately confirm the visit. The Pentagon and Israel’s embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for comment, and there was no immediate indication of what they discussed.

Trump endorsement

President Trump took to his social media platform Truth Social on Sunday to endorse Netanyahu in next week’s parliamentary election, the first vote since the Hamas-led October 7 attacks in 2023 and Israel’s genocidal campaign in Gaza began.

Trump praised the prime minister for being an ally of the US in its war on Iran. He added that Netanyahu had his “Complete and Total Endorsement”.

“BIBI NETANYAHU WILL NEVER LET YOU DOWN!” Trump wrote.

Netanyahu’s religious-nationalist coalition is projected to lose its governing majority, although the opposition may also struggle to form a government, opinion polls suggest.

US Vice President JD Vance, however, declined to endorse Netanyahu in an interview earlier on Monday, saying he was not getting involved in Israeli elections.

“I endorse American candidates, and that’s where I’m focused on is the midterms,” Vance, who travelled to Budapest and endorsed Viktor Orban in Hungarian elections earlier this year, said in an interview with digital media outlet 2WAY.



“I’m not anti-endorsing him, but I’m not pro-endorsing him; I’m not getting involved in Israeli elections,” Vance said.

World.title: Exiled critic of Rwandan president found beheaded in Uganda
World.content:
Ugandan police say a male body has been found in a village near Kampala, and his head has yet to be located.

An exiled vocal critic of the Rwandan government has been found decapitated near Kampala, south-central Uganda, according to a police spokesperson, in a case which remains under investigation.

Ugandan police said on Monday they were investigating the “murder of a male adult (around 50), whose head was cut off, and up to now, the head has not yet been recovered”, spokesperson Kituuma Rusoke told reporters, adding that the body had been identified by relatives as Robert Kabera.

The body was found in Luwala, a village near Kampala, and the killing likely took place late on October 16 or early on October 17, police added.

Robert Kabera, a former sergeant who fled Rwanda several years ago, was living in Uganda. The former soldier was not critical of the government during his time with the military, but grew increasingly opposed to Rwandan President Paul Kagame.

Kabera had a YouTube channel, “Major Robert TV”, with 144,000 subscribers. He featured a song praising opposition figure Victoire Ingabire, a rare voice of dissent in Rwanda who had been repeatedly imprisoned.

‘A witch-hunt’

In Uganda, “Robert had no issues with anyone”, his brother, Victor Agaba, told the AFP news agency.

“Our problem comes from home… The army created a criminal case against him. It was a witch-hunt,” he said.

Kabera was declared a fugitive after leaving Rwanda and accused of corrupting a minor, charges he denied.

Rwandan authorities have been accused of assassinating opponents of President Kagame, who has governed the country since coming to power in 2000. The Rwandan president took the reins in the aftermath of the 1994 genocide in which 800,000 people were killed, primarily from the minority Tutsi community.

Kabera is not the first opposition figure in exile to be assassinated.



In 2021, a former lieutenant in the Rwandan army, Revocat Karemangingo, was shot dead in Mozambique, where he was suspected of secretly supporting an opposition force.

Outspoken opponent Seif Bamporiki was shot dead in South Africa the same year, while a former Rwandan intelligence chief turned critic, Patrick Karegeya, was strangled in his South African hotel room in 2014.

Former general Faustin Kayumba Nyamwasa, who co-founded the Rwanda National Congress (RNC) opposition party with Karegeya and lives in exile, has survived several assassination attempts.

World.title: Mahmoud Khalil takes deportation fight to the US Supreme Court
World.content:
Lawyers for the former student leader seek to overturn an appeals court decision that would allow for his removal.

Share Mahmoud Khalil takes deportation fight to the US Supreme Court on social media

Pro-Palestine activist Mahmoud Khalil has petitioned the United States Supreme Court to review a court ruling that could pave the way for his re-arrest and deportation.

On Monday, Khalil’s lawyers filed an emergency application to the high court, seeking an immediate stay of a decision from Philadelphia’s 3rd Circuit Court of Appeals.

That court had ruled that federal law should have prohibited lower courts from ordering Khalil’s release from immigration detention in June 2025.

Instead, the appeals court said that Khalil’s detention should have been weighed first in an immigration court — a system overseen by the executive branch of the US government — and not in district court, which is part of the judicial branch.

In March 2025, Khalil became the first student protester known to be targeted for his pro-Palestinian views under the second administration of President Donald Trump.

A permanent US resident and former Columbia University graduate student, Khalil was arrested inside the student housing complex where he lived with his wife, a US citizen.

The push to deport Khalil has become a flashpoint in the debate over free speech on US campuses.

His petition to the Supreme Court could result in a major legal showdown that determines whether federal courts can intervene when noncitizens face retaliatory detention for speech protected under the First Amendment of the US Constitution.

Khalil’s lawyers have asked the Supreme Court to rule that noncitizens do indeed have the right to sue if immigration officials detain them as a reprisal for exercising free speech.



“If the Trump administration can punish someone for their pro-Palestine speech, this or any future administration can punish anyone for any speech,” Khalil said during a news conference on Monday.

Trump campaigned for re-election in 2024 in part on a pledge to crack down on the pro-Palestinian student protest movement, which had erupted in 2023.

Columbia University in New York became an epicentre for such activism. Khalil, who was born in a Palestinian refugee camp in Syria, had served as a spokesperson for the protest groups.

The Trump administration, however, has characterised pro-Palestinian activism as a threat to US foreign policy interests. It has argued it has the legal right to deport noncitizens who engage in such protests as a result.

After his arrest, Khalil was quickly moved to immigration detention centres in New Jersey, then Louisiana, where he remained in custody for more than three months.

Khalil faces deportation to Algeria or Syria if the 3rd Circuit Court’s decision holds.

In May, the 3rd Circuit narrowly voted six-to-five against reconsidering his case, but its decision will not go into effect until Khalil has exhausted his appeals.

He has fought his deportation both in the immigration court system and in the federal district court system, where he has filed a habeas corpus case. Both cases remain ongoing.

In April, the Board of Immigration Appeals denied his appeal in the immigration court system and issued a final order of removal in his case.

On Monday, faculty and staff at Columbia University held a silent vigil outside one of the school’s gates to protest what they described as “abducted students”, taken by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

Placards with portraits of Khalil and fellow student protester Mohsen Mahdawi, among others, were hoisted into the air. Demonstrators called for solidarity with the students facing deportation and pushed for Columbia University to reopen its gates to the public after their closure during the protest movement.

World.title: Colombia illegal gold mine collapse kills 14 people
World.content:
The collapse of an illegal gold mine in southwestern Colombia killed 14 people and injured seven others, local authorities said on Monday.

The accident took place in the rural Chambero sector of the Santa Barbara de Iscuande municipality, located in the department of Narino.

Search and rescue operations have concluded, Narino Governor Luis Alfonso Escobar said.

Jorge Tovar Castillo, a disaster response official in Narino, said that an additional 12 to 15 miners have been reported as missing following the accident.

He said that municipal authorities were handling the response but added that communication had been difficult.

Santa Barbara de Iscuande is surrounded by dense rainforest and can only be reached by boat or small aircraft.

In a message on X, Escobar said the gold mine was an “informal” mine.

Informal and unregulated mining is common in rural parts of Colombia, where operations often lack adequate safety infrastructure, leading to frequent fatal accidents.

“At this moment our priority is to save lives, accompany families and guarantee an opportune response to this painful tragedy,” Escobar wrote.

In August, 13 people died in a similar mining accident in the municipality of Policarpa, also in Narino.

World.title: Curfew imposed in parts of central Paris and other cities after rioting across France
World.content:
French authorities have imposed overnight curfews in parts of central Paris and other cities after a weekend of riots and looting across the country.

Police in Paris said a curfew would be in force between 23:00 local time (21:00 GMT) and 06:00 in Place de la RÃ©publique, where protesters had gathered over the weekend, and the Les Halles shopping area.

A ban on unauthorised gatherings has also been imposed in several other parts of the city centre.

Partial curfews variously restricting the movement of young people and gatherings were announced for cities including Marseille, Bordeaux, Nice and Lyon in the south as well as Lille and other towns in the north.

Earlier Interior Minister Laurent NuÃ±ez, who has been strongly criticised by opposition politicians over the preparedness for the disorder but whose resignation was rejected by President Emmanuel Macron, admitted police had "lost control" in some cities.

The protests began last month with students demanding better school conditions, but they have since escalated to take in a broader range of concerns, with numbers at demonstrations this weekend bolstered by trade unions and various protest groups.

More than 2,500 people have been arrested, officials said. One demonstrator's hand was blown off by a police crowd-control grenade, according to the AFP news agency. About 1,000 police officers were injured.

Following a crisis meeting on Monday, the prime minister said local mayors were being given the power to implement curfews "where they need", without specifying which cities where they would be enforced.

Prime Minister SÃ©bastien Lecornu, who did not rule out imposing a state of emergency in the country, said the government would also set aside money to help affected areas recover from the damage, and the funding would be recovered from those behind the violence.

"There will be a law that will be put in place to find ways of making sure that those who have damaged properties will have to pay," Lecornu said.

He also announced a partial unemployment fund for those who could not work as a result of the riots and looting.

World.title: Ukrainians dying because US restricting intelligence sharing, Zelensky adviser tells BBC
World.content:
Ukrainians have died because Kyiv is still not receiving reliable US warnings of incoming Russian attacks, according to a key adviser to President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Serhii "Flash" Beskrestnov told the BBC that lives had been lost because there had not been time to warn citizens about ballistic missile strikes, saying: "It's dangerous... I think it's really very bad... People [have] already died."

The adviser also said restrictions to Ukraine's use of the Starlink internet network were ongoing.

The White House said there had been no changes to intelligence sharing with Ukraine.

Ukraine first reported an interruption to US intelligence sharing last week, as a row with the Trump administrations over its controversial deal to import Russian oil sent relations to new lows.

Despite the denials from Washington, many in Kyiv suspect the issues are not a coincidence.

On Monday morning, Zelensky wrote on social media: "Overnight two ballistic missile attacks were reported on the capital, one without warning, the second with only minimal time to take shelter."

Hours earlier, an interview the president did with NBC was published, in which he said intelligence sharing had been restored after a three-day pause.

"We are very thankful for this," he said. "Only [the] United States has this unique intelligence to tell our side when Russia uses ballistic missiles."

But Beskrestnov told the BBC that American intelligence continued to be incomplete and inconsistent, and that the US had failed to provide a clear explanation for the issue.

"This looks very strange," he said. "Sometimes we receive this information before the attack, another time we [do] not."

He continued: "And for example, last night we received it, but... one minute before the attack."

However, he said other collaboration with US continues, adding: "Intelligence data keeps flowing, and the issue is solely with the air raid alert component."

Beskrestnov also said the US had given no clarity about who was responsible for the ongoing restrictions to the Starlink internet network and its military service Starshield, which Kyiv uses to provide connectivity for drones, helicopters and military communications.

Last week, Starshield restricted the speed at which mobile units could move while staying connected to the network to 100mph (160km/h).

This has limited Ukraine's ability to shoot down incoming drones or to launch mid-range drone attacks into Russian-occupied areas.

Starlink owner Elon Musk said last week that the US government ultimately controls access to Starshield, which was designed for the Pentagon, suggesting it may therefore be behind the restrictions. Trump has denied involvement.

Beskrestnov said he thought both issues occurring at the same time was "probably" a deliberate move to put pressure on Ukraine.

He told BBC News: "It's probably the United States trying to say [to] us, 'let's have the conversation, negotiation with Russia, you should find the compromise'."

Beskrestnov also said Ukraine had its own radar data to provide some limited warning of incoming attacks, but was urgently looking into using alternative communication systems.

He added: "Now we understand that something begins to happen with Starlink, and we're not sure what will be the next step.

"We understand that we should be prepared for some problems in future. And now we're thinking about an alternative for Starlink, not only for air defence, for communication between our forces, between our staff, for civilians also, because we don't know what we should expect in future regarding Starlink."

On Monday, when asked about intelligence sharing, Trump said: "We've given a lot to Ukraine. They've given us nothing."

World.title: Kenya cult leader who told parents to starve children guilty of 191 murders
World.content:
The leader of a Kenyan doomsday cult, Paul Mackenzie, has been found guilty of murdering 191 people, all but one of them children.

Mackenzie ordered members of his cult to starve their children to death so they could "meet Jesus".

His doctrine said that education was forbidden and modern medicine was "evil".

Twenty-eight other leaders of his cult were also convicted of murder. They had all pleaded not guilty, repeatedly insisting that nobody was forced to die.

Warning: This article contains details which some people might find distressing.

Delivering her eight-hour judgement in the port city of Mombasa, Justice Diana Mochache said Mackenzie's followers believed he was "Jesus's mouthpiece".

One of his co-accused said Mackenzie had told his followers that anyone who "resisted the directive to fast must be forced to go to heaven through kicks and blows".

Burials inside the forest where the cult was based were called "weddings". Those who died "were celebrated as having wedded with Jesus", the judge said.

One witness stated that a pregnant woman had been barred from nursing her new-born baby, who died 12 days later. "She was instructed to fast to death and follow her children," the witness said.

Mackenzie's former head of security, Enos Amanya Ngala, was initially accused but then entered a plea deal and became a witness for the prosecution.

Mackenzie and other leaders of the cult also face a raft of other legal cases, including for terrorism, radicalisation and denying education to children.

But this is the first time the pastor has faced a verdict on the most serious charges of murder. He is due to be sentenced on 6 November.

He was arrested in 2023, after the discovery of more than 400 bodies in shallow graves in Shakahola forest near the Kenyan coast, where Mackenzie had led his followers from across the country.

Stephen Mwiti, 48, said he lost all six of his children to the cult. His former wife was one of those convicted of murder alongside Mackenzie.

"I'm a happy man, that all persons have been convicted," he told the BBC outside court.

"All six of my children died in Shakahola forest," Mwiti said ahead of the verdict, visibly emotional holding a photograph of his family. "I only found and buried the remains of my son Samuel."

World.title: Tennis star Svitolina says emotional toll of Ukraine war led to Monfils separation
World.content:
Ukrainian tennis star Elina Svitolina has announced the end of her marriage with French former tennis player GaÃ«l Monfils, citing the emotional impact of the war in her country.

The 32-year-old, who is ranked number six in the world, wrote in a heartfelt post on Instagram about the effect the conflict and "what the war has done to me inside".

"This is the most difficult thing I have ever had to share," she wrote, saying "I need to find my way back to myself". Svitolina said she felt she could not do that within her marriage.

She said her husband Monfils, 40, "listened" and "respected what I need with a strength and grace I will never forget".

"Some battles happen deep inside you, and no amount of love from someone else can win them for you," the four-time Grand Slam semi-finalist wrote.

It was "the hardest thing I have ever had to tell the person I love", Svitolina said.

"Everyone knows how much Ukraine means to me," Svitolina, who grew up in Odesa, said.

Ukraine's Black Sea port city has been heavily bombed by Russia throughout the war.

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

"What you didn't see were the sleepless nights, the doubts, and the feeling of slowly losing myself."

The tennis power couple married in 2021 and have one child together - a four-year-old daughter called Skai.

Svitolina said her daughter "will always come first", adding "our marriage is ending, but our family is not".

Monfils, a former world number six, was expected to play the final tournament of his career at next month's Paris Masters in an emotional farewell.

However, the two-time Grand Slam semi-finalist's retirement was effectively confirmed last week when he appeared on the International Tennis Integrity Authority's list of retired players.

Once a player removes themselves from anti-doping protocols, they are not eligible to compete in professional tournaments.

Monfils, who won 13 titles on the ATP Tour, is preparing to start a new career in finance after joining a Swiss wealth management firm.

World.title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world
World.content:
El NiÃ±o has been strengthening for several months now and is already having a significant impact on global weather patterns.

Countries including Indonesia, India and the United States have been experiencing droughts, floods and heatwaves in line with projections about how extreme weather events will be supercharged by the phenomenon.

The World Meteorological Agency says the record-breaking El NiÃ±o will strengthen further and persist until at least 2027.

Here are five ways its impact is already being felt around the world.

World.title: Ex-OpenAI worker accused of planting device had Saudi support, says court filing
World.content:
A Saudi national charged with secretly planting a recording device in one of OpenAI's meeting rooms has been accused of having "considerable support" from the Saudi government, according to a court filing, external in California.

US prosecutors claimed Abdulrahman Alfozan, who worked for the AI firm, was in "frequent communication... with a member of the Saudi royal family", and say a member of the country's military paid for a one-way flight to Saudi Arabia for his wife and son after his arrest.

The 35-year-old engineer was on Monday deemed a flight risk and denied bail, pending trial.

The Saudi government did not immediately respond to BBC requests for comment.

Alfozan had worked at OpenAI for around a year before he allegedly made his attempt to plant an audio recorder.

The AI company discovered the device, which was plugged into the back of a TV in a conference meeting room and covered up with toilet paper, on 30 September.

A camera was placed in the room and on 5 October, Alfozan was filmed entering and appearing to look behind the television where the audio recorder had been inserted.

He was arrested by the FBI on 9 October and his contract with OpenAI was terminated.

The court filing claimed the suspect's alleged conduct could pose "a danger to the national security of the United States", because executives from the tech firm met with government officials in the room during the days the device was believed to have been installed.

It said Alfozan's arrest came three days before he was scheduled to fly from San Francisco to Riyadh on a one-way itinerary with his wife and son.

Following the arrest, the document claims the defendant's wife told FBI agents who interviewed her that "her US visa was expiring" and so she and her son were "permanently moving back to Saudi Arabia", and her husband intended to do the same.

On 10 October, the day after Alfozan was arrested, his wife and son flew from San Francisco to Doha, Qatar. They travelled on a one-way business class ticket booked and paid for by a Saudi military official.

"Ultimately, the defendant has little incentive to remain in the United States to see this case through," the prosecutors argued.

US district judge Alex Tse on Monday denied Alfozan's attorneys request for his release on bail, saying "there is a risk of non-appearance that is significant".

The FBI investigation is ongoing.

Alfozan was scheduled to âappear â in federal court in San Francisco later on Monday. If convicted, he faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison and a $250,000 (Â£188,000) fine.

World.title: Exiled critic of Rwandan president found beheaded
World.content:
A former Rwandan army sergeant major, who became an outspoken critic of President Paul Kagame, has been found beheaded in neighbouring Uganda.

Robert Kabera, 50, fled Rwanda after being accused of sexual assault, which he denied. He sought asylum in neighbouring Uganda, citing political persecution.

Ugandan police spokesperson Kituuma Rusoke on Monday said that Kabera's head had still not been recovered. His body was discovered by local residents on the outskirts of Kampala over the weekend.

The Rwandan government has not publicly commented on the killing. Several critics of Kagame have been killed, both in Rwanda and abroad.

His widow, Jeanne d'Arc Rwigema Uwizeye, told BBC Great Lakes in a written message that she now feared for her family's safety.

"It is scary. I feel crazy, the children and I don't have security," she said.

According to his family, Kabera had travelled to inspect a construction site about 45 km (30 miles) outside Kampala before his death.

Kabera built a public profile as a musician and YouTuber, attracting more than 144,000 subscribers to his channel, which featured over 800 videos, many criticising Kagame and his administration.

Reacting to news of his murder, exiled opposition group Rwanda National Congress (RNC) called for a thorough investigation and for those responsible to be brought to justice.

In a statement on X, the RNC said: "Today, his family is grieving, his voice is gone, and Rwandans in exile are confronting a terrifying question: where can we be safe?"

His death adds to concerns about the safety of Rwandan dissidents living in exile.

In 2014, Patrick Karegeya, a former Rwandan intelligence chief who helped set up the RNC, was found dead in his hotel room in Johannesburg, South Africa.

Karegeya fell out with President Paul Kagame and was arrested twice, serving an 18-month prison sentence for insubordination and desertion before fleeing to South Africa in 2007, where he became a vocal critic of the government.

Following his death, Kagame made remarks widely seen as a warning to other critics.

"Any person alive who may be plotting against Rwanda, whoever they are, will pay the price. Whoever it is, it is a matter of time," he said.

In 2019, South African authorities issued arrest warrants for two Rwandans accused of murdering Karegeya.

World.title: Houthi missile strike on Yemen camp kills 50 security recruits, local authorities say
World.content:
Monday's attack in Shabwa is one of the deadliest reported since the start of the escalation.

Shabwa province's media office said in a statement that ballistic missiles struck the Martyr Ahmed al-Sulaimani Training Centre, where recruits from several provinces were undergoing training to be members of the internal security forces. According to a preliminary assessment, 53 were killed and more than 200 injured, it added.

A video posted on social media appeared to show several bodies scattered across the ground.

Shabwa's deputy governor, Fahad al-Khalifi, told AFP news agency that hospitals in the province were overwhelmed and had been forced to transfer the most seriously wounded to neighbouring Hadramout and Aden, where the government is based. Some of them were in a critical condition, he said.

Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani said the attack constituted a war crime because the internal security forces training centre was not a military target.

He also accused the Houthis of "attempting to fabricate a false media victory, boost the morale of its collapsing elements, and cover up the defeats and setbacks it is suffering across various combat axes".

The Houthis' military spokesman, Yahya Sarea, said in a statement that the missiles targeted a gathering of "Saudi enemy" forces at al-Alam camp, which he said was run by Saudi officers.

There was no immediate comment from Saudi authorities.

In a separate development, Houthi-run media reported that a Saudi air strike on a home in the Sahar district of the Houthi-controlled northern province of Saada on Sunday killed at least 10 people and injured 23 others, many of them women and children.

According to the Houthi-run health ministry in north-western Yemen, a total of 141 people had been killed in Saudi strikes over the past seven weeks.

The government's health ministry, meanwhile, said last week that at least 1,282 people had been killed in the conflict across Yemen since 6 August.

In Saudi Arabia, at least 19 people have been killed in Houthi attacks targeting the kingdom's airports since the beginning of October.

Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from the capital, Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule.

A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.

The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they call a Saudi blockade of their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom.

World.title: Uba Sani resolves 10-year land dispute, offers 704 households plots, farmlands, Free Fertiliser
World.content:
Governor Uba Sani has vowed that no community will be rendered homeless in Kaduna State because his administration believes in human dignity and the sanctity of life.

The governor made the promise while distributing land titles to communities in Igabi local government, whose lands have been a subject of dispute between the military and the inhabitants.

Comprising 704 houses, the benefitting communities include Unguwan Malam Auta, Unguwan Alhassan and Unguwan Lauya as well as Unguwan Aboki, Unguwan Danjuma, Unguwan Musa and Unguwan Yohana.

The alleged land seizure took place before the coming of the present administration and when he came on board, Governor Uba Sani tried to resolve the matter amicably to no avail.

Although the matter is still in court, he directed the Director General of Kaduna State Geographic Information Service(KADGIS), Dr Bashir Ibrahim Garba, to give plots of land to the affected communities, including farmlands.

Speaking at the Birnin Yero Tsohuwa Primary School on Sunday, the Governor disclosed that there were over 5,000 people living within the affected communities and more than 2,000 of them had been displaced because of the land dispute.

‘’Today, we gathered here not only to give free plots of land to all the members of the communities and the households, we also here to ensure that we look at other problems.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

‘’Apart from giving you plots of land, ensuring that all of you have decent shelter is important to our administration because we believe in the human dignity. We also gave each one of you a farmland as a means of livelihood because 90% of you are farmers,’’ he added.

Governor Uba Sani also promised the communities five trucks of free fertiliser, in addition to extending a special intervention to enable them stand on their feet.

‘’I have directed the Secretary to Kaduna State Government, together with the Commissioner of Finance and Commissioner of Planning and Budget, to sit down with your leaders so as to support you with social intervention.

‘’We believe all the people here, particularly those that are vulnerable, deserve a level of compensation from our government. So, we are going to give you social intervention, so that some of you that have lost their livelihoods, will quickly go back to their activities, particularly those involved in small businesses,’’ he promised.

He assured that Kaduna State Government will not abandon any community, adding that ‘’our heart bleeds when we saw the level of the pain and what happened to you.’’

Uba Sani commended the communities for living in peace irrespective of their ethno-religious differences and party affiliations.

‘’I’ve seen the level of togetherness between the Muslims and Christians within these communities. You work together as one family. When the incident happened, I was informed you treated each other as one family,’’ he added.

In his welcome remarks, the Director General of KADGIS, Dr Bashir Ibrahim Garba, disclosed that the Governor Uba Sani administration has resolved 5,285 inherited land cases.

‘’The Governor has also supported more than 2,000 communities that were displaced by either disputes or land issues,’’ he added.

The DG recalled that the communities that were being compensated, were displaced by the military, adding that ‘’it is a 10-year dispute that has been lingering in court and past governments couldn’t resolve the matter.’’

Dr Garba commended the Governor for not only resolving the land matter but for also giving the communities farmlands that will sustain them because majority are farmers.

World.title: Rivers Assembly reinstates three pro-Fubara lawmakers
World.content:
The Rivers State House of Assembly has reversed its earlier decision declaring the seats of three lawmakers loyal to Governor Siminalayi Fubara vacant.

The Assembly took the decision a day after FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike, led lawmakers and the state’s 23 local government chairpersons to a reconciliation meeting with the governor in Port Harcourt.

The lawmakers are Timothy Oruibienimigha, representing Opobo/Nkoro Constituency; Victor Jumbo, representing Bonny Constituency; and Sokari Goodboy Sokari, representing Ahoada West Constituency.

The decision was “taken on Monday during the 68th legislative sitting of the fourth session of the 10th Assembly, following separate letters of appeal submitted by the three lawmakers to the Speaker of the Assembly, Martin Amaewhule.”

Martins Wachukwu, a media aide to the speaker, announced the development in a statement posted on Facebook on Monday.

According to the statement, the lawmakers apologised to the House for failing to resume legislative duties after their suspension was lifted in December 2023.

They attributed their continued absence to their alleged failure to receive official correspondence informing them that the suspension had been lifted following a presidential intervention, the statement said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The lawmakers were among four members suspended on 30 October 2023 amid the political crisis that divided the assembly into factions loyal to Mr Wike and Mr Fubara.

The statement said in Monday’s plenary, lawmakers debated the appeals and supported the request to rescind the earlier resolution declaring the seats vacant.

Mr Amaewhule said, “Investigations indicated that the three lawmakers might not have received the correspondence notifying them of the lifting of their suspension,” the statement added.

The lawmakers subsequently voted in favour of reversing the declaration, allowing their colleagues to return to the Assembly, according to the statement.

The latest decision comes amid renewed efforts to reconcile Mr Wike and Mr Fubara after more than three years of political hostilities that have repeatedly disrupted governance in Rivers State.

Background

The political crisis in Rivers State began in 2023, months after Governor Fubara succeeded Mr Wike as governor. The disagreement between the former allies escalated into a struggle for control of the state’s political structures, including the House of Assembly.

In October 2023, amid an impeachment attempt against Mr Fubara by lawmakers loyal to Mr Wike, the Assembly split into two factions. An overwhelming majority of 27 lawmakers backed Mr Wike, while four supported the governor.

Edison Ehie, who led the four-member faction loyal to Mr Fubara, obtained a court order allowing the group to continue legislative proceedings and subsequently emerged as speaker of the factional Assembly.

Mr Ehie resigned as speaker and as a member of the Assembly following a peace deal brokered by President Bola Tinubu in December 2023. Mr Fubara later appointed him chief of staff.

In May 2024, Mr Jumbo emerged as speaker of the pro-Fubara faction after Mr Ehie’s departure. The faction continued to hold sittings and pass legislation, including considering budget proposals and screening commissioner nominees, while the Amaewhule-led faction also conducted legislative business.

The legal battle over the Assembly’s leadership later shifted in favour of the Wike-backed lawmakers. In July 2024, the Court of Appeal reinstated the 27 lawmakers and recognised Martin Amaewhule as speaker. The Supreme Court subsequently ruled in February 2025 in favour of the Amaewhule-led Assembly, restoring the lawmakers’ status as legitimate members of the legislature. The ruling also affected the legal standing of decisions taken by the rival faction.

In October 2024, the Amaewhule-led Assembly declared the seats of the three lawmakers now seeking reinstatement vacant, citing their continued absence from legislative sittings. The House said it had notified the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to conduct elections to fill the vacancies.

Tinubu declares state of emergency

The crisis escalated in March 2025 when Mr Tinubu declared a state of emergency in Rivers State, suspending Mr Fubara, his deputy, Ngozi Odu, and members of the state Assembly for six months. The president appointed retired Vice Admiral Ibok-Ete Ibas as sole administrator of the state.

Mr Tinubu cited the breakdown of governance, the prolonged dispute between the executive and legislature, and security concerns in announcing the measure.

The emergency rule ended in September 2025, allowing Mr Fubara and the other suspended elected officials to return to their positions.

However, the political truce did not permanently resolve the dispute. Renewed reconciliation efforts followed, including further interventions by Mr Tinubu. In February 2026, the Assembly withdrew its impeachment move against the governor and his deputy amid fresh efforts to ease tensions.

The latest meeting between Mr Wike, the lawmakers, the 23 local government chairpersons and Mr Fubara, followed by Monday’s reversal of the decision declaring the three lawmakers’ seats vacant, could signal progress in the latest reconciliation effort.

World.title: Police arrest man over alleged plot to kidnap 16-year-old girlfriend for N50m ransom
World.content:
The police in Delta State have arrested a 23-year-old man, Terry Ogbonna, over an alleged plot with his friends to kidnap his 16-year-old girlfriend and demand a N50 million ransom from her mother.

The police spokesperson in the state, Bright Edafe, a superintendent of police, disclosed the incident in a video posted on X on Saturday.

According to Mr Edafe, the incident initially sparked panic among residents of the estate where the girl’s parents live, as people reportedly rushed around trying to rescue her.

However, police investigations allegedly revealed that the girl’s boyfriend was involved in the incident.

The girl said she was unaware that her boyfriend intended to kidnap her for ransom, while Mr Ogbonna told the police they had initially agreed to the plan but later changed their minds. He said his friends, however, proceeded with the arrangement after seeing the girl.

Girl recounts alleged kidnapping

During her interview with the police, the girl identified Mr Ogbonna as her boyfriend. “He’s my boyfriend,” she told the police.

She said he came to the estate and took her to his house.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The girl also admitted that her boyfriend had previously raised the idea of faking her kidnapping to obtain money from her mother.

“He brought it up, and I said no.”

She said she later discovered a ransom demand had been sent to her mother after one of her boyfriend’s friends took her phone and she checked her chats.

According to her, the message demanded N50,000 from her mother for her feeding.

“After sometime, he came back, and I showed him the text message and asked, ‘What is the meaning of this?’”

When the police asked at what point the alleged kidnappers demanded N50 million, the girl said she was taken to a riverside and threatened.

“They carried me to the riverside. I was close to the river, and my legs were touching water. They threatened to throw me into the river if my mother does not pay N50 million,” she said.

Police say another resident implicated

Mr Edafe said the suspects allegedly attempted to make another resident of the estate, identified as Theophilus, appear to be the mastermind of the kidnapping.

Theophilus was a co-tenant in the estate where the girl’s parents live.

“This suspect knew the history of Mr Theophilus and the mother, and they set up Mr Theophilus to make it look like Mr Theophilus is the mastermind of the kidnapping. Mr Theophilus was arrested for two days before the truth eventually emerged,” the police spokesperson said.

Suspect admits discussing kidnapping plan

During his interview with the police, Mr Ogbonna said he and his friend, Lucky, planned the kidnapping.

When asked how Lucky knew that Mr Theophilus lived in the same estate and was having issues with the girl’s mother, Mr Ogbonna replied: “I told him about it.”

He also told the police that the girl stayed in his house for two days.

Mr Ogbonna said he had finished secondary school. He said his mother lived in the village, while his father lived in Asaba in Delta State.

What Nigerian law says about sex with a minor

The case also raises legal questions about Mr Ogbonna’s admission that he had sexual relations with the girl, who is 16.

During the police interview, Mr Ogbonna said he began having sex with his girlfriend three weeks after they started dating “Three months ago”.

He also told the police he was unaware that having sex with someone under 18 was an offence.

Under Section 31 of Nigeria’s Child Rights Act, 2003, sexual intercourse with a child is an offence classified as rape, punishable by life imprisonment upon conviction. The law provides that a child’s consent and the accused person’s belief that the child was 18 or older do not, by themselves, provide a defence to a charge under that section.

If prosecuted and convicted under an applicable provision criminalising sexual intercourse with a child, Mr Ogbonna could face a lengthy prison sentence, potentially life imprisonment under the relevant child-rights provision.

The alleged kidnapping and ransom demand expose the suspects to separate criminal charges, depending on the evidence and the offences established by the police.

Mr Ogbonna’s admission during a police interview does not amount to a court conviction. The allegations must be tested in court, where the prosecution would be required to prove the relevant offences beyond reasonable doubt.

World.title: Sanwo-Olu asks LAWMA boss to resign over waste crisis – Report
World.content:
Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu has reportedly asked the Managing Director of the Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA), Muyiwa Gbadegesin, to resign over the persistent heaps of refuse across the state.

According to Punch Newspaper, an unnamed source within the agency said the governor was unhappy with Mr Gbadegesin’s handling of the crisis and had asked him to step down.

The source noted that the governor became dissatisfied after visiting the Olusosun dumpsite in Ojota about a month ago and directing that urgent action be taken to improve waste management.

“The governor was upset when he observed that the situation had not improved despite his clear directive. So, over the weekend, he asked him to resign, although he is begging and has reached out to some prominent Lagosians to beg on his behalf,” Punch quoted the source as saying.

It is not clear when Mr Gbadegesin succeeded in persuading the governor to rescind his decision.

PREMIUM TIMES contacted the Lagos State Commissioner for Information, Gbenga Omotosho, via text messages seeking the government’s reaction to the report, but he had not responded as of the time of filing this report.

The reported move comes after months of complaints from residents about refuse piling up on roads, streets and drainage channels in parts of Lagos, including Mushin, Egbeda, Surulere, Ajegunle, Ikorodu, Ojo, Obalende, Apapa and Mile 2.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In September, Mr Sanwo-Olu declared a state of emergency on waste collection after inspecting the Olusosun dumpsite. During the visit, he met with waste management stakeholders alongside his deputy, Obafemi Hamzat, to discuss measures to improve collection and disposal across the state.

The governor blamed part of the problem on the failure of Private Sector Participation (PSP) operators to meet their obligations in the preceding weeks.

He also said ongoing waste compaction at the Olusosun and Solous 3 dumpsites would increase their capacity to receive municipal waste. Recent fires at the facilities had disrupted operations, he added.

The crisis has also prompted action against private waste collectors. In October, LAWMA withdrew the operating licences of six PSP operators over concerns about their performance.

Despite the interventions, Mr Gbadegesin said the agency was continuing clearance operations in affected communities.

In a post on his X account on Saturday, he said 11 of the 15 routes covered by the week’s programme had received field updates.

He reported that Mile 2 had been cleared, while three additional trucks had been deployed to Doyin-Orile and its environs. Daily collection was also continuing on Ijesha Road and in Itire-Ikate, while Bucknor-Ijegun had been cleared and placed on a three-times-weekly collection schedule.

According to him, LAWMA had taken over interim collection in Okeira and Oluodo following the termination of their PSP operators’ contracts. Collection was continuing in Ogolonto and Igbokusu, while Obalende had been cleared and provided with a waste bin.

Clearance was ongoing in Iraye, but the agency was still awaiting field updates from Apapa, Abesan Estate, Idimu-Ejigbo Road and the Isheri-Igando corridor.

“The objective is to progress from clearance to sustained collection and prevention of recurrence, not simply remove visible waste,” Mr Gbadegesin wrote.

Mr Gbadegesin was reappointed as LAWMA managing director after Mr Sanwo-Olu’s re-election.

World.title: Two casualties as tanker catches fire under Otedola Bridge in Lagos
World.content:
Two casualties were recorded on Monday after a diesel-laden tanker reportedly fell from Otedola Bridge and caught fire underneath it, inward Berger, Lagos State.

The Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA) announced the incident in a post on X at about 5:10 p.m., saying firefighters were battling the blaze while emergency responders attended to the victims.

The agency said arrangements were being made to take the victims to hospital, while its personnel managed traffic around the scene.

LASTMA advised motorists approaching the area to drive cautiously and obey traffic officials’ instructions as emergency operations continued.

In a separate statement on Facebook, the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service said the 33,000-litre tanker was carrying petroleum products from a depot when it fell between the inward and outward sections of the bridge.

The service said it received a distress call at 4:09 p.m. and sent firefighters from its Alausa and Ikeja stations. They arrived at 4:16 p.m. and began putting out the fire.

The fire was later extinguished, although firefighters remained at the scene to deal with residual hotspots and prevent it from reigniting, the service said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The incident recalls a gas truck explosion near Otedola Bridge on 11 March 2025, which destroyed buildings and vehicles.

The National Emergency Management Agency reported that one person died, four others were injured and 14 vehicles were burnt in that incident.

The fire service stated that it would provide further details about the cause of Monday’s incident, casualties and property damage when the information had been verified.

Its Controller-General, Margaret Abimbola Adeseye, urged motorists to exercise caution around emergency scenes and obey safety instructions from responders.

World.title: Court dismisses El-Rufai’s N120 million rights suit against SSS, EFCC, ICPC, AGF
World.content:
The FCT High Court in Maitama, Abuja, on Monday, dismissed former Kaduna State Governor Nasir El-Rufai’s N120 million fundamental rights enforcement suit, which he instituted following an attempt to arrest him by security operatives at the airport in Abuja earlier in the year.

Mr El-Rufai, who has been detained since February, sued the State Security Service (SSS), the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) and the Attorney-General of the Federation.

Mr El-Rufai, who sought a total of N120 million in damages against the security agencies, alleged that they violated his rights by seizing his passport and attempting to arrest him at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport in Abuja upon his arrival in the country in February.

Judge Sylvanus Oriji said the case lacked merit and awarded N200,000 in costs against Mr El-Rufai in favour of each of the four respondents. The fines totalled N800,000.

Mr Oriji held that there was nothing wrong with the attempt by SSS operatives to arrest him at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport in Abuja.

He ruled that SSS, a secret police organisation, acted within its powers “to place persons of interest on its watchlist and arrest them where necessary.”

He added that the seizure of Mr El-Rufai’s passport by SSS operatives at the airport was lawful and within the agency’s powers.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The judge threw out Mr El-Rufai’s argument that the attempted arrest was unlawful because there was no warrant.

He added that the letters of invitation issued by the EFCC and ICPC were not a violation of Mr El-Rufai’s human rights.

According to the judge, the agencies’ invitations fell within their jurisdiction to ensure Mr El-Rufai provided information regarding his ongoing interrogation.

The judge ruled that Mr El-Rufai cannot use the court “to prevent the agencies from performing their statutory duties.”

He therefore dismissed the suit for lacking merit.

Background

PREMIUM TIMES reported that SSS operatives attempted to arrest Mr El-Rufai on 12 February, following his arrival from Cairo, Egypt.

While the arrest was unsuccessful, the security operatives seized the former governor’s passport.

The following day, Mr El-Rufai alleged during a live interview on ‘Prime Time’, an Arise Television programme, that the National Security Adviser (NSA), Nuhu Ribadu, was behind the alleged attempt to arrest him at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja.

He said he knew Mr Ribadu ordered his arrest from listening to a wire-tapped phone call made by Mr Ribadu instructing security operatives to carry out his arrest.

Ubong Akpan, one of Mr El-Rufai’s lawyers, condemned the dramatic incident at the Abuja airport at the time, linking the attempted arrest to a letter of invitation from the EFCC.

He added that his law firm wrote to the agency, notifying it that Mr El-Rufai would honour its invitation on 16 February.

The former governor was later detained after honoring the invitation. He was released two days after, and subsequently re-arrested by SSS operatives who handed him over to the ICPC.

He has since been in the custody of the ICPC which is prosecuting the former governor in two separate cases in Kaduna on money laundering and abuse of office charges stemming from his activities as the Kaduna State governor.

The ICPC announced a plan in March to prosecute five security officials for allegedly receiving bribes to grant access to Mr El-Rufai’s supporters to restricted areas of the Abuja airport when he arrived in Nigeria in February.

On 23 April, SSS arraigned Mr El-Rufai before the Federal High Court in Abuja, over his claim of wiretapping Mr El-Rufai’s phone call.

String of legal battles

Monday’s judgement came about 11 days after Judge Joyce Abdulmalik of the Federal High Court, Abuja, dismissed another fundamental rights suit Mr El-Rufai filed, in which he had sought to restrain the EFCC, ICPC, the SSS and the AGF from freezing his bank accounts or seizing his properties. Ms Abdulmalik threw out the case on 8 October.

Mr El-Rufai, who has been detained by the ICPC since February based on a court order issued in an ongoing corruption proceeding instituted by the ICPC against him in Kaduna, still has at least two other fundamental human rights cases in court.

Mr El-Rufai filed a suit in February seeking N1 billion in damages against the ICPC and other defendants for alleged violations of his rights during the search conducted at his Abuja residence on 19 February.

Mr El-Rufai filed the N1 billion fundamental rights enforcement suit on 20 February following his detention and the search of his Abuja home.

He asked the court to declare that the search warrant issued on 4 February by the FCT chief magistrate, which authorised the search and seizure at his residence, was invalid, null, and void.

He argued the search violated his rights to dignity, personal liberty, fair hearing, and privacy, and sought an injunction to restrain the respondents from using any seized evidence.

The ICPC opposed the suit, stating in a counter-affidavit that it acted on a petition against El-Rufai and under statutory powers to investigate, arrest, and prosecute offenders.

The police added that the search was conducted under a warrant issued by a competent court.

In August, he filed a N10 billion suit against the ICPC for allegedly stopping him from seeing his wife, Aichatou Asabe, and his son, Abba El-Rufai, while they were in custody.

The ICPC is currently prosecuting him in two separate corruption cases before two courts in Kaduna.

The SSS is also prosecuting him before the Federal High Court in Abuja on phone tapping charges.

World.title: Kwam 1 hands daughter to Lagos deputy governor for Assembly ambition (VIDEO)
World.content:
Fuji musician Wasiu “Kwam 1” Ayinde has sought the support of Lagos State Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat for his daughter, Damilola Ayinde-Marshall, who hopes to secure a seat in the state House of Assembly in 2027.

Damilola is contesting for Surulere Constituency II under the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the forthcoming general elections.

Kwam 1 made the appeal when Mr Hamzat, the APC’s governorship candidate in the state, attended a programme organised by the Muhtadeen Islamic Foundation (MIFO) on Sunday.

MIFO is a group of young-at-heart Muslims committed to promoting Islam as a religion of peace and correcting misconceptions about the faith.

In a video posted on his Instagram page that gained traction online on Monday, Kwam 1 handed his daughter over to the deputy governor, apparently seeking his backing for her political ambition.

Mr Hamzat laughed and gestured toward Damilola’s seat. The lawyer, meanwhile, appeared amused by her father’s public show of support.

“We’ll dance”

Welcoming Mr Hamzat, the 69-year-old thanked him for the honour and expressed confidence that he would win the state’s forthcoming governorship election.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The musician also predicted that President Bola Tinubu would secure a second term in office.

He said members of MIFO and state residents, alongside Nigerians worldwide, would celebrate the victories of both Mr Hamzat and Mr Tinubu.

“Obafemi Hamzat, our deputy governor today and the incoming governor, by January and February, we will dance a lot of victory dances. We will dance over the deputy governor who will become governor.

“We will dance over Nigeria and the Yoruba people across the world, and over our father, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, who will serve a second term, so that there can be peace and prosperity for this country. That is how it will be, by God’s grace”, he said.

Why Hamzat as governor?

Additionally, Kwam 1 said Mr Hamzat was reaping the benefits of his service as a member of former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola’s entourage, as well as his contributions to MIFO.

He added that MIFO members were delighted to welcome Mr Hamzat, noting that the forum had laid the groundwork for his governorship ambition 13 years ago.

“We have been struggling for him because I remember the covenant we made with God. Openly, 13 years ago, when we were on this same journey, everyone in this environment will bear me witness.

“Our excellency (Babatunde Fashola) at that time, who is a member of MIFO and has stood firm since we established MIFO, made us proud with his presence and everything he did to keep MIFO standing, and we supported him”, he added.

He said Mr Hamzat threw his weight behind Mr Fashola when the latter expressed his intention to become governor, doing everything within his power to support his bid.

“When he expressed interest in contesting for governor, we prayed for him. He came to this area and made several promises, and among his entourage that year was Dr Obafemi Hamzat. I stood beside Hamzat while our excellency, Babatunde Fashola, stood at the front.

“Because of Hamzat’s efforts that day to ensure Fashola emerged as governor, I held Hamzat’s hand and told him that he would also become governor of Lagos State. Since then, we have been on the journey toward his becoming governor.”

World.title: Nigerian Secondary School Flag Football League kicks off Season 5 with ₦3.7m prize pool
World.content:
The Nigerian Secondary School Flag Football League (NSSFFL) will begin its fifth season on Tuesday, with organisers promising cash rewards for top-performing schools and renewed efforts to expand opportunities for young athletes.

Nancy Damhindi, vice president of the Nigerian American Football Association (NAFA), said the competition has become a structured school-sports programme that connects students, schools, coaches, and communities through flag football.

Speaking at a press conference in Lagos on Monday, Ms Damhindi said the new season would build on the league’s progress while strengthening grassroots development and educational opportunities for student-athletes.

The preliminary competitions will lead to Aketi Bowl IV, the national championship scheduled for 17–20 November in Abuja.

League coordinator Oluwatobi Abe said the participating locations were selected following preseason assessments and development activities designed to determine which areas were ready to host competitive tournaments.

The locations announced for the preliminaries are Oyo, Akwa Ibom, Lagos, Ogun, Ondo, Benue, Cross River, Bayelsa, and Kwara states, along with the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

Mr Abe, popularly known as Coach Tobi, said NAFA had conducted activation and reinforcement exercises in areas where the sport had previously been introduced.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We were very intentional as to our developmental pathway,” he said, adding that the association used its assessments to select locations ready for the competitions.

National champions to receive ₦1 million

Mr Abe said the first-placed teams in the boys’ and girls’ divisions at the national championship would each receive ₦1 million.

The runners-up in both divisions will receive ₦500,000 each, while the third-placed teams will get ₦350,000 each, bringing the total prize money to ₦3.7 million.

He clarified that no prize money would be awarded at the state-level preliminaries, where the emphasis would remain on participation and identifying schools to represent their respective locations at the national tournament.

Mr Abe said the clarification followed questions about prize money during the previous season’s qualifiers.

The preliminary competitions are scheduled to run from 20 to 30 October, beginning in Oyo State at Bishop Phillips Academy, Iwo Road.

Other venues include Community Secondary Commercial School in Akwa Ibom; Government Secondary School, Garki, in the FCT; CMS Grammar School, Bariga, in Lagos; and St Peter’s Secondary School, Akure, in Ondo State.

Kwara will host its competition at Queen Elizabeth Secondary School, Ilorin, on 26 October, followed by Ogun on 27 October at St Peter’s Unity College, Abeokuta. Benue’s games are scheduled for 28 October at Goldman Secondary School, Gboko, while Bayelsa will conclude the preliminary schedule on 30 October at Bellary International Schools, Yenagoa. Cross River will also host its competition during the schedule.

Scholarships and international opportunities

Beyond the competition, NAFA seeks to create educational and international opportunities for participating students.

Mr Abe said Unique Open University has supported the league since its pilot season in Lagos in 2022, offering scholarships to outstanding teams.

Initially, scholarships were available to the first-, second- and third-placed teams in both divisions. From the second season, however, the awards were limited to the national champions in the boys’ and girls’ categories.

He said recipients could, with their parents, decide whether to study at the sponsoring institution or pursue other educational plans.

Mr Abe cited Divine Ayogu, a former Baptist Academy player who participated in the league’s pilot season and later represented Nigeria at the national team level, as an example of the opportunities the sport could provide.

He said a partnership with Nigerian American Football Outreach helped Ayogu secure a scholarship in the United States.

NAFA is also developing an under-13 programme to introduce younger children to the sport through the storybook Jojo and the Winning Play, alongside plans for a collegiate league.

Ms Damhindi said flag football’s scheduled debut at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games could offer another pathway for Nigerian athletes, though qualification would depend on the applicable process.

Schools urged to sustain participation

Ms Damhindi acknowledged the Nigerian School Sport Federation (NSSF) as a key partner in organising the competition and connecting it to the country’s school-sports system.

She also highlighted support from Browns Nigeria and NFL FLAG through the One Ball, One Flag, One Future initiative, which provides about 2,000 American footballs and 5,000 flag football kits.

During the question-and-answer session, Segun Omodunni, representing the NSSF president, said school principals were required to confirm students’ enrolment before they could represent their schools, with state-level officials also involved in the verification process.

The organisers said their immediate priority was to deliver credible competitions and give students opportunities to develop their skills, pursue education, and progress toward national and international competition.

World.title: PSN seeks tougher penalties for drug fakers, proposes N25m fine, 20-year jail term
World.content:
Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria, PSN

By Chioma Obinna

The Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) on Monday called for tougher punishment for manufacturers and distributors of fake drugs, proposing a minimum fine of N25 million and prison terms of between five and 20 years for offenders to deter offenders and protect public health.

Addressing a press conference ahead of the society’s 99th Annual National Conference, the PSN President, Pharm. Ayuba Tanko Ibrahim, urged the National Assembly to expedite work on the amendment of the Fake Drug Act.

Ibrahim said the existing penalties, including fines as low as N5,000 and N10,000 in some cases, were inadequate to discourage offenders operating in the lucrative counterfeit drug business.

“How can you say somebody is caught faking drugs and pays a fine of N5,000 or N10,000? So it encourages them,” he said.

The PSN president explained that the proposed amendment would prescribe a fine of not less than N25 million, imprisonment for a term of not less than five years and up to 20 years, or both, as well as forfeiture of assets where applicable, depending on the nature of the offence.

He said the society had presented its position at a recent public hearing at the Senate, expressing hope that lawmakers would accelerate the legislative process to ensure the proposed changes became law.

According to him, the profitability of counterfeit medicines makes stronger sanctions necessary, even as regulatory agencies intensify enforcement operations.

“Drug faking has come to stay. Nobody should assume that it can be eliminated because it’s a very lucrative business. So, as they are doing, we should be thinking of how to checkmate them,” Ibrahim said.

He urged the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC), the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN) and the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare to sustain efforts to identify, arrest and prosecute those involved in the trade.

Beyond tougher punishment, Ibrahim called on federal and state governments to fully implement the National Drug Distribution Guidelines (NDDG), approved in 2015, to improve the regulation of medicine distribution and curb the circulation of fake and substandard products.

The guidelines provide for the relocation of major open drug markets to Coordinated Wholesale Centres (CWCs), where medicine distribution can be better monitored.

The PSN identified the major open drug markets in Idumota, Lagos; Head Bridge, Onitsha, Anambra State; Sabon Gari, Kano; and Ariaria, Aba, Abia State, as requiring sustained government attention under the reform.

Ibrahim said the CWC initiative had recorded progress in Kano, while projects in Lagos and Anambra required continued attention to ensure their completion and effective operation.

He added that Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, had promised support for the initiative in the state.

He urged the Federal Government to collaborate with the affected state governments to remove administrative and other obstacles delaying the establishment and operation of the centres.

According to him, effective implementation of the guidelines, alongside stronger penalties, would help strengthen the medicine supply chain and improve patient safety.

The PSN president also warned against placing the responsibility for identifying fake medicines on patients, insisting that pharmacists and other qualified professionals had a critical role to play in protecting consumers.

He said manufacturers conducted quality-control checks before releasing medicines to the market, while some companies had introduced product-verification systems to help detect suspected counterfeits.

“It is not the job of a patient to check or confirm whether a drug is fake or not. The pharmacist that showed the drug to him should be able to check if the drug is fake or not,” he said.

Ibrahim advised Nigerians to purchase medicines from registered pharmacies rather than unregulated outlets, warning that unauthorised sales of prescription medicines, including antibiotics, could expose consumers to serious health risks.

He stressed the need for public education on the safe purchase and use of medicines, noting that patent medicine vendors were subject to restrictions on the products they could legally sell.

On the rising cost of medicines, the PSN president said government incentives for pharmaceutical manufacturers would have limited impact unless authorities addressed the broader costs of local production.

He explained that reductions in import tariffs alone might not translate into cheaper medicines if manufacturers continued to face high diesel prices, electricity costs and transportation expenses.

“Unless the government takes a holistic view of the drivers of the prices of pharmaceuticals, we are not going to see any appreciable decrease in the cost of drugs,” he said.

Ibrahim urged the government to consult pharmaceutical manufacturers and their industry associations before introducing policies intended to reduce medicine prices, arguing that manufacturers could provide practical insights into the factors driving production costs.

He also called for stronger collaboration between government agencies responsible for natural-product research and pharmaceutical manufacturers to develop promising research findings into medicines for local use.

The PSN president warned that the high cost of medicines was pushing some Nigerians away from conventional healthcare towards traditional remedies, underscoring the need to improve access to affordable and quality-assured medicines.

Meanwhile, PSN National Secretary, Pharm. Gafar Madehein, cautioned Nigerians against assuming that herbal products were safe simply because they carried NAFDAC registration numbers.

He explained that a registration number issued for listing purposes did not necessarily mean that a product had undergone clinical trials demonstrating its safety and efficacy.

Madehein also warned that combining herbal remedies with conventional medicines could trigger harmful interactions, urging consumers to seek professional advice before using them together.

The pharmacists spoke ahead of the PSN’s 99th Annual National Conference, scheduled to hold in Awka, Anambra State, from November 1 to 6, 2026, under the theme, “One Health, One Pharmacy: Bridging Knowledge, Practice and Policy for National Impact.”

The conference is expected to bring together pharmacists, policymakers, regulators, researchers and other healthcare professionals to discuss pharmacy practice, clinical collaboration, education, research and pharmaceutical policy.

World.title: Reps back Tinubu, Dangote, NMDPRA, demand pipeline funding
World.content:
…Open probes into NIPCO gas licences,

NNPCL executive

By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja

The House of Representatives Committee on Petroleum Resources (Downstream) has passed votes of confidence on President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) and industrialist Aliko Dangote, declaring that Nigeria’s drive towards energy security is gaining momentum.

The committee, however, called on the Federal Government to increase funding for pipeline surveillance, enforce domestic crude supply obligations and strengthen legislation to protect local refineries from supply disruptions and unfair competition.

Chairman of the committee, Ikenga Imo Ugochinyere, announced the votes of confidence on Monday in Abuja at the technical briefing marking the end of Downstream Week 2026.

He said the committee’s assessment of developments in the downstream petroleum sector showed improvements in domestic refining, fuel supply and pipeline security, while stressing the need for sustained government support to consolidate the gains.

Ugochinyere commended the NMDPRA Chief Executive, Rabiu Abdullahi Umar, and the authority’s executive directors for what he described as a job well done, saying the regulator had “brought stability where there was uncertainty”.

According to figures presented at the briefing, domestic refineries now contribute more than 75 per cent of national petrol supply, while the country has recorded no supply shortfalls and maintained more than 25 days of national sufficiency.

The committee also highlighted the commissioning of the Port Harcourt petroleum product laboratory, the licensing of a petroleum liquid trading exchange described as Africa’s first, and the completion of a framework for a National Strategic Stock capable of covering up to 20 days of supply.

It said plans were underway to increase the strategic reserve to 90 days in 2027.

Pipeline security, crude supply

On crude oil production, the committee expressed confidence that Nigeria could achieve its target of three million barrels per day, attributing the recent increase in output partly to improved pipeline surveillance and security.

Ugochinyere said better protection of oil infrastructure would reduce crude losses, increase feedstock availability for domestic refineries and boost government revenue.

“Fewer breaches mean less crude lost, more product for our refineries, and more revenue for the Federation,” he said.

The committee urged the Federal Government to increase funding for pipeline surveillance contractors and ensure the timely release of funds and logistics needed to sustain operations.

It commended the contractors for their contributions but maintained that improved funding and operational support would further strengthen crude oil production.

The chairman said the committee was also working on legislation to address the persistent challenge of crude oil availability to domestic refineries.

“A refinery without reliable crude is an investment at risk,” he said, stressing the need for statutory guarantees on crude supply, fair market access and a stable policy environment.

On petroleum product importation, Ugochinyere said imports should only be permitted to address verified supply shortfalls rather than serve as a permanent alternative to domestic refining.

“Our goal is balance: security of supply today, and a strong domestic refining industry for tomorrow,” he said.

The committee also disclosed that it had rejected a World Bank recommendation on import licences, insisting that Nigeria’s energy policy must reflect the country’s economic and industrial priorities.

“Nigeria’s energy policy must be written in Nigeria,” Ugochinyere said.

He added that the committee was advancing the Petroleum Industry Act (Amendment) Bill to strengthen provisions on domestic crude supply, licensing, protection of local refiners and regulation of petroleum product imports.

Dangote refinery, marketers

The committee also commended Dangote over the ongoing initial public offering of the Dangote Petroleum Refinery, describing the facility as a strategic national investment valued at about $20 billion.

Ugochinyere said the refinery had introduced fresh momentum into the downstream petroleum market, adding that the National Assembly would support measures to protect domestic refining investments while ensuring fair competition.

He also praised petroleum marketers’ associations, including the Major Oil Marketers Association of Nigeria, the Depot and Petroleum Products Marketers Association of Nigeria, the Independent Petroleum Marketers Association of Nigeria and the Petroleum Products Retail Outlets Owners Association of Nigeria.

He said the associations had invested in depots, jetties, trucks and filling stations, helping to sustain distribution and bridge supply gaps whenever domestic output fell short.

The committee said the contributions of the marketers remained important to national fuel security, particularly as Nigeria worked to expand local refining capacity.

Reps open probe into petitions

Meanwhile, the committee has established two sub-committees to investigate petitions seeking the cancellation of gas distribution licences issued to NIPCO Plc and alleging money laundering and abuse of office against NNPC Limited’s Executive Vice President, Downstream, Dr Mumuni Dagazau.

The petition against NIPCO seeks the investigation, suspension and cancellation of gas distribution licences issued by the NMDPRA to the company for Lagos, Ogun, Oyo and Osun states, as well as the Lagos and Lekki Free Trade Zones.

The petitioners have also requested a public hearing on the matter.

The committee appointed a sub-committee chaired by Mathew Nwogu, with Shehu Dalhatu as deputy, to conduct a preliminary investigation and report its findings to the main committee.

In the second petition, Dagazau was accused of money laundering and abuse of office.

The committee appointed a sub-committee chaired by Aliyu Ibrahim Al-Mustapha, with Cyril Hart as deputy, to investigate the allegations and submit its report within seven days.

Ugochinyere emphasised that the petitions had not been proven and that the committee had yet to reach any conclusion on the allegations.

“These are allegations, and the Committee has reached no conclusion on them. All parties will be given a full and fair opportunity to be heard,” he said.

He added that the committee would not ignore complaints capable of affecting public confidence in the downstream petroleum sector.

The chairman also disclosed that the committee had opened an inquiry into alleged underpayment for crude oil by some companies and questioned NNPC Limited over legacy transactions and refinery rehabilitation.

“We will not accept silence as an answer,” he said.

Neither NIPCO Plc nor Dagazau had publicly responded to the petitions as of the time of the briefing.
