World.title: IEC promises glitch-free 2026 local government elections
World.content:
2026 local government elections are just two weeks away, along with the additional public holiday given to South Africans. For those who’ve been living under a rock, 2026 local government elections take place on Wednesday 4 November 2026.

Better still, the Electoral Commission (IEC) insists everything will go off without a hitch, so you won’t be wasting too much time in queues on your bonus day off. Nevertheless, there are still a few things you can do to make the process as timeous as possible …

2026 LOCAL GOVERNMENT ELECTIONS

At a recent event in Midrand, all participating parties committed to the electoral code of conduct. IEC chairperson Mosotho Moepya said the commission had worked on its voter management devices after being made ‘painfully aware of the technical challenges in 2024.’ Contrary to the massive delays two years ago, both voter registration weekends ahead of 2026 local government elections went ‘exceptionally well,’ said Moepya.



As such, the IEC confirms that:

The results system has completed end-to-end testing.

Parties verified this with independent experts between 5 and 12 October .

. Voting station layouts have been improved to speed up queues.

More than 60 000 staff have been trained.

MIDRAND OPERATIONS CENTRE FAILURE

There are a few precautions you can take before voting that could save you time on the day. Image: File

Back In 2024, the results leaderboards at the Midrand operations centre failed for about two hours. The IEC insisted the results weren’t affected, but it did lead to a number of parties challenging the validity of the election. Furthermore, the embattled ANC claims technical glitches on its online platform stopped it from submitting its full councillor list recently.

This accusation was disproved in the Electoral Court. However, the ANC is escalating the matter to the Constitutional Court. Separately, the IEC has approved 2.6 million special-vote applications have been approved. It also warns of fake voting information and bogus announcements online, so stick to official IEC channels only.

HOW TO VOTE IN 2026 LOCAL GOVERNMENT ELECTIONS

Before you cast your vote in the 2026 local government election, check your nearest station. In this iteration, you can only vote at the station where you’re registered, even if you’ve moved. SMS your ID number to 32810, or WhatsApp ‘Hi’ to 060 088 0000. If you’re not on the voters’ roll, it’s too late, you can’t vote.

On the day, a fortnight from now, bring your valid identify document: A smart ID card, a green barcoded ID book or a valid temporary ID certificate will all be accepted.

Note that driver’s licences, passports, student cards and photocopies of IDs will not be.

Voting stations are open from 7am to 9pm on 4 November , but may stay open longer if necessary.

, but may stay open longer if necessary. Approved special voters can do so on 2 and 3 November , 8am to 5pm.

, 8am to 5pm. At the station. An official will check your ID against the roll, you receive your ballots, and your indelible thumbnail ink mark.

Finally, SASSA beneficiaries should note that payment dates were moved to 30 October, 2 November and 3 November, so grants no longer land on voting day for 2026 local government elections.



But what do you think? Do you think voting will be glitch free like the IEC promises? Did you have a good experience during the 2024 national elections? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: Beachgoers and anglers: Here’s what Tuesday’s tides look like
World.content:
Beachgoers and anglers can check Tuesday’s high and low tide times before planning activities along South Africa’s coastline. Image: Unsplash

If you’re heading to the coast on Tuesday, check the tide times before planning your activities.

Water levels change throughout the day, while wind, waves, swell and the shape of the seabed also affect conditions along the shore and at sea.

Damaging winds and waves along the KZN coast

The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has issued a Yellow Level 2 warning for damaging winds and waves along the KwaZulu-Natal coastline



These conditions could temporarily disrupt beachfront activities and operations at small harbours and ports until Tuesday morning.

Beachgoers, anglers and others planning coastal activities should follow the latest weather warnings and check local sea conditions before heading out.

When to expect the next spring tide

Spring tides are important to watch out for because they bring higher high tides and lower low tides than usual.



The next spring tide is expected around the full moon on Monday, 26 October 2026.

These changes can affect swimming, surfing and fishing. High tides may cover rocks and reefs, while low tides expose more of the shoreline.

Check the tide times and the latest weather and marine warnings before you head to the coast.

World.title: ‘Half a loaf is better than nothing’: Why some SASSA recipients are saying thank you
World.content:
Not every SASSA grant recipient met festive season payment news with anger. A number of South Africans used the moment to express gratitude for the support they receive.

The comments, posted on The South African’s Facebook page, offer a different side to a conversation dominated by frustration over grant amounts.

‘At least we are receiving something’

Mpho Joyce put it simply. “Half a loaf is better than nothing thank you,” she wrote, adding a smiling and praying emoji.



Zandile Macu shared a more personal reason for her thanks, pointing to the role grants play in single-parent households.

“I just want to appreciate and thank you, SASSA, for helping us when there is no father at home, at least we are receiving something rather than nothing. “keep it up guys” Keep it up, guys, with good work,” she wrote.

Macu’s comment highlights how the Child Support Grant often serves as a lifeline for mothers raising children alone.

Faith and perspective from the SASSA recipients

Some commenters turned to faith. Christelle Van Biljon wrote in Afrikaans: “SE Liewers dnk Vir GOD wat one help,” which loosely translates to a call to rather thank God for the help received.

Olivia Hossell focused on older recipients, writing: “This can help the elderly.” Francina Radebe kept it short with a simple “Thanks.”

The December bonus question

Not everyone was fully satisfied. Nokuthula Bhanana raised a question many recipients ask every year.



“Sassa suppose to give an extra money in December, is that too much?” she wrote.

The idea of a December bonus or “13th cheque” for grant recipients circulates widely each year, but SASSA has repeatedly dismissed such claims. Recipients should rely only on official SASSA channels for information about payments and be wary of social media posts promising extra money.

Bhanana’s question shows how even grateful recipients feel the pressure of the festive season.

The mixed reactions reveal a divided community. While some recipients feel the grants fall far short of what they need, others see them as essential support that keeps their households going, especially in homes with no other income.

Win R2 000 in the South African SASSA grant survey

If you receive a SASSA grant and want to share your story, we want to hear from you.

Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

World.title: Four Springboks in doubt for the end-of-year tour
World.content:
Four Tests for the Springboks in November will form part of the conclusion to the Nations Championship tournament, which will see Rassie Erasmus’ team face Italy, France and Ireland as well as one final opponent at the end of November.

It will be interesting to see what selection options Erasmus opts for when it comes to these fixtures, while the medical staff will need to weigh up a few concerning injuries.

Recently, the Sharks confirmed that Eben Etzebeth had “lower limb injury” and that they were now “awaiting a further medical examination to determine the extent of the injury”.



Although there have been no further updates since then, it does seem that Etzebeth could be set for another spell on the sidelines, and could quite possibly be in doubt for the end-of-year tour.

The Springboks have also missed the services of RG Snyman and Kwagga Smith throughout this season due to serious knee injuries, and neither player is expected to be fit in time to return as soon as November.

Adding to this, it’s also likely that Cheslin Kolbe could be in doubt for the tour after he broke his jaw during Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series.

The Springboks are set to regroup at the end of October before heading abroad for their first of four Tests to conclude the Nations Championship.

Springboks’ end-of-year fixtures

Saturday 7 November: Italy v Boks Venue: Allianz Stadium, Turin Kick off: 16:00

Italy v Boks Friday 13 November: France v Boks Venue: Stade de France, Paris Kick off: 22:00

France v Boks Saturday 21 November: Ireland v Boks Venue: Aviva Stadium, Dublin Kick off: 19:30

Ireland v Boks 27–29 November: Finals Weekend Venue: Twickenham Stadium, London Kick off: TBC

Finals Weekend

How does the finals weekend work?

For the Nations Championship, across remaining pool matches in November, teams from the southern and northern hemisphere will continue to compete against each other. Points earned from those matches determine a final one to six ranking for each hemisphere’s table, and the finals weekend pairs each team against their direct equivalent rank from the opposite conference.

So, during the finals weekend, teams play a seventh and final match against their exact equivalent seed from the opposite hemisphere (e.g. sixth vs sixth, fifth vs fifth, down to the first vs first Grand Final).

World.title: Soweto school, church hit by storm
World.content:
SOWETO - A storm has caused damage at Reutlwile Junior Secondary School and at the Regina Mundi Church in Soweto.

Johannesburg Emergency Services are attending both scenes.

Reutlwile is a public no-fee school, while Regina Mundi is one of Soweto’s most prominent churches.

Emergency teams are assessing structural damage and any risk to nearby residents.

READ | Record El Niño? Depends who's counting

No injuries were reported in both incidents, but officials say specialised teams remain on high alert to respond to any emergencies that may occur overnight.

South African Weather Service said partly cloudy and warm to hot conditions are expected on Monday and Tuesday.

But central and eastern parts of the country can expect possible isolated to scattered showers & thunderstorms.

World.title: World Athletics puts ASA on notice
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - World Athletics has put Athletics South Africa (ASA) on notice, giving them six months to adopt a revised Constitution and hold fresh elections.

In a letter to Athletics South Africa leaked to eNCA, World Athletics has appointed Zakhele Dlamini, President of the Southern African Confederation of Athletics, to oversee its directives.

This follows findings earlier this month by ASA's disciplinary panel, which found suspended President James Moloi guilty of the misuse of funds and recommended Moloi's removal.

READ | Cape Town Marathon becomes Africa's first Abbott world major race

No action has yet been taken against Moloi by ASA.

The letter goes on to say that failure to adopt a revised ASA Constitution within the prescribed six-month period would have far-reaching consequences.

This may include the suspension of ASA, a measure which would impact South African athletes on the world stage.

World.title: Bronkhorstspruit Water Crisis: Tshwane deploys 36 water tankers
World.content:
PRETORIA - Strict measures have been issued to the City of Tshwane (CoT) after it failed to warn residents of Bronkhorstspruit, Pretoria East, that their water was unsafe.

More than 400 cases of gastrointestinal illness have been reported in the area since early this month.

Most of those affected are under the age of four.

Now the city is working on increasing the supply of clean drinking water to affected communities. This includes the deployment of a total of 36 water tankers.

Water and Sanitation Minister, Pemmy Majodina, revealed this at a meeting on Monday.

READ |Over 400 ill after Tshwane failed to chlorinate Bronkhorstspruit's water

She said an investigation found that water from the Bronkhorstspruit Water Treatment Works (BWTW) was unchlorinated from 24 September to 14 October after the city experienced issues with its chlorine supplier.

She said water quality tests found extremely high levels of E. coli and total coliforms in the water emanating from the treatment plant.

“Since 14 October, CoT has been distributing drinking water to residents using water tankers. The water tankers obtain water from the Cullinan WTW, and CoT and the Department of Water and Sanitation have conducted laboratory tests on the water from the Cullinan WTW, which indicate that the water is safe to drink.”

Other measures in place include further tests being conducted to confirm whether any other harmful contaminants are present in the water.

Additionally, more specimens have been collected by the National Institute for Communicable Diseases.

This, according to Majodina, will strengthen the epidemiological evidence and help determine whether a formal outbreak declaration is required.

READ |DA promises R10bn in eThekwini water restoration

She said the city is in the process of appointing Rand Water as an implementing agent to address these issues after an investigation also found that various components of the BWTW were not working, such as pumps, sand filters, and other mechanical equipment.

World.title: Solontsi takes over Bok women captaincy
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Sizophila Solontsi will take over captaincy duties for the Springbok Women.

The former sevens rugby player will lead South Africa in the final two Global Series tests against Ireland in Cape Town later this month.

Solontsi resumes the leadership role after regular skipper Babalwa Latsha was ruled out of the series due to an ankle injury.

READ | Dominant Australia wary of Pacific threat at Rugby League World Cup

The experienced Solontsi has already co-captained the side with Unam Tose against Italy last month.

Meanwhile Nombuyekezo Mdliki also failed to recover from her rib injury sustained against Spain earlier this month.

World.title: Masemola's return puts police leadership in focus
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Independent policing Union of South Africa says all eyes will be on National Police Commissioner Fannie Masemola as he returns back to work.

This comes as questions remain about police leadership and the decisions needed to improve command and control.

The union's general secretary, Mpho Kwinika, said that whether or not Masemola drew lessons from his suspension, it would only be he who would be able to answer that question through his actions.

“He might have learned a lot. We don't know, but we will see him. I think these six months should have taught him a lot: That when a decision is supposed to be made, he need to make it. He does not have to wait for someone to advise. "These were not complex matters. These are command and control decisions which he has to make. And unfortunately, we saw what happened, from January 2025 up until he was suspended…”

After 6 months on the sidelines, charged with violating the PFMA, Masemola is now back at work.

READ | SAPS renewal tops agenda as Masemola returns to office

But he returns to a police service ravaged by allegations of corruption and infiltration by underworld figures and faces a tough task of restoring public confidence in the SAPS.

Masemola says unity is paramount within police

“I return to office determined to unite the organisation, strengthen its institutional integrity and advance our constitutional responsibility to serve and protect the people of South Africa. It's not about an individual; it's about the responsibility entrusted to the office for leadership continuity which the organisation SAPS is central to our democracy in the country."

As he returns to duty, Masemola says his first priority is preparing for the upcoming local government elections

World.title: Expectations of credit rating upgrade grow ahead of Medium-Term Budget
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Investors are hoping that this week's Medium-Term budget will make the case for a credit rating upgrade.

There are growing expectations that South Africa is on track for a credit rating boost.

By 2020, all major agencies had downgraded South Africa to below investment grade or so-called junk status.

But since late last year South Africa has started to crawl its way back up again.

READ | Key takeaways from the Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement

S&P lifted its rating late last year, and Fitch followed suit in June.

Moody's said earlier that it could upgrade South Africa's rating if fiscal performance continues to improve.

Investec says South Africa could regain its investment-grade rating by 2028.

World.title: Mbeki denies meddling in prosecution of TRC cases
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - After a failed legal bid to have Commission Chairperson Justice Sisi Khampepe recuse herself for allegations of bias.

Former president Thabo Mbeki finally took the stand at the Khampepe Commission of Inquiry in Johannesburg on Monday.

Mbeki claimed that it is a lie that he interfered in the prosecution of some TRC cases.

READ | WATCH | Mbeki testifies before TRC cases inquiry

He also denied that there were secret meetings to discuss an amnesty deal for apartheid generals responsible for atrocities.

Families known as the Calata group, unhappy with the slow pace in prosecuting matters emanating from the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, want answers on allegations of political interference.

World.title: The scorecard: Ruto's 'land of glory' promise remains a pipe dream as Kenyans grope in uncertainty
World.content:
Lamu County officials, led by Chief Engineer for Roads and Structural Works David Jomeli, inspect an affordable housing project in Lamu County. [Robert Menza, Standard]

A year after President William Ruto pledged to make Kenya food-secure, 2.7 million people face crisis-level hunger, inflation and the cost-of-living measure has climbed to 6.8 per cent, and key flagship promises remain unfulfilled, a Standard review of his then Mashujaa Day speech shows.

In his October 2025 Mashujaa Day address at Ithookwe Stadium in Kitui County, Ruto outlined an ambitious agenda centred on four pillars.

World.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola involving a 65-year-old woman who is a close relative of the first two patients.

The Ministry of Health, in a statement, said the woman developed a fever, sore throat and malaise while in quarantine, prompting her isolation and testing.

Her samples tested positive for Ebola at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI).

According to the Health Director-General Patrick Amoth, the patient has been transferred to an infectious disease unit, where she is receiving supportive care and being monitored.

“Having been in quarantine, she was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care, improving her chances of recovery while limiting the risk of further spread of the disease,” the statement read.

The second patient, on the other hand, is in stable condition and responding well to supportive care.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

According to the Ministry, of the 130 contacts identified so far, 127 had been traced and placed in quarantine, with efforts ongoing to trace the remaining three.

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.

World.title: Ruto wades into growing ODM-UDA conflict
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto marks Mazingira Day by planting trees in Elgon downs, Trans-Nzoia County. [PCS]

President William Ruto delved into the growing tension among Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) and United Democratic Alliance (UDA) contenders in the Coast and asked them to tone it down during his recent tour of the region.

Speaking hours before he wound up his eight-day tour, Ruto appeared to notice the widening cracks and told politicians within the two parties to embrace a ceasefire and unite against the opposition.

The head of state, who is facing a formidable challenge from the united opposition, warned that divisions in the ODM and UDA could weaken their team, whose union gives it a chance to win the 2027 general election.

“ODM and UDA are one team, and you should accommodate each other under a broad-based government. We should not allow divisions in ODM and UDA to undermine our unity of purpose,” he stated.

His statement appeared to be directed at the growing tensions among contenders, particularly in Kwale, Mombasa and Kilifi counties where prominent politicians face challengers within the ODM and UDA political union.

President Ruto’s earlier attempt to zone the region in favour of sitting governors is also blamed for the cracks in the broad-based team at the Coast.

In Mombasa County, UDA secretary general Mr Hassan Omar has already rejected a plan by the so-called broad-based team to support governor Abdulswamd Nassir’s re-election.

Omar, who is also a member of the East African Legislative Assembly (EALA) insisted that he will challenge Mr Nassir.

Already, businessman and EALA member Mr Suleiman Shahbal has quit ODM after he left he could not get the party ticket as the president's allies favour Nassir, a deputy party leader.

Shhabal has since aligned himself to former Laikipia governor Mr Murithi Nderitu’s Kenya Reform Party even as he insisted that he will be on the ballot.

In Mombasa, Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs Cabinet Secretary Mr Hassan Joho and governor Nassir appeared to be handing over Coast which was the ODM leader late Raila Odinga’s political turf, to President Ruto.

“This region stands with Ruto because he has dignified us with title deeds and many other development projects. We however expect him to support us when we seek the presidential seat in 2032,” Joho said.

Joho’s elder brother Abubakar Joho, who is a prominent businessman, has also joined the campaign for President Ruto.

While touring Kwale, Ruto addressed the growing noise among the main contenders, Governor Fatuma Achani (UDA), Prof Hamadi Boga and Engineer Lung’anzi Chai (ODM) after the broad-based leaders appeared to settle for Ms Achani who has the backing of Sports CS and former Kwale governor Salim Mvurya.

After witnessing the rising political tension, Ruto changed tone and told the three contenders to directly seek support from the voters rather than relying on external political backing.

In a complete change of heart and political tact, Ruto emphasised that the power to choose leaders ultimately belongs to the electorate, who will evaluate candidates based on their track record and development agenda for the region.

“You should all seek votes from the people and not rely on external backing. What I need from all of you is your support,” he stated.

For long, Governor Achani has enjoyed unwavering backing of President Ruto, Mvurya and recently Joho, who had preferred Kwale to be zoned in favour of the governor and UDA.

But Prof Boga, who has been Mr Joho’s ally, described the broad-based government’s zoning arrangement as undemocratic and a coercion to the Kwale electorate who he said should be allowed to choose their leaders without external interference.

Boga has been critical about the attempt to stop some aspirants from contesting seats in the broad-based government, noting that it was possible to zone candidates and difficult to do so for the voters.

In a statement, Boga noted that former Gender CS and Kilifi governor aspirant Ms Aisha Jumwa’s recent departure from UDA to Wiper Patriotic Front (WPF) reflected a growing sense among a segment of coastal leaders that decisions about their political future are increasingly being made elsewhere, then handed down as settled outcomes rather than negotiated realities.

“Zoning at the Coast is a fantasy: You can zone candidates but you cannot zone the voters,” Boga had warned.

“And if UDA and ODM are not paying attention to that signal, they may be underestimating the political consequences of their emerging arrangements at the Coast. “There is a dangerous assumption taking root in the broad-based arrangement: that coastal politics can be settled around a table in Nairobi and then delivered to voters as a finished political package. You take this seat, we take that one, and the voters will follow,” he added.

Boga, who came second in the 2022 governor poll, warned that if the Coast is mishandled, the problem will not necessarily be that voters have suddenly embraced another political formation, but the greater danger is that voters may decide that none of the established arrangements speak for them, creating either a rebellion or apathy.

In Kilifi County, the broad-based team publicly worked with Governor Gideon Mung’aro, forcing Ms Jumwa, his main challenger, to quit the government team in protest.

Kilifi Senate aspirant Mr Stephen Kahocho and Ganze parliamentary aspirant Ms Zawadi Kingi have publicly warned that they might be forced to quit UDA and vie as independent candidates or join other political formations.

This is after it emerged that the broad-based arrangement was behind Mung’aro (ODM), Kilifi senator Stewart Madzayo (ODM) and Ganze MP Kenneth Kazungu Tungule of Pamoja African Alliance (PAA), an affiliate of UDA.

World.title: Pope Leo discharged from hospital after lung cancer surgery
World.content:
Rome —

Pope Leo XIV left hospital Saturday, four days after undergoing lung cancer surgery in a swift return to his duties following the first health scare of his papacy.

Leo walked out of hospital unaided, greeting well-wishers, including a 13-year-old Ukrainian girl who gave him a stuffed toy as a gift.

The 71-year-old first American pope was admitted to the Gemelli hospital on Tuesday with doctors removing a nodule that was determined to be pulmonary adenocarcinoma, the most common type of lung cancer.

Leo was deemed ready to leave hospital after blood tests and an X-ray, his doctors said ahead of his release.

He is due to offer the traditional Sunday blessing from a window overlooking St. Peter’s Square on Sunday, a week after he announced he would need surgery.

News of the pope’s illness has been met with shock and concern inside the Vatican, while raising questions about what this means for his papacy.

Pope Leo was elected last May at the relatively young age of 69 and is in good physical shape. As a cardinal living in Rome, he had a personal trainer and is known to enjoy sports such as tennis and swimming.

The pope is scheduled to make a packed trip to Latin America from 6-17 November, including Uruguay, Argentina, and a “homecoming” to Peru where he served as a missionary and bishop for years. The Vatican is remaining cautious about those travel plans.

“We need to see how the Pope feels once he is discharged—what his state of health is—and based on that, he will decide whether to keep or cancel his trips,” Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Holy See Secretary of State, told reporters Friday.

Since his surgery, however, the pope has worked from the hospital, receiving cardinals and having a telephone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin, where he raised the plight of civilians in the southern Ukrainian city of Oleshky.

The pontiff’s doctors told reporters on Saturday there were “no clinical reasons” why his visit to Latin America next month should not take place. They said they expected it would take a couple weeks for Leo to make a “truly complete physical recovery.”

Past popes have written letters of resignation in case of a severe illness or medical emergency that impedes them from carrying out their duties.

Parolin, however, told reporters that he didn’t think Leo had made such a provision. “I don’t think he left anything. It didn’t even seem to me that there was any need and that the matter was so serious to be able to foresee an absence of government.”

Just days before his surgery, however, the pope had confirmed Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle as the Dean of the College of Cardinals.

The dean, who is the “first among equals” leader of the college, plays a crucial role in presiding over a conclave (providing he’s under 80) and the pre-conclave meetings. Any future papal election is considered far into the future. But the appointment of the 69-year-old Tagle, a charismatic figure previously tipped as a possible pope, was an important piece of housekeeping.

This story has been updated. Sharon Braithwaite, Barbie Latza Nadeau and Stefano Pozzebon contributed reporting.

World.title: Elon Musk says he will give a SpaceX share to ‘every kid in America’
World.content:
London —

Elon Musk has said he will give every child in America a stake in SpaceX, his $2 trillion aerospace and artificial intelligence company, as tech firms face intensifying scrutiny over their impact on society.

“Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America,” he wrote on X on Monday. “This will be the first of many.”

SpaceX only began trading publicly in June (and had the biggest initial public offering in history). The company’s shares were trading for about $146 when the market closed on Friday.

Musk’s proposal was thin on detail. It is not clear how those shares would be distributed to the tens of millions of American children or whether all of them would even be eligible.

According to the United States Census Bureau, there are roughly 73 million people under the age of 18, making Musk’s potential giveaway worth about $10.7 billion at SpaceX’s current share price.

Offering young people a stake in the US stock market isn’t a new idea. This month, the Treasury Department automatically signed up millions of under-18s to Trump Accounts, a new federal savings and investment vehicle, with children born between the start of 2025 and the end of 2028 eligible for a one-off $1,000 government contribution.

Damage control?

Musk’s offer came in response to Anthropic’s announcement on Sunday that it will commit at least 5% of its shares — worth $48 billion at the private company’s latest valuation — to a “Public Benefit Fund” that will donate money to social causes.

The fund could make “large donations” to non-profit organizations or “direct distributions to specific populations,” the company wrote on its website, adding that the money could help mitigate the impact of artificial intelligence on people’s jobs.

Musk retorted on X: “I recommend giving the shares directly to the public… This is what I will be doing.”

Both offers come as AI companies face intense backlash over the safety of their products (Anthropic itself recently warned of the “existential risk to humanity” posed by the technology), the potential for AI to push humans out of their jobs en masse, as well as the social and environmental impact of the industry’s gargantuan data center build-out.

Tech titans more broadly are catching heat.

New movies like “The Social Reckoning” — about a Facebook employee blowing the whistle on unsafe company practices — and documentary “You Can See Everything” — following blood testing start-up founder and convicted fraudster Elizabeth Holmes — are helping to remind audiences of the long-running recklessness of some in Big Tech.

Musk himself is the subject of the new documentary “Musk,” charting his life and career. It is unsparing in its criticism of some of his business practices and controversial foray into politics.

World.title: France’s Macron vows to hold accountable those who ‘sought to bring down the Republic’ during major protests
World.content:
France’s President Emmanuel Macron addressed the nation on Sunday evening as communities reeled from one of the most violent nights of unrest in recent years after largely peaceful anti-government protests descended into rioting, leaving government buildings torched, one police officer and one protester dead.

Macron said that the full force of the law would be brought to bear on those who had damaged property or participated in rioting.

“Those who destroyed must pay,” Macron said. “Those who looted must pay back. Those who sought to bring down the Republic will be held accountable.”

Macron described the violence as the work of “seditious elements from far-left factions, joined by numerous delinquents.”

“Watching these images, we were all wondering: what had got into them? How can French people do that to France?”

“Nothing can justify it, explain it or excuse it,” Macron said. “Tonight we all feel both anger and shame.”

The president added that the government should listen to public grievances, and that many protesters did not participate in violence.

“Yesterday, hundreds of thousands of our compatriots demonstrated to state legitimate claims,” Macron said. “Never must we confuse the latter with those who destroyed and vandalized.”

Macron said that he had asked the government to convene stakeholders – including students, teachers, trade unionists and others – this week to discuss “concrete proposals.”

There were at least two deaths connected to rioting and protests over the weekend. A 22-year-old police officer died after being “struck by a third-party vehicle” in the city of Nantes, about 250 miles southwest of Paris, France’s Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said.

One protester died just north of Paris following a “cardiorespiratory arrest,” CNN affiliate BFMTV reported on Sunday, citing the Paris Police headquarters.

Police have detained more than 2,000 people, Nunez said,adding that more than 600 police officers were injured.

Scenes unfolded again on Sunday of police officers launching tear gas into the hallowed Place de la République, where dozens of people gathered in response to messages on social media to “continue the movement,” BFMTV reported. In the central city of Limoges, the 143-year-old town hall was set ablaze on Saturday, with video showing its spire collapsing. In Marseille, masked protesters dressed all in black broke into city hall and defaced the building, and in Lyon, protesters torched the city’s tourist office.

Lawmakers and regional officials launched mounting criticism over the government’s law enforcement plan, BFMTV said, with French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu set to meet the mayors of Paris, Lyon and Marseille, who called for greater reinforcement to repair the damage.

As night fell in Paris on Saturday, groups of young people looted shops and started fires as protests wound down, prompting police to respond with tear gas and baton charges in the narrow streets. Alexandre Bompard, CEO of retail giant Carrefour, said in a social media post Sunday that around 1,500 stores across the country were affected by violence.

More than 600 police officers have been injured, France’s Interior Minister Laurent Nunez posted on X on Sunday, warning that “nothing can justify” the unrest. Earlier this weekend, Lecornu also condemned “unacceptable levels of violence.”

The destruction followed what had been largely peaceful protests, which have grown out of sweeping student-led rallies that gripped parts of France last month, sparking a broader movement against crumbling schools, the spiking cost of living, and perceived government inaction. The rallies have become emblematic of long-simmering, intergenerational anger among people who say their calls for social and political change are going unmet by negligent governments.

Some 550,000 protesters hit the streets across France, including 110,000 in Paris, Nunez said on Saturday. Organizers said far more people turned out.

“There’s an accumulation of wealth and power that’s completely out of control,” one protester, who gave her name as Pauline, told CNN in Paris on Saturday.

“We’re also here to support the youth. There are victories, but if we look at the bigger picture, it’s not going in the right direction,” the 36-year-old added.

Another demonstrator complained of “less democracy” and a “concentration of power” under Macron’s leadership. “There are billionaires who control the media,” Louise, 38, told CNN. “We are fighting to change things.”

Macron slammed “sowers of chaos” for interfering with peaceful protests, and warned late on Saturday that “those who have broken, attacked (police) prefectures, as well as businesses, looted even our town halls, will be prosecuted and punished.”

French police detain a protester during clashes prior to the start of a demonstration in Marseille, southern France, on Saturday, October 17, 2026. Thibaud Moritz/AFP/Getty Images

“We do not back down in the face of rioters and those who’ve come to attack law enforcement,” said the Paris Police Prefecture – the body that oversees the Paris Police Force, emergency services and various other administrative departments – adding that its staffers stood “their ground with courage and professionalism.”

‘Two worlds, two realities’

The police response to the weeks of protest has come under scrutiny. Earlier in the week, that response had left a 14-year-old boy with a fractured jaw. Another police officer was captured on camera using a headlock on a girl in the northwestern area of Alençon, an action now prohibited by law.

This is the second reported instance of a demonstrator losing their hand in the current wave of student protests.

A student in the northeastern city of Lens lost his hand after reportedly picking up a grenade earlier this month, prompting the temporary suspension of one type of stun grenade by police. That ban, which still allowed police to use several different grenades, has now been rescinded.

Overall, authorities said that the “vast majority of individuals” had demonstrated peacefully on Saturday, according to BFMTV.

Police officers charge at demonstrators at Place de la Republique in Paris on Saturday, October 17, 2026. Geoffroy Van Der Hasselt/AFP/Getty Images General view of the Place de la Republique as protesters walk through tear gas during a demonstration at the Place de la Republique in Paris on Saturday, October 17, 2026. Jack Taylor/Reuters

Posting on X, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, leader of the far-left La France Insoumise Party, emphasized that the majority of demonstrators on Sunday had made their point peacefully. “While news channels are flooded with images of violence in dozens of cities, everything is unfolding peacefully with tens of thousands of people calmly mobilized. Two worlds, two realities.”

Masked protesters raise their arms as they face off with French riot police during a demonstration in a street near the Gare du Nord train station in Paris on Saturday, October 17, 2026. Abdul Saboor/Reuters

Youth activists also led solidarity protests in Belgium, Albania and Italy, where police arrested more than 70 people for identification in the city of Milan on Sunday, according to CNN affiliate SkyTG24.

Reuters reported Sunday that police in Milan clashed with stone-throwing demonstrators for a second day, with law enforcement firing tear gas and water cannons in response. SkyTG24 shared video from a supermarket in Milan, showing the windows smashed out and merchandise scattered over the floor after looting.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni condemned the looting in a statement posted on social media, and said that she will convene a meeting in Rome on Monday to “evaluate further measures against those who exploit legitimate demonstrations to sow violence and chaos.”

The wave of protests in France has its roots in the country’s public school system. Earlier this fall, French high school students organized scattered protests demanding reduced class sizes, increased spending on teachers, investments in infrastructure designed to withstand the climate crisis and an end to police violence against young people.

In the past decade and a half, a rise in fertility coupled with funding cuts has led to more students, but fewer teachers in classrooms. The French Education Minister Edouard Geffray has met with student protesters multiple times in recent weeks, although an agreement is yet to be made.

This story has been updated with additional information.

World.title: Amid US pressure on settler violence, Israel arrests at least 10 suspected of West Bank attacks on journalist, diplomats
World.content:
Jerusalem — Amid US pressure on a surge of settler violence in the occupied West Bank, Israeli police arrested at least 10 suspects in the weekend attacks on a Washington Post journalist and an entourage of European diplomats.

Police said the operation to locate and arrest the suspects was called “Olive Leaf,” an apparent reference to the recent start of the olive harvest in the West Bank, which has seen a dramatic rise in settler attacks.

On Friday, settlers attacked and hospitalized veteran Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine as she traveled with a group of Palestinians at the start of the olive harvest. One day later, settlers attacked a group of European diplomats visiting the Palestinian Christian town of Taybeh.

US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee welcomed the arrests as a “very positive development in finding & punishing those who severely attacked and beat Heidi Levine.”

American freelance photojournalist Heidi Levine leaves the emergency room of the government hospital in the Israeli-occupied city of Ramallah, after being treated following an attack by Israeli settlers as she photographed Palestinian farmers harvesting their olives, in the Palestinian village of Abu Falah on October 16, 2026. Ahmad Gharabli/AFP/Getty Images

According to police, security forces worked with the Israeli military to locate and arrest the suspects across the area with the attacks took place. “During this activity, 10 suspects were arrested, findings linking them to the incidents were sized and several vehicles were confiscated,” police said.

“We are working to collect evidence, findings and testimonies and to consolidate an evidentiary infrastructure that will enable bringing those involved to justice,” said Israel Police Superintendent Moshe Pinchi in a statement.

Israeli human rights group Yesh Din documented more than 530 incidents of settler violence since the beginning of the olive harvest in late-September, averaging 27 violent incidents each day. According to Yesh Din, Israeli soldiers were present at roughly one quarter of the attacks over this period.

Palestinians harvest their olive trees in the Israeli-occupied West Bank village of Deir Abu Mashal on October 19, 2026. Ilia Yefimovich/AFP/Getty Images Palestinian Amal Abu Awad, 62, collects olives during the harvest in the West Bank town of Turmus Ayya, Sunday, October 18, 2026. Leo Correa/AP

On Saturday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the Trump administration has told Israel that the US “doesn’t want to see a new spark” in the West Bank and called on Israel to take action against settler violence.

“We’ve asked the Israelis and continue to ask them to crack down on that stuff,” said Rubio before his flight to India and Uzbekistan. “The President has been very clear. He’s said this repeatedly. He does not want to see friction or anything – a crisis – going on in the West Bank.”

Despite video of the attacks on both Levine, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has tried to cast doubt on the violence, saying afterwards that “serious questions remain.” In an apparent attempt to avoid upsetting his right-wing voter base so close to Israel’s elections, Netanyahu has repeatedly downplayed the severity and scale of settler violence, claiming it’s carried out by a rogue group.

Palestinian farmers, accompanied by Israeli and international activists, return to the land where an attack took place the previous day to harvest olives during olive harvest but are prevented from proceeding by Israeli forces on October 17, 2026 in Abu Falah, West Bank. Faiz Abu Rmeleh/Getty Images

Meanwhile, Israel’s defense minister said on Monday he would not reinstate administrative detention against Jewish Israelis, which allows authorities to hold suspects without charge or trial. The draconian measure was one of Israel’s most effective tools against settler extremism, but the defense minister cancelled its use against Jewish Israelis as one of his first decisions nearly two years ago.

On Sunday, President Donald Trump endorsed Netanyahu ahead of the election, which will take place on October 27, calling him “Strong, Brave, and Brilliant.” For weeks, Trump had sidestepped questions on whether Netanyahu should be re-elected, including just days earlier when he said, “I don’t trust anyone in the world of politics.”

World.title: Egypt highlights private sector role in healthcare development, pharmaceutical localization
World.content:
Minister of Health and Population Khaled Abdel Ghaffar stressed the private sector’s central role in Egypt’s healthcare development, particularly in localizing pharmaceutical and vaccine production, which currently meets more than 91 percent of domestic market needs, as well as managing healthcare facilities and delivering high-quality services.

He made the remarks during a high-level roundtable organized by the American Chamber of Commerce in Egypt, attended by healthcare and pharmaceutical industry leaders and representatives of major international and local companies operating in the medical and pharmaceutical sectors.

Abdel Ghaffar outlined the main pillars of Egypt’s national healthcare strategy and the government’s efforts to ensure equitable access to high-quality medical services for citizens across all governorates.

He highlighted the gradual shift from reactive curative care to proactive preventive healthcare through expanded screening and early-detection programs. He also cited President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s support for efforts to reduce hepatitis C infection rates, culminating in Egypt’s receipt of international Gold Tier recognition on the path to eliminating the disease.

The minister also highlighted the Universal Health Insurance System and legislation regulating private-sector investment in healthcare infrastructure, saying these measures provide investors with a secure and stable legislative framework.

The ministry is accelerating digital transformation and automating administrative procedures for licensing medical facilities and registering pharmaceutical products, in full coordination with the Egyptian Drug Authority, he said.

Abdel Ghaffar underscored the government’s efforts to establish a transparent investment climate underpinned by predictability and regulatory stability, reducing paperwork and facilitating the introduction of advanced technologies and modern treatment solutions to the Egyptian market, thereby encouraging innovation and investment.

He also said Egypt’s healthcare system had demonstrated its capacity to withstand ongoing regional challenges and crises, reaffirming the government’s commitment to removing obstacles facing domestic and foreign investors and strengthening Egypt’s position as a leading regional hub for healthcare and medical tourism.

World.title: Madbouly stresses commitment to developing social protection system
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly affirmed the government’s commitment to continuing to develop the social protection system and enhance integration among government policies and programs in a manner that helps meet citizens’ basic needs, ensures the efficient allocation of resources, and reaches the most vulnerable groups.This came during a meeting held by the prime minister on Sunday, October 18, 2026 to follow up on the latest developments regarding the session entitled “Market Regulation and a More Effective Social Protection System,” as part of ongoing preparations for the “Egypt Forum 2026,” which is scheduled to begin tomorrow and run through October 24 in the New Administrative Capital.

The meeting was attended by Social Solidarity Minister Maya Morsy, Supply and Internal Trade Minister Sherif Farouk, Planning and Economic Development Minister Ahmed Rostom, and Head of the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS) Akram al-Gohary.

At the beginning of the meeting, Madbouly stressed that it was being held as part of the follow-up to preparations for the “Market Regulation and a More Effective Social Protection System” session at Egypt Forum 2026, given the importance of this issue and its direct connection to the state’s efforts to improve citizens’ quality of life and strengthen social stability.

During the meeting, the main themes of the session were reviewed to ensure that it addresses the various dimensions of social protection and security, highlights the state’s efforts to strengthen the social protection system and support food security, and promotes integration among government policies and programs. These efforts aim to ensure the efficient allocation of available resources and improve citizens’ living standards.

The meeting also reviewed the government’s efforts to ensure that essential commodities are available in adequate quantities and that supplies remain regular. Discussions covered measures to enhance market stability through continuous monitoring of stock levels, intensified inspections of markets and retail outlets, and action against monopolistic practices and attempts to manipulate prices, thereby protecting consumer rights and helping ease the cost-of-living burden on citizens.

The meeting further addressed the objectives for the coming phase and mechanisms for developing relevant programs and initiatives. It emphasized the importance of highlighting achievements and existing challenges in order to improve government performance, enhance responsiveness to the needs of target groups, and support the state’s efforts to consolidate social protection and security.

World.title: Azhar calls for urgent mediation committee to end regional conflicts
World.content:
Al Azhar has called for the urgent formation of a mediation committee comprising respected figures from Arab and Islamic countries to help end wars and conflicts in the region.

In a statement issued on Sunday, Octobor 18, 2026 Al Azhar Grand Imam Ahmed al-Tayyeb called on Arab and Muslim nations to stop fighting immediately and resolve their differences through dialogue.

He warned that the current conflicts were claiming innocent lives, destroying resources and threatening regional stability.

Al Azhar proposed forming a committee of respected figures from Arab and Islamic countries to ease tensions, bring opposing sides together and seek peaceful solutions to existing disputes.

El Tayyeb expressed his readiness to support the committee’s efforts to end conflicts and prevent further bloodshed.

He also called on all parties to put aside their differences and prioritize peace, national sovereignty and the protection of innocent lives.

Al Azhar stressed the importance of dialogue and cooperation to protect the future of Arab and Muslim nations.

World.title: Egypt, Kazakhstan discuss boosting tourism, archaeological cooperation
World.content:
Minister of Tourism and Antiquities Sherif Fathy met Kazakh Ambassador to Egypt Askar Zhenis on Sunday, Octobor 18, 2026 to discuss ways to strengthen cooperation in tourism and antiquities and attract more visitors from Kazakhstan to Egypt.

During the meeting, Fathy highlighted the growth in tourist arrivals from Kazakhstan, stressing the importance of sustaining this momentum by promoting Egypt’s diverse tourism offerings.

He noted that Kazakh tourists’ interest in cultural tourism and archaeological sites, particularly Mamluk-era Islamic monuments, presents an opportunity to expand promotion of Egypt’s cultural tourism product.

For his part, Zhenis said Egypt is an important destination for Kazakh tourists, highlighting the popularity of Sharm El-Sheikh and growing interest in Egypt’s North Coast.

He added that many Kazakh visitors are keen to visit the Sultan al-Zahir Baybars Mosque in Cairo’s Daher district, praising the cooperation behind its restoration and development. It is worth mentioning that the mosque reopened in 2023.

World.title: Leijdekkers’ Shadow Over Liberia’s Cocaine Probe Grows Harder to Ignore
World.content:
MONROVIA – For most of this year, Jos Leijdekkers has lived in Liberia as a whisper. Security officers traded sightings no one could pin down: a convoy on the Bo Waterside road, a boat slipping down the coast from Freetown. Each time FrontPageAfrica asked for a name, a date or a document behind the talk, the answer came back the same.

By Rodney D. Sieh

“We couldn’t confirm because it was all ‘they-say,’” a member of Liberia’s Joint Security investigative team told FrontPageAfrica, speaking on condition of anonymity. “We have no confirmation based on our investigation. Jos knew both European and US officials were looking for him and Liberia was a no-go.”



But Liberia’s security establishment has not always treated Leijdekkers as rumour. FrontPageAfrica can now report that in July, days after the record cocaine seizure off the RIA Highway, a senior security official named the Dutch fugitive as the mastermind behind the attempt to traffic US$19 million worth of cocaine through Roberts International Airport on June 8. It was the first time a Liberian official had tied the country’s cocaine crisis directly to Leijdekkers. FrontPageAfrica has not independently verified the claim beyond the official’s account, and no charging document naming Leijdekkers has been made public.

On October 14, The Guardian newspaper in London went further. Its investigation, built on what it describes as dozens of interviews with intelligence and police officers on two continents, says Leijdekkers has turned Sierra Leone into the world’s first true narco state and built operating bases across the region, Liberia among them. It also attributes July’s record Liberian seizure, not the smaller airport shipment, to him.

Three accounts now sit side by side: an official who named him in July, an investigator who says his presence was never confirmed, and a foreign newspaper that says he was here and owned the biggest haul of all. They cannot all be fully right. Which one holds will shape the most consequential drug prosecution in Liberia’s history.

What Liberia Knew in July

The June 8 airport case was the first crack. Screeners at RIA flagged six cargo boxes declared as Maggi cubes and lappas. Inside were 198 compressed plates of cocaine, 237.6 kilograms in all, valued at about US$19.2 million and bound for London via Brussels Airlines.

Six weeks later, on July 21, a Joint National Security Investigative Task Force raided a compound on Cement Road in the VOA Community, off the RIA Highway. Investigators recovered 3,971 plates of cocaine, nearly four tonnes, which the State values at US$317.68 million. They also found diving suits, a firearm, GPS trackers, a drone and Starlink satellite equipment. Two foreigners were arrested at the scene: Johann David Garces Grajales, who carries Colombian and Spanish passports, and Srdan Seles, a Serbian national.

Justice Minister Oswald Tweh said at the time that the evidence pointed to a sophisticated, well-funded trafficking network that had operated in Liberia for more than six years. Inspector General of Police Gregory Coleman said both the June and July shipments entered Liberia from Sierra Leone. Within 48 hours of the raid, at least two senior officers of the National Security Agency and the Liberia National Police had been detained for questioning.

Even then, the case had loose ends. Colombia’s Honorary Consulate in Monrovia told FrontPageAfrica it had no record of Garces Grajales as a Colombian national and could not vouch for his passport. Reports at the time said the Liberia Immigration Service could not produce a record of his entry into the country. And investigators noted that the June and July shipments were packaged differently, an early sign that more than one network might be at work.

The Promises: An Indictment and a Dutch Team

The July official’s claim did not come alone. That same week, National Security Advisor Samuel Kofi Woods and Justice Minister Tweh met Dutch government officials in Accra, Ghana. The two sides agreed that the Netherlands would send a team to Liberia in August. Two senior government officials told FrontPageAfrica that Liberia was preparing an indictment against Leijdekkers, treading carefully because of his ties to the Sierra Leonean government.

Three months later, neither commitment is visible on the public record. The Ministry of Justice has not said whether the Dutch team arrived or what it found. No indictment naming Leijdekkers has been filed in any Liberian court. Inspector General Coleman promised in July to pursue suspects abroad through extradition and mutual legal assistance; FrontPageAfrica has seen no request to Freetown or The Hague.

Instead, the cases moved in other directions. In August, prosecutors charged former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor in connection with the US$317 million seizure. On October 7, a 55-page indictment named her, former NSA deputy director Gerald Folley Smith, former airport operations chief Mark Kuiah and others. All are presumed innocent. Leijdekkers’ name appears in neither the airport indictment nor the VOA indictment.

‘They-Say’: The Presence Question

The Joint Security source and the July official are not necessarily contradicting each other. One is talking about where Leijdekkers was. The other is talking about whose network moved the cocaine.

A trafficker of Leijdekkers’ reach does not need to set foot in Liberia to run cocaine through it. His operation works through proxies, corrupt port workers and a small circle of trusted lieutenants, keeping the boss far from the product. The investigator’s point is narrower: Liberian agencies never established that he entered the country.

The Dutch appeared to believe he did, or planned to. In May, De Telegraaf reported that Dutch special forces twice came close to seizing Leijdekkers in international waters off Sierra Leone as he travelled by boat to Liberia. Both operations were called off at the last minute; one, according to Omroep Brabant, because he never left Sierra Leone. Dutch prosecutors would neither confirm nor deny the account. If the Dutch had intelligence that Liberia was his destination, it is fair to ask whether that intelligence was shared with Monrovia, and what the promised August team brought with it.

What the Guardian Adds

The Guardian’s Liberia claims are brief, but each lands on a raw nerve in Monrovia:

* A base in Liberia. The report says Leijdekkers has established operating bases in Liberia, Guinea-Bissau and, most recently, Ghana.

* Diplomatic passports and an open border. It says he and his men move around the region on diplomatic passports, and cites witnesses who describe Liberian police applauding his convoy as it crossed the border.

* Ownership of the record haul. It describes the nearly four tonnes found near Monrovia on July 21 as Leijdekkers’ cocaine.

* Presence on the eve of the bust. It says sources reported that he returned to Freetown from Liberia the day before the July bust was announced, and that the same sources recognised the man arrested with the Monrovia cocaine as someone seen with Leijdekkers in Freetown.

The report quotes a Dutch official warning that “the entire West Africa region is at risk.” It does not say whether Liberian authorities were asked to comment on these claims, and none is quoted. Its sourcing, on Liberia as on Sierra Leone, is largely anonymous intelligence and police officers. Leijdekkers’ lawyer has dismissed the allegations as politically driven. The Guardian reports that Leijdekkers is married to Agnes Bio, daughter of Sierra Leone’s President Julius Maada Bio, while stressing there is no suggestion the president is implicated in any illegal activity linked to him.

Where the Accounts Collide

The sharpest problem is not whether Leijdekkers entered Liberia. It is which cocaine was his.

In October, Liberian investigators told FrontPageAfrica they had found no connection between the US$19 million airport case and the US$317 million VOA case. The airport pipeline, they say, ran Sierra Leone–Liberia–United Kingdom/Netherlands, moving cocaine out by commercial airfreight under false declarations. That fits the July official’s account, which placed Leijdekkers behind the airport shipment.

The VOA case, as laid out in the October indictment, is a different operation: cocaine landed from the Atlantic in May, a fishing business and a front airline as cover, and protection allegedly bought from senior Liberian officials. Investigators describe its route as Colombia–Brazil–Liberia–Ghana–Eastern Europe–Dubai.

The Guardian attributes the VOA haul to Leijdekkers. Liberia’s investigators do not. There are three ways to read the gap. The Guardian’s sources may have folded Liberia’s two seizures into one story, as many Liberians did for months. Liberian investigators may have drawn the line between the two networks too neatly. Or the networks may be separate on paper but connected at the top, with Leijdekkers or his associates touching both.

One thread makes the third reading hard to dismiss. In September, FrontPageAfrica reported that investigators had traced four Balkan-linked operatives tied to Liberia’s drug trade, including one named Seleš, to multiple visits to Freetown, with what officials described as strong indications of ties to Leijdekkers. Srdan Seles, the Serbian arrested at the VOA compound, shares that name. The Guardian says the man arrested with the Monrovia cocaine was seen with Leijdekkers in Freetown. Whether these refer to the same man is a question Liberian investigators can answer, and so far have not.

The official account has also shifted on how the VOA cocaine came ashore. In July, investigators told FrontPageAfrica it was run in by speedboat and canoe at Robertsport, Grand Cape Mount County, about 10 miles from the Sierra Leone border, with divers in wetsuits bringing it in from the water. The October indictment places the landing on the Po River at Royesville, in Bomi County. Either the cocaine moved through both, or the State revised its account. Defence lawyers will want to know which.

How the Report Changes the Investigation

1. Silence is no longer an option. Until now, Liberian officials could treat Leijdekkers as speculation in public while naming him in private. A major international newspaper has now stated on the record that Liberia’s biggest drug haul belonged to him and that Liberian police cheered his convoy. If that is false, the Liberia National Police, the Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency and the Ministry of Justice need to say so, with reasons. If it is true, they need to explain why their own investigators say they found nothing.

2. The Accra commitments are now a test. The July meeting in Accra produced two promises: a Dutch team in August and an indictment against Leijdekkers. The Guardian report makes both a matter of public interest. If the Dutch came and shared intelligence, Liberians are entitled to know what the State did with it. If the indictment was shelved, they are entitled to know why.

3. The border and immigration questions are now specific. The claim that police applauded a convoy at the border, and that the network travels on diplomatic passports, points to named institutions: border police, the Liberia Immigration Service and whoever authorises diplomatic courtesies at entry points. The State still has not publicly explained how Garces Grajales entered Liberia without a record. Inspector General Coleman has already named officers he says took about US$5,000 each to escort a cocaine landing. The Guardian’s claim widens that circle.

4. The prosecution has a new vulnerability. The State’s theory in the VOA case is a Latin American and Balkan network shielded by Liberian insiders. A credible public claim that the same cocaine belonged to a Dutch kingpin operating from Freetown is a gift to defence lawyers looking for doubt, as is a landing site that moved from Robertsport to Royesville. Liberia has been here before. In 2022, officials found 520 kilograms of cocaine, worth about US$100 million, at the Sonit compound in Monrovia; a jury acquitted all four defendants in May 2023, a judge ordered US$200,000 in seized cash returned, and the men left the country. Weak chains of custody, thin forensics, and trouble proving who owned the cargo sank that case. This one is eight times heavier.

5. Liberia’s reputation is now tied to Freetown’s. Europe is already tightening scrutiny of passengers from Liberia and Sierra Leone on Brussels-bound flights. Ghana has arrested men accused of representing Leijdekkers’ network after French customs seized nearly 3.9 tonnes of cocaine in Dunkirk. A suspect linked to Liberia’s case was arrested in Accra at Liberia’s request and then reportedly vanished. Every week Liberia spends unable to say clearly what it knows makes it easier for partners to treat Monrovia and Freetown as a single problem.

The Questions That Remain

* Did the Dutch team arrive in August, and what intelligence did it share on Leijdekkers’ links to Liberia?

* Is the indictment against Leijdekkers still being prepared, or has it been set aside?

* What evidence led a senior security official to name him as the mastermind of the June airport shipment?

* Is Srdan Seles the same man investigators traced to Freetown, and has anyone placed him with Leijdekkers?

* Did the VOA cocaine land at Robertsport, Royesville or both?

* Has the Liberia Immigration Service checked entry records at the Sierra Leone border for the dates the Guardian’s sources cite, including the eve of the July 21 bust?

* Will the Ministry of Justice publicly respond to the Guardian’s claim that the US$317 million haul was Leijdekkers’ cocaine?

Myth or Map?

Liberia’s security establishment has said two things about Jos Leijdekkers this year. In private, a senior official named him as the hand behind the airport shipment, and colleagues spoke of an indictment. On the investigative team, he remains “they-say.” The truth may sit between: a man who never crossed into Liberia himself, but whose money, people and cocaine did.

What has changed is the cost of not knowing. A rumour can be ignored. A published claim that Liberian police cheered Europe’s most wanted trafficker across the border cannot. The Guardian has done what months of whispers could not: it has made Leijdekkers Liberia’s question to answer, in public.

Jos Leijdekkers has not been charged with any crime in Liberia and, through his lawyers, denies the allegations against him. All defendants named in this report are presumed innocent unless proven guilty by a court of competent jurisdiction.
