World.title: Costa Rica Faces an $882 Million Revenue Hole as Courts, Police and Schools Take Cuts
World.content:
Costa Rica expects to collect about ₡400,000 million ($882 million) less than it budgeted for 2026, and the Finance Ministry is asking lawmakers to close the gap with a mix of spending cuts and new borrowing that would push the deficit to its highest level since 2020.

The measures are contained in the second extraordinary budget of 2026, now before the Legislative Assembly’s Hacendarios (budget) committee. The bill makes a net reduction of ₡167,968 million ($370.4 million) to this year’s national budget and seeks authorization for an additional ₡187,000 million ($412.4 million) in borrowing, according to the bill and the Comptroller General’s Office (CGR).

The Judicial Branch takes the largest single cut, at ₡13,105 million ($28.9 million). That includes ₡5,020 million ($11.1 million) from the Judicial Investigation Agency (OIJ) and ₡4,680 million ($10.3 million) from the Public Prosecutor’s Office. The security sector loses about ₡12,922 million ($28.5 million), with ₡7,445 million ($16.4 million) of that coming from the Ministry of Public Security’s citizen security program. The reduction also eliminates funding for 172 vacant security positions.

The Ministry of Public Education (MEP) faces a cut of about ₡8,973 million ($19.8 million). The bill trims ₡3,648 million ($8 million) from classroom technology, including laptops, robotics kits and internet connectivity, and ₡363.6 million earmarked for a student transportation program that was due to begin in late November. Funding for 10 new schools is moved to 2027.

Across the government, the bill removes ₡14,259 million ($31.4 million) tied to 2,714 vacant positions and lowers debt-service spending by ₡110,000 million ($242.6 million). The Supreme Elections Tribunal, the Ministry of Environment and Energy and roughly 20 other institutions also see reductions.

Deputy Revenue Minister Víctor Carvajal told the committee that the drop in collections stems from informal commerce, smuggling, problems with the TRIBU-CR digital tax platform and the exchange rate. Carvajal said the trend could reverse once September and late-October collection figures are tallied.

Deputy Expenditure Minister Luis Molina told legislators the extraordinary budget was necessary because of the decline in revenue. Finance Ministry officials have said they want to contain spending without automatically turning to more debt and without taking on new permanent commitments that lack funding.

The CGR projects total revenue nearly ₡400,000 million below budget, of which ₡373,000 million ($822.5 million) is tax revenue. The office warned that the bill would produce the country’s largest fiscal deterioration since 2020. According to the CGR, the financial deficit would rise from 4.3% to 4.8% of gross domestic product, or about ₡2.5 trillion ($5.5 billion).

The primary balance, which excludes interest payments, would turn negative for the first time since 2021, at a deficit of ₡30,000 million ($66.2 million). Because the cuts do not cover the full revenue shortfall, the remaining gap would be financed with additional debt. The CGR also projected that the tax burden would fall to 12.6% of GDP, down 0.7 percentage points.

Acting Comptroller Bernal Aragón recommended measures to strengthen revenue collection and make public income more sufficient and sustainable. The CGR called for a medium-term revenue strategy based on a comprehensive review of the tax system, noting that income, value-added and selective consumption tax receipts have shown weak and at times negative growth for several months.

Aragón also told the committee that no preventive studies had been carried out on how the security cuts would affect public safety, and that such analysis would come with the year-end budget settlement. Julissa Sáenz of the CGR’s public finance oversight area also presented the office’s concerns to lawmakers.

Opposition legislators questioned the approach. Diana Murillo of the National Liberation Party said adjustments are necessary when revenue falls but asked whether repeated cuts of this size point to poor financial planning, adding that presenting cuts is the easier part compared with proposing alternatives.

Frente Amplio deputy María Eugenia Román said it was ironic that the Judicial Branch is criticized for slow case resolution while its budget is restricted. She also warned that provisions in the 2027 budget could limit new hiring in the courts. The bill does not propose new taxes. It is the second round of cuts this year, after the first extraordinary budget of 2026 reduced spending by ₡70,000 million ($154.4 million), including ₡40,000 million from the CEN-CINAI child nutrition and care program.

Finance Minister Rodrigo Chaves said in June that cuts were coming for every branch of government. The ruling Pueblo Soberano party holds 31 of the Assembly’s 57 seats, a majority sufficient to approve the bill. The Hacendarios committee aims to issue its reports on the extraordinary budget and the 2027 national budget by tomorrow, after which both go to the full Assembly for debate.

World.title: Costa Rica Owls: Camera Traps Reveal Their Hidden Live
World.content:
Costa Rica is home to an array of owl species. They come in a variety of patterns, shapes, and sizes, but they have a few things in common. They are all predators and most do their hunting at night. They generally have stout bodies and round heads. My favorite shared trait among owls is how ticked off they always look. Every time I see them in person or record them with my camera traps, the expression is always the same, a stern face that seems to say, ‘Hoo are you looking at?!’ (Sorry, I couldn’t resist.)

Another attribute that makes owls popular amongst birders and the public in general is the sense of mystery surrounding them. Most remain hidden during the day and difficult to spot at night. Frequently a distant hoot or shriek is the only evidence of their presence in the forest. That makes a sighting or camera trap recording of any owl species a special treat. I’ve only seen and recorded a few species over the years, and I’d like to tell you a little about each. They will appear in the order that I talk about them in the video below.

A Giant Owl

The spectacled owl (Pulsatrix perspicillata) is a hefty beast. Its Spanish name is oropopo, which is easy to remember because it’s fun to say. I see this owl in person more than any other owl species. There’s a type of habitat and time of year where I see them most frequently. It’s during Guanacaste’s dry season in trees that still have their leaves along dried streambeds.

They seem to enjoy hiding in the shady trees during the day, waiting for night to fall. I’ve gotten so good at predicting where to see them, that one time I was hiking with another biologist, and I told him that this seems like a good place to see spectacled owls and one flew over us ten seconds later. That counts for 1,000 biology points! I can still feel a buzz of pride when I think back on it.

I record these big owls pretty frequently with my camera traps as well. Some recent highlights include one drinking from a puddle in the mouth of a beautiful cave, one eating a white-throated magpie-jay on a tree branch, and a couple of different individuals splashing around, taking a bath.

Two Small Owls

The Pacific screech owl (Megascops cooperi) and the Ferruginous pygmy owl (Glaucidium brasilianum) come in on the other end of the owl size spectrum. The screech owl is small, and the pygmy owl is straight up tiny. Every once in a while, I’ll look up from messing around with a camera trap at the base of a tree and notice a Pacific screech owl staring daggers at me from the branch of a nearby tree. The pygmy owl, I always hear before spotting.

Their call is a repetitive whistle that’s easy to imitate. I’ve learned that I can repeat their simple call back to them and they’ll fly in to investigate, but I’ve also learned to not do it too frequently because many times, I’ll call one over to me and it’ll end up getting mobbed by all the local birds who don’t appreciate the presence of the tiny predator as much as I do.

I record the screech owl much more frequently than the pygmy owl with my camera traps for reasons that are unclear to me. When I record either species, it is generally doing the same exact thing, snacking on an insect.

More Owls

Of the many other species of owl in Costa Rica, I’ve only had interactions with a few others. I once worked with a striped owl (Pseudoscops clamator) in a wildlife rehabilitation center, and its striped plumage and long ear tufts made it one of the most beautiful birds I’ve ever seen. I helped raise three barn owl (Tyto alba) chicks at the same rescue center and I recorded one really nice, clear barn owl video with one of my camera traps. Finally, every once in a while, I’ll record a mottled owl (Ciccava nigrolineata) with my cameras, though I’ve never seen one in person.

About the Author

Vincent Losasso, founder of Guanacaste Wildlife Monitoring, is a biologist who works with camera traps throughout Costa Rica

World.title: Police investigate whether improperly parked car contributed to fatal bus crash that killed Sherri Mejia and 4-year-old Taleenie Garbutt
World.content:
Police investigate whether improperly parked car contributed to fatal bus crash that killed Sherri Mejia and 4-year-old Taleenie Garbutt

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating whether a car parked partially in the path of oncoming traffic contributed to Saturday evening’s fatal collision between a National Bus Company bus and a Toyota Corolla on the Thomas Vincent Ramos Highway.

The accident, which occurred between Miles 37 and 38 near San Juan Village, claimed the lives of Sherri Mejia and four-year-old Taleenie Garbutt.

During Monday’s police press briefing, Assistant Superintendent Stacy Smith said investigators believe the car had stopped along the highway to allow a passenger to relieve themselves.

According to preliminary findings, the bus was travelling in the opposite direction when its driver apparently attempted to swerve to avoid the parked car but was unable to prevent the collision.

Smith said an examination of the scene and the vehicle suggested that the car had not been parked completely off the roadway and may have been partially obstructing the lane used by oncoming traffic.

Mejia died at the scene, while Taleenie later succumbed to her injuries while receiving medical treatment. Four other occupants of the car were injured.

According to public reports, Taleenie’s father, Walton Garbutt, sustained a broken foot and a knee injury requiring surgery.

Police have obtained a urine sample from the bus driver and served him with a notice of intended prosecution.

Investigations continue to determine the precise circumstances of the collision and whether traffic violations contributed to the deaths.

World.title: Police launch internal investigation into chokehold used during arrest in Unitedville
World.content:
Police launch internal investigation into chokehold used during arrest in Unitedville

By Breaking Belize News Staff: The Belize Police Department has launched an internal investigation into a viral video showing an officer placing a man in a chokehold during an arrest in Unitedville, Cayo District.

During Monday’s press briefing, Assistant Superintendent of Police Stacy Smith explained that chokeholds are classified as deadly force under the department’s policies and procedures manual, comparable to discharging a firearm or striking someone in the head with a baton.

Smith said such force should only be used as a last resort when there is an imminent threat of death or grievous bodily harm. The internal investigation will determine whether the officer’s actions were justified under those circumstances.

She also suggested that less-lethal alternatives, including pepper spray, could have helped de-escalate the confrontation, but noted that the officers involved did not appear to have that option readily available.

The man involved has been identified as Samuel Parham, whose family has publicly questioned the officers’ actions following the October 16 incident.

Police confirmed that Parham has since been charged with grievous harm after an officer reportedly suffered a broken arm during the confrontation.

Smith said investigators had obtained additional footage showing an officer being thrown to the ground, an incident that was not visible in the shorter recording she initially reviewed.

The Professional Standards Branch is investigating the matter, and police are encouraging witnesses to cooperate as investigators seek to establish whether the use of force was justified.

World.title: Belize City man accused of raping ex-girlfriend in her home with her son present despite restraining order, remanded to prison
World.content:
Belize City man accused of raping ex-girlfriend in her home with her son present despite restraining order, remanded to prison

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 26-year-old Belize City construction worker has been remanded to the Belize Central Prison after being charged with allegedly raping and assaulting his former girlfriend despite an existing protection order against him.

Shadron Gillett, of Iguana Street, appeared in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on Monday, October 19, where he was charged with rape, harm and damage to property in connection with an incident involving a 28-year-old woman on July 2, 2026.

According to the allegations, the woman was resting on her verandah around 3 p.m. when Gillett approached her and insisted on speaking with her. She reportedly reminded him of the protection order and demanded that he leave.

The woman told police that when she attempted to record him with her cellphone, Gillett grabbed the device and smashed it. During a subsequent struggle, he allegedly damaged another cellphone before the confrontation moved into her bedroom.

The complainant alleged that Gillett grabbed her by the neck, ordered her to stop screaming for help and struck her in the head with a surge protector before sexually assaulting her.

During the alleged attack, the woman’s son reportedly knocked on the door. Gillett allegedly ordered him to leave, but the woman urged her son to remain. She further alleged that Gillett punched her in the mouth before fleeing the residence.

Police subsequently charged Gillett with rape, harm and damage to property involving two cellphones valued at a combined $1,300.

No plea was taken on the rape charge, which is an indictable offence to be tried before the High Court.

Gillett was offered bail of $5,000 with one surety of the same amount or two sureties of $2,500 each. His bail conditions prohibit him from interfering with the complainant or her family and require him to remain at least 100 yards away from her.

However, he was unable to meet bail and was remanded to prison until he can do so. His next court appearance is scheduled for December 28, 2026.

World.title: Augustine sisters acquitted of burning down mother-in-law’s $32,000 home in Crooked Tree
World.content:
Augustine sisters acquitted of burning down mother-in-law’s $32,000 home in Crooked Tree

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Two Belize City sisters accused of burning down their former mother-in-law’s home in Crooked Tree Village more than four years ago were acquitted of arson on Monday after a nine-member jury returned a unanimous not guilty verdict.

Janiene Augustine, 27, and her younger sister Janiece Augustine, 23, broke down in tears as the verdict was delivered before Justice Nigel Pilgrim in the High Court. The jury, comprising six women and three men, deliberated for approximately two hours before reaching its decision.

The sisters were accused of intentionally setting fire to a woman’s home on July 16, 2022, destroying a wooden structure valued at $30,000 and household contents worth an additional $2,000.

Prosecutors alleged that Janiene, who had been living at the property with her then common-law husband and their children, was motivated by a dispute that resulted in the common-law husband putting her out of the house two days before the fire.

The prosecution relied on circumstantial evidence, including testimony that the sisters had entered the property shortly before the blaze. However, no witness testified to seeing either woman start the fire.

In his summation, Justice Pilgrim highlighted the absence of scientific evidence establishing that the fire had been deliberately set. He reminded jurors that the burden rested entirely on the prosecution to prove guilt beyond a reasonable doubt.

Both sisters denied setting the house ablaze, maintaining that they had visited the property only to collect Janiene’s belongings.

The women were initially charged in April 2024, nearly two years after the fire, following directives from the Director of Public Prosecutions.

Janiene was represented by attorney David McKoy, while Janiece was represented by attorneys Leeroy Banner and Lesly Mendez.

Monday’s unanimous verdict brings the lengthy criminal proceedings against the sisters to an end, with both women cleared of the arson charge.

World.title: Coast Guard member Lionel Logan critically injured, Julian Dyer shot in attack on SUV in Corozal
World.content:
Coast Guard member Lionel Logan critically injured, Julian Dyer shot in attack on SUV in Corozal

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A member of the Belize Coast Guard was critically injured and another man wounded after gunmen opened fire on a vehicle travelling along the Philip Goldson Highway near Carolina Village, Corozal District, on Sunday evening, October 18, 2026.

The victims have been identified as 35-year-old Lionel Logan, a Belize Coast Guard member from Libertad Village, and 35-year-old Julian Dyer, a construction worker from Corozal Town.

According to initial reports, the men were travelling in a black Chevrolet Equinox with several other passengers after leaving a football game in Carolina Village when a black van carrying approximately four men pulled alongside their vehicle. Occupants of the van reportedly opened fire on the SUV, striking both men.

Logan sustained multiple gunshot wounds to his left forearm, lower abdomen and the back of his head. He was transferred to the Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital in Belize City, where he was listed in critical condition. His current condition has not been independently confirmed.

Dyer suffered pellet injuries to his right forearm and lower abdomen. He was treated at the Corozal Community Hospital but subsequently discharged himself.

A nine-year-old girl travelling with her mother also sustained a minor cut to the palm of her right hand, reportedly caused by shattered glass. Both managed to escape from the vehicle during the attack.

The Chevrolet Equinox was later found abandoned in the San Antonio Village area with multiple apparent bullet holes and shattered windows.

The motive for the attack remains unknown, and no suspects have been publicly identified. Police investigations continue.

World.title: Deon Jones, Lloyd Faber injured as gunman opens fire on group socializing on King Street
World.content:
Deon Jones, Lloyd Faber injured as gunman opens fire on group socializing on King Street

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating an attempted murder incident in Belize City that left two men injured after a gunman opened fire on a group socializing on King Street on Saturday night, October 17, 2026.

The victims have been identified as 27-year-old Deon Jones and 43-year-old Lloyd Faber, a stevedore, both residents of Belize City.

According to police, around 10:20 p.m., four men were socializing in a yard on King Street when an unidentified male emerged from behind a building and fired several shots in their direction, striking Jones and Faber.

Police received reports of the shooting around 10:30 p.m. and responded to the scene, where they learned that both injured men had already been transported to the Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital for treatment.

The extent of their injuries has not been disclosed, and police have not established a motive for the attack.

The shooting comes amid renewed concerns about gun violence in Belize City, following a series of murders reported earlier this month.

Police investigations continue.

World.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs and OAS discuss Belize-Guatemala relations
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs and OAS discuss Belize-Guatemala relations

By Zoila Palma: Today, Foreign Minister Francis Fonseca met with Ambassador Antonia Urrejola, Special Representative of the Secretary General of the Organization of American States (OAS) for Belize-Guatemala relations, to discuss matters relating to the Belize-Guatemala relationship and ongoing regional engagement.

The meeting was attended by Oscar Arnold, Chief Executive Officer for Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade, and Directors of International Affairs, Ambassador Ayesha Borland and Ambassador Alfonso Gahona.

World.title: Muffles College counsellor Hayden Mendez charged with sexual assault and encouraging child pornography
World.content:
Muffles College counsellor Hayden Mendez charged with sexual assault and encouraging child pornography

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 31-year-old counsellor at Muffles College in Orange Walk has been criminally charged following allegations of sexual misconduct involving a 17-year-old female student.

Hayden Mendez appeared in court on Monday, October 19, 2026, charged with sexual assault and encouraging child pornography. He was granted bail.

According to Assistant Superintendent of Police Stacy Smith, the investigation began after police discovered a screenshot circulating on social media suggesting sexually explicit interactions between the counsellor and the student.

Investigators subsequently visited the school, contacted the student and her parent, and involved the Human Services Department. Police recorded several statements and collected evidence before bringing charges against Mendez.

Smith indicated that the alleged incidents occurred between 2025 and 2026, describing the allegations as a breach of trust involving an adult employed at the institution.

Police are also conducting a separate investigation into how the school’s administration handled the allegations, including whether appropriate action was taken after the matter was brought to its attention.

Last week, BBN reported that Muffles College had placed a staff member on administrative leave after receiving an allegation of misconduct on October 6. The school pledged to cooperate with investigations by police and social services.

Police have not determined whether there are additional alleged victims and are encouraging anyone with relevant information or similar experiences to come forward.

Mendez has not been convicted of the offences, and the allegations remain before the court.

World.title: Fi Wi Land: Beyond the duppy stories, discover the value of Jamaica’s bats
World.content:
Often misunderstood and surrounded by folklore, bats are among nature’s hardest-working environmental protectors, helping to control insect populations, pollinate plants and disperse seeds. Discover more about these fascinating creatures as the Jamaica Observer in association with the National Environment and Planning Agency (NEPA) premieres ‘Fi Wi Land’ on Monday.

In the debut episode, host Carlysia Ramdeen is joined by NEPA Environmental Officer Damany Calder who shares insights about bats, their importance to Jamaica’s ecosystems and why they deserve greater appreciation.

The new 12-week environmental series by the Jamaica Observer and NEPA explores Jamaica’s unique wildlife, ecosystems and natural resources while highlighting efforts to protect the island’s environment for future generations.

Catch the premiere on the Jamaica Observer’s YouTube channel and other digital platforms.

World.title: Proud moment for Barnswells as husband and wife conferred with national award
World.content:
Councillor Scean Barnswell and wife Danielle pose for a photograph after receiving their Badge of Honour for Gallantry at the 2026 Ceremony of Investiture and Presentation of National Honours and Awards at King’s House on Monday, October 19. 2026. (Photo: Llewellyn Wynter)

It was a historic and proud moment for the Barnswell family from Clarendon, when the husband and wife team of Councillor Scean Barnswell and Danielle Anna-Marie Barnswell stood on the dais at King’s House Monday morning to accept their national award – the Badge of Honour for Gallantry, from Governor General Sir Patrick Allen.

The occasion was the 2026 Ceremony of Investiture and Presentation of National Honours and Awards.

The Barnswells were among 149 Jamaicans who were honoured for outstanding contributions in various fields.

The two were recognised for their “quick and courageous” actions that led to the rescue of a six-year-old girl who was reportedly abducted from the St Thomas More Preparatory School in May Pen Clarendon on December 9 last year.

“In growing up you’re told to mind your business but in Jamaica, the children are all our business so in this case I’m happy we did that and I wouldn’t change anything,” said Mrs Barnswell during rehearsals for Monday’s ceremony.

Scean Barnswell is the councillor for the Hayes division in the Clarendon Municipal Corporation and a former Mayor of May Pen. He is looking to return to that position as the balance of power in the corporation recently swung from the Jamaica Labour Party (JLP) to the Opposition People’s National Party (PNP).

This came after the JLP-elected councillor for the May Pen North division, Tanya-Lee Williams, resigned from the JLP, giving the PNP a clear 12-10 majority in the corporation. The PNP has stated that this gives it the right to appoint the mayor and deputy mayor but a court injunction granted last Friday has stalled those plans. The PNP has said it will be going back to court.

According to reports from December 2025, Barnswell and his wife spotted a man walking with a small child along Bustamante Highway and, sensing something was wrong, immediately intervened. Their actions resulted in the safe recovery of the child and the capture of the suspect, who was arrested by the police.

In a statement at the time, the PNP described the incident as an act of humanity, noting that Councillor Barnswell showed decisive, selfless leadership in a moment of crisis. The party said his response reflected the values of community vigilance and public service and urged others to do likewise.

WATCH: Barnswell honoured for rescuing abducted six-year-old

The PNP also expressed gratitude to members of the public who raised the alarm and commended the Jamaica Constabulary Force for its swift response.

“It emphasised the importance of strong community–police partnerships in protecting children and preventing crimes of this nature,” the party said.

-Lynford Simpson

World.title: Fresh questions over MVP as Clayton twins linked to new track setup
World.content:
The twin sprinting duo of Tia (left) and Tina Clayton. (Photo: Garfield Robinson)

Rumours of sprint twins Tia and Tina Clayton possibly leaving MVP Track Club for a new professional outfit being established by coach Corey Bennett – reportedly with funding from athletics wear giant Nike –have raised fresh questions about the future of one of Jamaica’s most successful athletics programmes.

Neither the Clayton sisters, Bennett nor Nike have publicly confirmed the reported move.

Observer Online reached out to the MVP President Bruce James for a confirmation or denial and his terse response was, “we do not respond to rumours”.

However, the rumours come at a particularly sensitive time for MVP, following the death of its founder and long-time head coach Stephen Francis on July 4 this year.

For over two decades, Francis was the standard bearer of MVP, building the club from its inception into an internationally respected sprinting powerhouse that produced world beaters including Shelly-Ann Fraser-Pryce, Elaine Thompson-Herah, Asafa Powell, Shericka Jackson, and now Kishane Thompson.

His demanding training methods, technical expertise and ability to identify and develop talent made MVP a major force in Jamaican and international athletics. Under his leadership, the club became synonymous with sprinting excellence and helped establish Jamaica as a dominant power on the global stage.

Francis’s death has therefore left more than a coaching vacancy. It has created questions about succession, athlete retention and whether the system he built can maintain its identity and success without its central figure.

The Clayton twins are among the club’s most promising younger professionals and represent an important part of its future. The sisters emerged from Edwin Allen High School under coach Michael Dyke before joining MVP in 2022 after signing professional contracts with Nike.

Both enjoyed outstanding junior careers, helping Jamaica win world under-20 titles. Tina has since established herself among the world’s leading senior sprinters. She won silver in the 100 metres at the 2025 World Athletics Championships in Tokyo before capturing the Diamond League Final title in Brussels in September 2026. Tia meanwhile has stepped out of her twin sister’s shadow and, at just age 19, placed a creditable seventh in the women’s 100m final at the Olympic Games.

Their development has been a significant part of MVP’s ongoing talent pipeline, making any potential departure noteworthy, even though no move has been confirmed.

The suggestion that Bennett could establish a new training group also raises broader questions about the next phase of Jamaican athletics, particularly as coaches seek to attract and retain elite athletes in an increasingly competitive professional environment.

It has been reported that promising hurdler Kerrica Hill has left MVP to join her high school coach Bennett. The two-time world Under-20 100 m champion’s departure is significant and follows that of Olympic bronze medallist Rasheed Broadbell, who joined the Lonnie Green coaching camp in the United States.

If the rumours prove true, the implications for MVP could extend beyond the loss of two talented sprinters. It would add to the pressure on the club to demonstrate that its coaching structure, athlete-development system and international appeal can endure beyond the man who built its reputation.

The challenge is whether MVP can successfully transition from a programme so closely identified with one influential coach into an organisation capable of sustaining its standards under new leadership.

For now, the Clayton twins’ future remains uncertain, and the reported Nike-backed Bennett project has yet to be confirmed. But the speculation has placed a spotlight on a bigger question: who will carry the MVP legacy forward in the post-Francis era?

World.title: ‘Cherish our heritage’
World.content:
Opposition Leader Mark Golding (right) shares a word with Minister of Culture Olivia Grange at the National Heritage Week Thanksgiving Service at Church of the Open Bible on Washington Boulevard, in St Andrew, on Sunday. At left is state minister in the Ministry of Industry, Investment and Commerce Delano Seiveright. (Photo: Karl Mclarty)

PASTOR of Lakes Pen Apostolic Church, Overseer Cassel Dunkley is urging Jamaicans to reclaim the everyday acts of kindness and respect that once brought communities together.

He argued that the country’s heritage is found not only in its national heroes, anthem, and history books, but also in the values passed down through generations as Jamaica confronts mounting challenges.

Dunkley, who was addressing the National Heritage Week Thanksgiving Church Service on Sunday at Church of the Open Bible on Washington Boulevard, in St Andrew, said Jamaica must preserve the traditions that taught people to care for their neighbours, help grieving families, and treat other people’s children as their own.

He recalled a time when a family experiencing a death could expect relatives and neighbours to arrive with food and other assistance, contrasting that tradition with what he described as a loss of community spirit.

“When somebody died in the country, granny came with a bunch of bananas, auntie came with something, cousin came with something.

Nowadays, when somebody dies, it becomes a party. We want beer, we want Red Stripe, and black stripe, and white stripe.

But I come from a heritage that when something happens, your neighbour is going to look out for you — [and] those are the things we want to get back to,” Dunkley said.

He also called for a return to the close community relationships in which neighbours shared responsibility for children and looked out for one another, regardless of whether they expected anything in return.

“We want to get back and cherish the heritage where your tears become my tears, when I try to do something to help you more than try to do something to belittle you,” he said.

Dunkley said Jamaica’s heritage must also be reflected in how people treat others. “We must cherish respect for all, irrespective of your belief.

We must learn to love, forgive, and respect each other. But sometimes we allow material things to shift our focus, and we judge people by the car they drive, we judge them by the place they live.

But remember… we are one blood,” he said. “Love those who can’t buy you a shirt.

Love those who can’t give you nothing in return. Because sometimes we only give to those who can give back to us, we only are kind to those who can be kind back to us.

But somebody around the corner is looking for your love, somebody who hurt you is looking and waiting for your forgiveness,” Dunkley said.

He argued that preserving the country’s heritage requires Jamaicans to remember the lessons taught by previous generations, including honesty, respect for others, and responsibility for the wider community.

Dunkley recalled how children were expected to return items they found if those items did not belong to them, saying such lessons should not be lost as the country develops.

“Do you remember the time in Jamaica when if you brought home a pen, your mother says, ‘Where did you get it from?’ and granny tied her head and said, ‘We are going to school with you in the morning because you have to give it back’? We couldn’t say ‘finders keepers’; we were taught to return the things that do not belong to us.

We cannot afford to lose that heritage,” he said. Beyond these everyday customs, Dunkley reminded the congregation of the sacrifices made by Jamaica’s national heroes and other leaders in shaping the country’s history.

Dunkley said Jamaicans have much to be thankful for, including the country’s educational institutions and the role the Church played and continues to play in society.

He urged Jamaicans not to allow negative news and the country’s problems to overshadow its achievements.

“But I borrow the words of [Governor General] Sir Patrick Allen. He said, ‘We can use what is right about Jamaica to fix what is not right,’ ” Dunkley said.

He also called for greater civic pride, including respect for the environment, and recalled school lessons that encouraged children to pick up litter and keep their surroundings clean.

Dunkley also called for Jamaica’s national anthem and pledge to be given greater prominence at public gatherings, arguing that the words and values they represent should remain part of the country’s everyday life.

He said Jamaica’s history and traditions should help guide the country through its present difficulties, adding that people must understand their past if they are to make sound decisions about the future.

“We must cherish our heritage! We might have different theological beliefs… but, brothers and sisters, we must embrace and understand where we are coming from — because if we don’t know where we are coming from we will not know where we are going,” said Dunkley.

World.title: PM wants security forces to get tougher on criminals
World.content:
HOLNESS...we must stop making excuses for men who carry illegal guns, terrorise communities, and prey upon the vulnerable.

PRIME Minister Dr Andrew Holness has urged the leadership of the Jamaica Constabulary Force (JCF) to intensify its efforts to go after criminal gangs and the people who support them.

Holness, who returned to the island on Saturday, was immediately briefed by Police Commissioner Dr Kevin Blake about the developments in the Five Miles area off the Sligoville main road in St Catherine which left five men — JCF members Corporal Trevoy Shaw, and Constable Devoney Rose; and civilians Errol Hussey, his son Malique Hussey, and nephew Javoun Cogle — dead, and a 10-year-old girl nursing a gunshot wound.

In his response Holness offered condolence to the families of the dead cops, the hope for the full recovery of the injured child, and expressed relief that other civilians who were in the house escaped unharmed.

The prime minister said the reports on the incident provide a stark reminder that Jamaica cannot let its guard down or relax the laws.

“We must maintain our resolute posture against organised criminal violence. The emerging accounts of this incident point to a disturbing level of planning and coordination. You reported that there was misdirection, diversionary gunfire from outside, [and] there was support and prearranged transport. All of this must be fully investigated.

“We must uncover and dismantle every person, every network, every resource, every facilitator who enabled this violence,” added Holness.

He said the police account also reveals something even more chilling, that the gunmen were willing to use members of their own households as shields to protect themselves.

“This is the kind of evil that we are confronted with in our society. These men had a choice, they could have put down their weapons, they could have surrendered and had their day in court. Instead they chose lethal violence,” Holness said.

“But let me be blunt, we must separate these evil men from our society. We must stop making excuses for men who carry illegal guns, terrorise communities, and prey upon the vulnerable. They are not protectors; they are not justified by poverty, exclusion, or social injustice. They are not freedom fighters, they are not Robin Hoods, they are not rebels or misunderstood victims. They are parasites and pestilence upon our society,” declared Holness.

According to the prime minister, these criminals are obstructions to the progress of the society, which is better off without them.

“They must be identified, disarmed, arrested, prosecuted, and removed from our communities through the full force and uncompromising force of the law. There can be no moral equivalency. There can be no romanticising of guns; no glorifying of gunmen; and no tolerance for those who shelter finance, arm, and celebrate them. We must never comfort ourselves with the illusion that organised terror cannot exist in our communities,” said Holness.

He said the attack on the security forces on Friday has shaken members but it has not diluted the resolve of both the JCF and the Jamaica Defence Force.

Holness said the National Security Council will have its regular monthly meeting this week during which it we will review the situation.

“But I can tell you from now, commissioner… the policy direction is that you should intensify the operations that you have planned to target the criminals, the gang leaders, those who you have been pursuing with intelligence.

“Bring them forward. Intensify it. Because what this has shown is a new level of criminal organisation that is a threat to our national security. Whatever resources you need, we will discuss it but you should make a big push now to get as many of these who are just lying in wait to confront and challenge the security of the country,” added Holness.

He argued that Friday’s incident in Five Miles must be used as a watershed and a turning point as it underscored that there are people with criminal intent and the capability and wherewithal to unleash terror on the society.

“And we must meet them head on. We must meet them head on and maintain our civility and the rule of law. So the word to all gunman: ‘Tek weh unnuself!’ ” declared Holness.

World.title: Police step up hunt for alleged killer ‘Papa’
World.content:
Alleged gang enforcer Kenroy “Papa” Williams who has been linked to at least five murders.

AN islandwide manhunt is now on for Kenroy “Papa” Willis who the police have described as a “high-risk target” linked to at least five murders committed across sections of St Andrew between May 2024 and May 2025.

Jamaica Observer sources say 25-year-old Willis was the main target of an early morning operation last Friday in the Five Miles area, off the Sligoville main road in St Catherine, which left five men dead and a 10-year-old girl nursing gunshot wounds.

The dead men have since been identified as Jamaica Constabulary Force (JCF) members Corporal Trevoy Shaw and Constable Devoney Rose; and civilians Errol Hussey, his son Malique Hussey, and nephew Javoun Cogle.

According to the Observer sources, Malique Hussey, otherwise called Mal Boss, is a known associate of Willis who is of a Rose Hall District, Lawrence Tavern, St Andrew, address.

Willis has been identified in the JCF’s Violence Producers Workbook as an alleged enforcer of the Rose Hall gang and a suspect in several serious violent crimes, including murder, shootings and robberies.

He is specifically wanted in connection with the October 26, 2024 murder of Verne Ewan Joseph along Essex Hall Main Road.

Willis has also been linked to the killing of Alexian Daley in Mahoney District, Lawrence Tavern, on May 26, 2024; Matthew Williams, who was killed at Lawrence Tavern Square on June 14, 2024; Oshane Blackwood, who was killed along Brooks Level Road, Stony Hill, on May 11, 2025.

Three of the five killings occurred within approximately five weeks in 2024, all in communities in and around Lawrence Tavern. The sources say the police are now targeting several locations where Willis may have sought refuge or maintained connections, including Golden Spring, Lawrence Tavern, Glengoffe in St Catherine, and Bull Bay and Clarks Hill in St Andrew. The police have previously conducted targeted raids as part of their efforts to locate Willis, and Friday’s operation was believed to be the latest move by the cops to nab him. The sources say there was gunfire in areas outside the zone the police had cordoned off during the operation, and they suspect this was an effort by Willis, or his cronies, to distract them while they were being fired on from inside the house. Willis has remained the subject of police interest throughout 2026, with published reports identifying him as wanted for murder and under investigation in connection with other violent crimes. “Willis’s reported gang affiliation, alleged involvement in multiple murders, and associations with other suspected violent offenders have made him a subject of sustained police interest,” added the Observer source.

World.title: NUFF offers more than enough
World.content:
From left: Nadean Rawlings, director, NUFF; Alisa Jones, production assistant, NUFF; and Jesse Royal, recording artiste (Aceion Cunningham)

Negril Universal Film Festival (NUFF), formerly known as the Skylark Film Festival, brought four days of Jamaican and international storytelling from Thursday, October 8, to Sunday, October 11.

The weekend paired film screenings with conversations, industry sessions, culture and hands-on learning, creating a gathering for audiences and emerging film-makers alike.

The festival, now in its 7th staging, opened with a special 25th-anniversary screening of Stephanie Black’s landmark documentary

Life and Debt. The film’s examination of Jamaica and the forces shaping its economy provided a fitting starting point for a conversation about the issues it raised and how they resonate a quarter-century later.

On Friday, the programme shifted from film-maker development by day to a celebration of Jamaican storytelling in the evening. The WES Studios-sponsored Vertical Film-making Masterclass, led by Richard Lawson of Hyperlens Studios, offered practical insight into a changing screen format. Documentary shorts and opportunities to learn, connect, and exchange ideas rounded out the daytime programme.

Friday night’s Jamaican Film Block gave way to a special Jimmy Cliff tribute featuring his daughter Odessa Chambers. Storm Saulter then presented the first two episodes of his new

SKY-TV series,

Possession. An in-depth conversation and question-and-answer session invited the audience to explore the series and its creative vision with the film-maker.

World.title: 149 outstanding Jamaicans to be honoured today
World.content:
Members of the Jamaica Defence Force in rehearsal on Saturday for today’s Ceremony of Investiture and Presentation of National Honours and Awards at King’s House. (Photos: Naphtali Junior)

Six Jamaicans will receive the nation’s fifth highest honour, the Order of Jamaica (OJ), at the 2026 Ceremony of Investiture and Presentation of National Honours and Awards today at King’s House.

They are the former Bank of Jamaica Governor Richard Byles; Minister of Energy, Transport and Telecommunications Daryl Vaz; Chief Executive Officer of Sagicor Group Jamaica Christopher Zacca; philanthropist Donette Chin-Loy Chang; former Government minister Maxine Henry-Wilson; and former Government minister Derrick Smith.

They will be among the 140 Jamaicans who will be recognised for their sterling contribution to nation-building. The ceremony is scheduled to take place on the lawns of King’s House, starting at 9:00 am.

Twenty-five people will be conferred with the Order of Distinction in the rank of Commander; 41 with the Order of Distinction in the rank of Officer; 33 with the Badge of Honour for Meritorious Service; and 30 with the Badge of Honour for Long and Faithful Service.

Three civilians will receive the Badge of Honour for Gallantry. They are Danielle Anna-Marie Barnswell and her husband, Councillor Scean Barnswell, as well as Susan Annmarie Higgins.

As customary, several members of the unformed groups will be awarded with the Medal of Honour for Meritorious Service — 25 from the Jamaica Constabulary Force; 13 from the Department of Correctional Service; 15 from the Jamaica Fire Brigade; and 12 from the Jamaica Defence Force.

The ceremony will be presided over by Governor General Sir Patrick Allen. Under the National Honours and Awards Act, promulgated on July 18, 1969, provision is made for those outstanding Jamaicans to be conferred with one of the honours of the Orders of the six Societies of Honour.

The six honours by rank are Order of National Hero, Order of the Nation, Order of Excellence, Order of Merit, Order of Jamaica, and the Order of Distinction. There is also the Medal of Honour and Badge of Honour, which recognises gallantry and meritorious service.

World.title: French riots lay bare risks and opportunities for 2027 election candidates
World.content:
Police officers stand near a fire during an unauthorized demonstration marked by riots and clashes with law enforcement at Place de la Republique in Paris on October 18, 2026. | Gauthier Bedrignans/Hans Lucas/AFP via Getty Images

PARIS — Looting and rioting across France over the weekend are threatening to reshape the contours of the French presidential race.

Far-right frontrunner Marine Le Pen is seizing on the crisis to cast herself as the candidate of law and order, but there are risks for her too. Many voters see her as a highly divisive leader whose 2027 victory would only deepen the societal fault lines exposed by the riots.

Far-left firebrand Jean-Luc Mélenchon, widely tipped to challenge Le Pen in the second round next year, is also treading carefully as rivals accuse him of encouraging the rage on the streets that has morphed into pillaging and arson.

World.title: Spanish left-wing chaos dampens Sánchez’s hopes of election miracle
World.content:
With negotiations stuttering, an exasperated Mónica García, health minister and candidate for the left-wing Broad Front, warned on social media that the left risked getting “trapped in egos, worries, internal disputes and electoral and/or personal calculations that are good for nobody except the right.”

The Broad Front took shape shortly after the election was called in order to bring together several parties to the left of Sánchez. But after several days of frantic discussions, prominent left-wing party Podemos did not join the united ticket — except in the Canary Islands and the Valencia region — hampering the far left’s overall electoral prospects.

“The only way for [Sánchez] to be able to govern again is for there to be a strong presence to the left of the Socialists,” said Kiko Llaneras, polling analyst for media outlet El País, who pointed out that “the Broad Front isn’t actually that broad.”

He added, “The big question is whether this new movement will be strong enough to allow the left to form a majority — and that’s going to be very difficult.”

Defying the odds

The Broad Front is made up of Sumar, the junior partner in the current Socialist-led government; the Catalan Comuns; the communist-led United Left (IU); Más Madrid; and an array of regional left-wing parties. The lead candidate of the ticket will be Ada Colau, the former mayor of Barcelona.

Spain’s electoral system rewards united platforms, and the Broad Front is not as inclusive as a similar alliance — created in 2023 and including Podemos — which helped Sánchez defy the odds and form a new administration after the last election.

World.title: Trump says he is open to trilateral summit with Putin and Xi
World.content:
The president told reporters that such a meeting would focus on denuclearization, not the war in Ukraine as Moscow had suggested earlier.

President Donald Trump said Monday he was open to a trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, but said such a meeting would not focus on the war in Ukraine.

Trump told reporters at the White House that he would participate in a summit with both leaders if the purpose was to discuss denuclearization. The comments came after reports that Putin had proposed that the three leaders meet on the sidelines of next month’s APEC summit in China to discuss how to end the war in Ukraine.

“I would do it, not so much for Ukraine,” Trump said. “Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine. They have not been doing much. And the same thing with China. We would have it to talk about nuclear weapons, denuclearization. And anytime I can have a meeting on denuclearization.”

World.title: EU Parliament launches probe into fake email seeking to sway internal election
World.content:
The email disparaged the work of Portuguese EPP lawmaker Sebastião Bugalho ahead of the EPP’s vice-chair elections. When asked, Bugalho’s office said he “will obviously not comment on forged emails.”

Pedro López de Pablo, the EPP’s press director, said: “The group has been informed that there will be an investigation.”

The Parliament’s probe was announced by EPP group chair Manfred Weber to all the group’s lawmakers at a closed-door meeting on Monday afternoon, according to four people in the room. They were granted anonymity to discuss the sensitive internal matter.

Halicki sent his request for an investigation by Belgian authorities to Parliament President Roberta Metsola on Friday. “As I know, the Parliament immediately reacted, and the investigation has been launched,” he said, referring to the internal probe.

The email comes amid a fierce campaign for the EPP’s vice-chair positions, which are to be voted on on Tuesday. Twelve lawmakers, including Bugalho and Halicki, are battling it out for 10 spots.

CORRECTION: An earlier version of this report misstated Pedro López de Pablo’s role. This article was updated Oct. 19 to correct his title to press director.

World.title: After looting spree, France tells online resellers to crack down on traffic of stolen goods
World.content:
During a government press conference earlier in the day, Minister for Small Businesses Serge Papin said officials were working on “coordination between investigators and online platforms” to identify the individuals behind suspicious listings. A specific protocol is expected to be put in place, according to a government source speaking to POLITICO.

A spokesperson for Vinted France said the sale of stolen goods, or soliciting the purchase of such goods, is strictly prohibited on the platform. "We have a zero-tolerance policy on this matter," said the company representative. "Since this past weekend, our teams have taken immediate action to identify and remove listings that may involve stolen goods, and we have stepped up our monitoring of suspicious listings."

Other platforms weren't immediately available for comment.

The discussions with the reselling websites are also likely to touch on longer-term questions around platform responsibility and the monitoring of illicit trade within the EU’s digital marketplace.

The issue of looted goods sold on online marketplaces “is a new dimension and the Commission is happy to look at it in collaboration with French authorities," European Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier told POLITICO.

French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has instructed local authorities to enact “partial curfews” Monday evening to prevent further looting and rioting. Papin said a “special support fund” will be set up to provide financial assistance to the estimated 3,000 local businesses affected by the weekend’s unrest.

Eliza Gkritsi contributed to this report.

World.title: EU’s ‘trust’ and ‘leverage’ at stake over development cuts, UN food aid boss warns
World.content:
Record need for aid

Funding cuts to the organization come when the need for its programs has never been higher. According to WFP projections, as many as 363 million people could face acute food insecurity this year — nearly 90% more than in 2021.

“We see the consequences of the cuts that we're now going through. They are human, because we are cutting [food programs for] women and children, who are likely to die in South Sudan, in Afghanistan, in Somalia, off our support because of these deep funding cuts we've been going through,” said Skau.



The world’s largest food aid agency is now running dangerously short of cash and has to make “impossible choices,” such as “choosing between the starving,” Skau said. Moreover, wars, extreme weather, the looming threat of El Niño and disruptions to global trade routes are deepening hunger crises worldwide.

Some officials previously warned that cuts to development aid risk fueling more migration into Europe, something Brussels has been trying to curb.



“I would not put that as my main argument, but there is a clear linkage," said Skau. “And if that's what it takes to get the resources needed to save lives in South Sudan, you know, fair enough,” he added.

Skau is serving as WFP’s interim chief following Cindy McCain’s departure. He is set to hand over to Luke Lindberg at the end of October.

World.title: UK and Poland accuse Hegseth of downplaying allies’ role in Afghanistan
World.content:
But he added: “Except there were maybe five that contributed. It was actually closer to one or two that by the end were actually involved in kinetic operations. In fact the patch ISAF, we joked it meant ‘I Saw Americans Fighting’.”

All of NATO’s then-28 members participated in the U.S.-led war in Afghanistan, after the alliance invoked Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty – NATO’s collective defense clause – on September 12, 2001, a day after the terrorist attacks that took place on 9/11.

It remains the only time the article has been invoked in alliance history.

Asked about his comments Monday, U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s official spokesperson pointed out that “thousands of British and allied families made huge sacrifices to play their significant part in that war and uphold our values,” while “more than 450 British personnel never returned.”

“Their sacrifice and that of other NATO forces was made in the service of collective security and in response to an attack on our ally,” he continued.

“We are incredibly proud of our armed forces, and their service and sacrifice will never be forgotten. And it is wrong to diminish their role.”

World.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang warns Germany is falling behind in AI race
World.content:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang warned that Germany is falling behind in the artificial intelligence race as he spoke to members of the media in London last week.

 

Despite its strong potential and wealth of talent, Huang believes progress in Europe is being blocked by too much hesitation and analysis and has called on policymakers to be quicker to put AI into practice.

In response to concerns about the country's technological competitiveness, the German government has been planning closer cooperation with the US company.

At the Invest in Germany investment summit in Berlin this week, Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Huang are set to unveil a joint AI pact intended to speed up the integration of AI products across German industry.

The German government is preparing to commit hundreds of millions of Euros to the initiative.

Alongside start-up Black Forest Labs, around 10 established German companies including Siemens and Audi are expected to take part.

The partnership builds on the Sovereign Open Source Foundation Models initiative, an alliance dedicated to developing powerful open-source AI systems.

The funding is to be used primarily to buy computing capacity in Deutsche Telekom's Industrial AI Cloud, which is equipped with Nvidia's latest Blackwell hardware.

The government hopes the investment will make Germany a more attractive destination for innovation and technological development.

On Tuesday, senior international executives, investors and government officials at the Invest in Germany summit will discuss new investment in Germany, focusing on artificial intelligence, energy and infrastructure, as well as the competitiveness of the German economy.

World.title: Pope Leo XIV holds call with Zelenskyy, Vatican says
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV held a call with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy late on Monday afternoon, just days after he spoke with Russian leader Vladimir Putin, the Vatican said.

 

During his conversation with Putin, the pontiff had called for a humanitarian truce in Oleshky, a city under Russian siege, to allow food and medical aid to arrive and for civilians to be evacuated safely.

According to a statement from the Vatican's Press Office, Oleshky was also the focus of his talks with Zelenskyy.

"During the conversation, the Holy Father drew attention to the serious situation in the city of Oleshky, in the Kherson region, referring to the request for a humanitarian truce already submitted to the President of the Russian Federation," the statement reads. "The Holy Father expressed the hope that the cooperation of both sides will allow food and medical aid to reach the city and ensure the voluntary and safe evacuation of the civilian population."

Ukraine and Russia are in the process of finalising the details of a civilian evacuation in the city and six nearby settlements, the Ukrainian Commissioner for Human Rights, Dmytro Lubinets, has announced.

Chicago-born Leo has kept in regular contact with Zelenskyy.

In May 2025, Leo held an initial telephone call with the Ukrainian leader, in which Zelenskyy invited him to Kyiv and reiterated his country's readiness for further negotiations.

The two met later that month, immediately after the mass marking the beginning of the pope's pontificate in St Peter's Square.

They met again on 9 July 2025 for a private audience at Villa Barberini, the papal residence in Castel Gandolfo, where they discussed the possibility of hosting future peace talks at the Vatican.

And once again on 9 December, again in Castel Gandolfo, to discuss the need to keep dialogue open, questions surrounding prisoners of war and the return of Ukrainian children deported to Russia.

On 3 April this year, the pope again spoke to Zelenskyy as Russian drone and missile attacks ramped up across Ukraine.

He expressed his solidarity with the Ukrainian people, underlining the urgency of humanitarian aid, the release of prisoners and a negotiated peace.

World.title: Video: Priest dies after cross falls on him during Mass in Ecuador
World.content:
Ecuadorian priest Patricio Sánchez died after a large cross fell on him while he was celebrating Mass at a church in Guayaquil on Saturday evening.

 

Footage captured the moment the cross came loose from the wall behind the altar and struck Sánchez as he addressed the congregation.

The service was being streamed live on social media. The Archdiocese of Guayaquil later confirmed his death and expressed its condolences to the religious congregation he belonged to.

A memorial Mass was held at the church on Sunday, attended by clergy and parishioners.

World.title: Cristiano Ronaldo suspended for 30 days after quitting Portugal camp
World.content:
Portugal legend Cristiano Ronaldo has been given a 30-day suspension by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) after leaving an international camp last month.

 

In addition to the ban, Ronaldo will have to pay a fine of €255.

According to a ruling by the association's disciplinary committee, part of the player’s suspension has already been served, as he had already been suspended.

Ronaldo, who now plays his club football for Saudi side Al-Nassr, began his punishment on 1 October, leaving 11 days left to serve. That means he could be available for the national team’s upcoming matches against Denmark on 14 November and Wales on 17 November.

'Mitigating circumstances'

The ruling said Ronaldo had asked that "mitigating circumstances be taken into account," in particular his "lack of any disciplinary record in the current season and the previous three seasons, provision of services of relevance to football, commendations for sporting merit and contribution to establishing the material truth."

"With regard to the mitigating circumstances of providing services of relevance to football and commendations for sporting merit, the defendant Cristiano Ronaldo submitted his sporting CV, including the awards and recognitions he has received over the course of his career," the document reads.

It adds that, in terms of "contribution to establishing the material truth," the player referred to the statement published on his Instagram page on 6 October.

Related Cristiano Ronaldo suspended by Portuguese FA for leaving training camp

The ruling sets out in detail the sequence of events after Ronaldo left the training camp.

On 30 September, the former Real Madrid and Manchester United star walked out of a camp before a training session at Parken Stadium in Copenhagen.

The player is said to have left without notifying anyone from the FPF or the squad in advance.

The document states that the player informed FPF President Pedro Proença of his decision by phone, saying that he did not feel in the right frame of mind to play.

"During the aforementioned telephone conversation, the defendant player informed the president of the FPF that he was not in an emotional condition to remain with the National Team at the training camp," the disciplinary committee noted.

Media coverage

In assessing the case, the committee acknowledged Ronaldo's services to football and his multiple awards. The body also took into account "his conduct after the events, in particular the remorse shown in the statement of 06.10.2026."

Even though certain mitigating factors were recognised, there were also aggravating elements in the FPF's view, notably the media coverage of the case and his role as team captain.

World.title: Deadly floods sweep through eastern Spain after torrential rain
World.content:
Torrential rain caused severe flooding in eastern Spain, leaving at least four people dead and prompting more than 400 rescues in the Valencia region.

 

Floodwaters swept away parked cars, submerged roads and left some residents stranded, with emergency crews airlifting people to safety.

In Oliva, one of the worst-hit areas, two people died, including a 79-year-old woman found at home.

Authorities ordered around 100 municipalities to remain indoors for several hours as heavy rain battered the Mediterranean coast. Most restrictions were lifted by early Monday afternoon as conditions improved.

World.title: Rubio puts Trans-Caspian trade and critical minerals at centre of Central Asia talks
World.content:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and the foreign ministers of five Central Asian countries agreed to deepen cooperation on transport, critical minerals and security at a C5+1 meeting in Samarkand on Monday.

 

The talks brought together the United States, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. In a joint statement, they backed investment in the Trans-Caspian trade route, closer industrial cooperation and simpler customs procedures.

A trade route to Europe

The Trans-Caspian route, also known as the Middle Corridor, connects Central Asia with European markets through the Caspian Sea, the South Caucasus and Turkey, bypassing Russia.

"We're going to enhance the infrastructure of the Trans Caspian trade route and give our partners more ways to reach American and Central Asian markets," Rubio said.

Washington also wants to diversify supplies of critical minerals used in energy technologies and advanced manufacturing. The six governments identified mineral processing, energy cooperation and cybersecurity among their priorities, but the joint statement gave no figures for new infrastructure funding.

C5+1 ministerial meeting in Samarkand Uzbekistan Kylie Cooper/Pool Photo via AP

Uzbek Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov proposed cooperation extending from mineral exploration to processing and local industrial clusters. He also called for closer links between the C5+1 diplomatic forum and the B5+1 business platform to involve companies in identifying projects.

The US push comes as the five Central Asian states maintain extensive economic ties with Russia and China. Speaking separately to Euronews in Samarkand, Rubio said Washington was seeking competition, not exclusivity.

"This is not about coming here to say, stop talking to somebody else or stop working with some other country," he told Euronews.

Bilateral talks with the five ministers

Rubio also held separate meetings with each of his Central Asian counterparts.

Kazakhstan's Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi discussed trade, energy, critical minerals and technology with Rubio. Kazakhstan's Foreign Ministry said the US Secretary of State expressed interest in visiting the country after the G20 summit in Miami in December, although no date was announced.

The US State Department said they also discussed Kazakhstan's commitment to join the Abraham Accords, a US-backed framework for normalising relations with Israel.

Rubio also met Kyrgyzstan's Foreign Minister Jeenbek Kulubaev to discuss bilateral cooperation. Tajik Foreign Minister Sirojiddin Muhriddin raised trade, investment and regional security, according to his ministry.

Rubio held talks with Turkmenistan's Rashid Meredov, with the two countries preparing another round of political consultations in Ashgabat in November.

Uzbekistan and the US held the first session of their Enhanced Strategic Partnership Dialogue, covering trade, energy, technology and security. Following the talks, Foreign Minister Saidov signed the Artemis Accords in Rubio's presence, making Uzbekistan the 77th country to join the international framework for peaceful space exploration.

World.title: Lavrov backs Iran, hours after Trump says Russia doing 'very little' to help Tehran
World.content:
"I am confident that Iran's cause, like Russia's, is a just cause," Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said on Monday at a joint press conference in Tehran with his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Araghchi.

 

Lavrov accused Washington and Israel of launching what he described as an unprovoked military campaign against the country whilst reaffirming Moscow's commitment to continue supporting Tehran.

His remarks came hours after US President Donald Trump defended easing economic pressure on Moscow, arguing that further sanctions could jeopardise negotiations to end the war in Ukraine. He said he also wanted to ensure that Russia did not provide further support for Iran.

"Russia is doing very little, if anything, to help the Islamic Republic of Iran, compared to what they could be doing, and I want to keep it that way," Trump wrote on Truth Social on Sunday.

The US president said he did not want to risk driving Russia away from the negotiating table by imposing further economic pressure, despite criticism of his recent decision to waive some sanctions targeting Moscow.

"I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don't want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table," Trump wrote.

Moscow pledges continued support for Tehran

Lavrov said Russia remained willing to help find a diplomatic solution to the conflict between Iran and the US and Israel, which he characterised as a crisis caused by US and Israeli military action.

"We once again expressed our country's readiness to assist in finding mutually acceptable solutions to overcome this man-made crisis," he said, according to remarks reported by Kremlin-controlled media.

He welcomed Tehran's stated willingness to pursue diplomacy and called for a return to conditions that prevailed before the conflict in the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, including restoring freedom of navigation and securing guarantees against renewed military action.

Lavrov also claimed Moscow had worked at the United Nations to prevent attempts to justify US and Israeli strikes against Iran, whilst providing humanitarian assistance, including medicines and regular food shipments.

Beyond diplomatic support, he made clear that Russia had no intention of abandoning its economic relationship with Tehran.

"Despite the difficult circumstances, Russia does not intend to abandon the implementation of agreements with Iran in the economic and investment spheres," Lavrov said.

Trump defends easing pressure on Moscow

In the same Truth Social post, Trump also directed fresh criticism at Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, accusing him of damaging global diesel markets by continuing Ukrainian strikes against Russian oil refineries.

Trump claimed it was Kyiv's attacks and not Moscow's invasion or Washington's war on Iran that was hurting American farmers, businesses and consumers, as he praised Russia for agreeing to supply diesel to international markets at relatively low prices.

He also accused Zelenskyy of having little interest in ending the war, suggesting that Ukraine had missed earlier opportunities to negotiate a more favourable settlement.

His comments followed Washington's decision to waive a new sanctions package targeting Russia and to ease restrictions on Russian diesel, measures that have drawn criticism over their potential to provide Moscow with additional revenue whilst its war against Ukraine continues.

The White House has defended its approach as part of efforts to preserve peace negotiations and relieve pressure on global fuel markets.

World.title: 'How are we supposed to recover?': Shopkeepers react to looting and destruction across France
World.content:
France is reeling after violent clashes and looting during nationwide protests over the cost of living and school conditions. In Paris, Lille, Lyon, Marseille and other cities, damaged shops, smashed windows and burnt debris marked the aftermath.

 

Shopkeepers condemned the destruction, saying it traumatised staff and threatened family-run businesses, while others stressed that violence undermined the protesters' cause.

Cleanup crews and residents worked to clear the streets as the country assessed the damage from one of its worst episodes of unrest in recent years. Watch the video for more.

World.title: Shipping attacks threaten Turkey's resolve to keep warships out of Black Sea
World.content:
A wave of deadly attacks on cargo ships in the waters of NATO members Bulgaria and Romania has jolted the alliance into calling an emergency meeting on Black Sea security. Yet any move to send NATO ships hinges on Turkey reversing its steadfast refusal to allow warships into the Black Sea.

Advertising

Thursday saw two chemical tankers struck by drones close to a Romanian port.

It follows two similar attacks in Bulgarian waters in the past week. More than 20 sailors have been killed or remain missing.

“The war has come in full force to the Black Sea now,” said Yoruk Isik, a maritime analyst who runs the Istanbul-based Bosphorus Observer consultancy. “With the change in technology compared to the beginning of the war, drones really disrupted maritime traffic.”

According to Isik, the latest attacks underscore the growing spread of the conflict between Russia and Ukraine. “Russian ports and Ukrainian ports are heavily targeted, but now even in NATO waters ships are getting hit, in Bulgarian waters, Romanian waters.

“We are at a point where there is no safe place.”

The latest strikes targeted vessels along a key Ukrainian shipping route, casting Russia as NATO’s prime suspect as Moscow intensifies its assault on Ukrainian trade.

After meeting on Thursday with the leaders of Bulgaria and Romania, both NATO members, Secretary-General Mark Rutte said the military alliance would “continue to work closely with our allies in the Black Sea, adjusting our deterrence and defence posture as needed”.

Romanian President Nicușor Dan said NATO would hold a crisis meeting next week to discuss the situation.

Gatekeeper to the Black Sea

NATO could deploy air defence systems against drones to protect Bulgarian and Romanian waters.

But any deployment of naval ships will depend on NATO member Turkey, which controls access to the Black Sea through the Turkish Straits under a long-standing international treaty, the 1936 Montreux Convention.

Since Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022, Ankara has blocked entry of Russian and Ukrainian warships or military vessels belonging to NATO members without a Black Sea coast, arguing for a diplomatic solution.

In recent weeks the Turkish government has sought to broker a ceasefire on commercial shipping, without success. Isik claims that failure, coupled with the latest escalation in attacks, is increasingly calling into question Ankara’s reliance on diplomacy alone.

“Either they’re going to have a breakthrough and the Kremlin is going to de-escalate, or Ankara is going to accept the reality that there needs to be a more credible force here – bigger vessels have to come,” the analyst said.

He pointed out that the navies of Romania and Bulgaria are not equipped to handle such an operation alone, with Cold War-era ships nearing the end of their lifespan.

“So Turkey's engagement is key to any successful NATO planning in the Black Sea.”

Russian leverage

Despite Turkish-owned cargo ships coming under attack in recent weeks, and Turkey’s deep reliance on Black Sea trade, Ankara has so far kept its powerful navy on the sidelines.

International relations expert Huseyin Bagci, of Ankara’s Middle East Technical University, says Turkey fears an escalation in the conflict and will be wary of allowing NATO ships into the Black Sea.

“I do not think the government would dare,” said Bagci. “Probably the government considers this a provocation to drag Turkey into the war... Turkey is afraid of getting involved in the Black Sea against Russia, this is somehow a trauma in the Turkish mind.”

Moscow also retains powerful leverage over Ankara, he suggested.

Russia’s state nuclear company Rosatom is about to complete a multi-billion-dollar nuclear power station in Akkuyu, southern Turkey. Ankara sees it as vital to the drive to reduce its heavy dependence on imported energy. “It is illogical to oppose Russia now while you let the Russians complete the nuclear plant,” said Bagci.

Erdogan hints at larger nuclear partnership with Russia, unsettling Turkey's allies

Ankara also knows that letting NATO vessels in while barring Russian warships could provoke Moscow into contesting Turkey’s prized status as the gatekeeper to the Black Sea.

However, retired Turkish diplomat Selim Kuneralp, an expert on the Montreux Convention, warns Turkey’s control over Black Sea access is likely already in Russian President Vladimir Putin’s sights.

“This has probably had an impact on Russia’s ability to conduct the war, and I doubt that Putin is very happy with the situation,” said Kuneralp. “So if he were to win the war, there is a very strong risk that he will take the initiative of saying: ‘this is unacceptable and we want to have free passage of warships from now on, regardless of whether there is a war’.”

As a signatory, Moscow has the right to call for a revision of the Montreux Convention every five years.

For centuries, Russia fought repeated wars with the then Ottoman Empire for control of the Turkish Straits. In the early years of the Cold War, even Joseph Stalin tried his hand, but the United States intervened and thwarted him.

Now Ankara walks a tightrope between Moscow and its NATO partners to avoid a resurrection of those historical rivalries.
