World.title: AI recordings of doctor-patient conversations the new norm for Estonian hospitals
World.content:
Artificial intelligence systems that record conversations between patients and doctors, produce written summaries and help physicians make diagnoses and recommend next steps are already a reality in a number of hospitals.

Confido CEO Edvard Garder told ERR that the company began testing AI solutions last year, making it one of the first in Estonia to do so.

"The solution is now in use in several departments and we plan to roll it out across the entire organization. Patients have responded positively to the solution because doctors have more time to spend with them," Garder said.

Narva Hospital is currently seeking Estonian-language speech recognition and transcription software through a public procurement process. The software would convert conversations between doctors or nurses and patients into electronic text that can be processed, automatically translated, played back and stored.

Narva Hospital also wants the AI assistant to suggest medical codes and support doctors in making decisions. However, the procurement requirements emphasize that doctors must remain the decision-makers in all processes. AI-generated content that has not been reviewed and approved by a healthcare professional must not be entered into patients' medical records.

Tartu University Hospital began testing AI in its emergency department in mid-October and plans to continue the trial for three months. If the technology proves useful, the hospital will extend the trial period to obtain definitive confirmation of the application's benefits.

"The aim of using the EMO24 application is to reduce the time doctors and nurses spend on documentation. It also helps eliminate duplication where patients have to describe their condition to different staff members multiple times," said Aime Keis, head of the hospital's emergency department.

Heba Clinic also uses AI to compile patients' medical histories before appointments, document conversations during visits and subsequently prepare summaries and explanations for patients.

Heba Clinic CEO Ain Aaviksoo noted in an opinion article (in Estonian — ed.) published by ERR last week that AI cannot make decisions on behalf of doctors but should support solutions that help people manage their own health and enable doctors to assist them in doing so.

Every hospital looking for its own AI assistant

The Ministry of Social Affairs has not conducted a comprehensive assessment of the current use of artificial intelligence solutions across all hospitals, said Nele Labi, the ministry's deputy secretary general for innovation. However, the ministry is aware of several initiatives.

"We see that private hospitals have generally made the fastest progress in testing new solutions," Labi added.

According to Labi, there is no unified nationwide system to help hospitals streamline their work using AI and hospitals are largely seeking solutions independently based on their own needs.

"At the national level, however, two major AI-based solutions are currently under development: a transcription tool for family medicine and a transcription tool for the electronic ambulance system. The state has several other AI projects, but these two are expected to have the greatest impact on healthcare professionals' administrative workload in the near future," the deputy secretary general said.

Confido's CEO noted that healthcare professionals welcome the opportunities offered by AI and that skepticism is relatively rare. According to Garder, there is no significant difference between medical specialties in terms of the potential benefits as automated transcription tools and clinical decision support systems can reduce the documentation burden in virtually every field.

"This gives doctors more time for direct interaction with patients and also means that discharge summaries and other medical reports reach the national health portal more quickly," he said.

However, adopting AI does not mean immediate cost savings for hospitals, as initial investments are required. Garder nevertheless believes the technology will help reduce workloads and burnout among doctors and nurses, although the financial benefits of improved employee well-being cannot always be measured precisely.

The Ministry of Social Affairs also confirmed that projects in other European countries have clearly demonstrated the positive impact of such solutions in reducing administrative workloads.

"Estonia's approach is to seamlessly integrate general-purpose tools such as speech recognition and transcription into our hospitals' workflows so that medical professionals can spend their time on patients rather than paperwork," the deputy secretary general said.

Patients must be notified of AI involvement

A separate question is how to ensure that information exchanged between patients and doctors remains confidential and does not fall into the wrong hands.

According to Garder, Confido considers the solutions it currently uses to be secure and continues to do everything possible to mitigate potential risks. Nevertheless, Confido patients have the option to decline the use of AI during their appointments.

Tartu University Hospital also said participation in its AI pilot project is voluntary. If an emergency department patient does not wish to use the application, information gathering, diagnosis and treatment will proceed as before.

The Ministry of Social Affairs' deputy secretary general confirmed that strict data protection rules apply to the processing of such information and that patients must be informed about recordings and their purpose.

"However, because the technology is developing very rapidly, we need greater legal clarity and must ensure that patients understand how it is used and that the process is transparent. Working groups have already been established at the ministry to address this issue," Labi said.

Confido's CEO believes the state should develop a standard for security criteria. However, Garder does not consider it necessary for the state to develop a single AI solution for all healthcare institutions.

"Especially since tying all healthcare providers to a single system would create a monopoly and stifle innovation. Moreover, I'm not sure that would be the most efficient use of public funds," Garder said.

Instead, he believes the state should focus on ensuring that all data in the national health portal can be processed by AI, which would in turn speed up preparations for medical appointments.

"At present, the state is clearly moving far too slowly in adopting AI," the Confido CEO said.

World.title: 1,200-year-old archaeological site discovered Iraq’s Babil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The central Iraqi province of Babil announced on Sunday that an exciting archaeological site has been discovered.

Located in the al-Qasim district in the southern part of the province, the remains are believed to date back to the Abbasid era, a period of immense cultural, scientific, and architectural prosperity throughout Iraq.

The Governor of Babil, Ali al-Jamali, conducted an official site visit to examine the structural features, evaluate its historical context, and lay out administrative frameworks to safeguard the artifacts under strict national archaeological laws.

Local officials stressed that this discovery goes much beyond the previous statistics. Professional excavations and investigations are likely to provide additional details about ancient life centuries ago.

Officials are investigating legal alternatives for securely developing the area into a significant tourist destination, raising Babil’s global historical prominence.

The recent announcement follows the discovery of a large ancient city in Basra, dating back 1,200 years, as well as the uncovering of hundreds of ancient Islamic and Hellenistic artifacts revealed by rain at the Borsippa site, both occurring in 2025. This adds to a remarkable series of historical discoveries in Iraq.

The newly discovered archaeological site in Babil’s al-Qasim district provides a crucial physical link to the vast networks that powered the Islamic Golden Age. During the Abbasid era, Iraq was the undisputed geopolitical and economic center of the Islamic world.

World.title: Iraq increases oil exports to 3.4 million barrels per day
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Minister of Oil Basim Khudair said on Monday that the export rate during October has risen to 3.4 million barrels per day through three routes, including the Strait of Hormuz.

Iraq’s crude oil export in October surpassed 3.4 million barrels per day through the Strait of Hormuz, the Turkish port of Ceyhan, and the Syrian port of Baniyas, according to Khudair.

Despite the military conflict in the Strait of Hormuz, the Iraqi Ministry of Oil—through the State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO)—has managed to maintain an average export rate of three million barrels per day over the past nine months, according to the oil minister.

However, since the beginning of October, the export rate has risen to over 3.4 million barrels per day, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

The Ministry of Oil is trying to boost export capacity, which will provide financial revenue for the state. Khudair noted that developing export capacity will allow the government to carry out its tasks and secure the required funds for different governmental expenditures.

Khudair noted that crude oil exports are directed to European and Asian markets, as well as the American market.

Eco Iraq revealed on Saturday that oil production during September reached its highest daily average since the beginning of 2026, at 4.39 million barrels per day.

Iraq’s oil output stayed at normal levels in January and February, averaging more than 4.1 million barrels per day, before falling drastically in March as a result of the war in the region.

Iraq’s average daily oil output was 4.09 million barrels in January and 4.14 million barrels in February before falling to 1.9 million barrels in March and 1.63 million in April.

In May, the country’s oil production fell to 1.4 million barrels per day before rising to 1.52 million in June.

The improvement in oil output continued until the third quarter of the year. According to figures from OPEC, average output increased to 2.9 million barrels per day in July, 3.74 million barrels per day in August, and 4.39 million barrels per day in September.

World.title: Iraq, World Bank discuss financing strategic projects
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Finance Minister Faleh Sari and World Bank Group Vice President for the Middle East and North Africa Ousmane Dione discussed on Thursday financing strategic projects and support for economic reforms in Iraq.

The meeting took place on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group, held in Bangkok, Thailand, according to a statement released by the Finance Ministry.

Sari stressed the World Bank’s role in Iraq’s economic and financial transformation. He outlined the country’s desire to use the World Bank’s expertise and financial contributions to carry out significant projects in the energy, education, transportation, and digital transformation sectors.

The step aims to promote sustainable development and improve the efficiency of public services in Iraq, according to Sari.

Dione praised the collaboration with the Iraqi Finance Ministry, indicating that it has efficiently arranged its operational and communication mechanisms with the World Bank.

The World Bank official highlighted that the efforts of the Iraqi government pave the way for additional initiatives to support the country’s economic and financial goals in the upcoming period.

Sari reaffirmed last week Iraq’s commitment to continuing economic and financial reforms, diversifying revenue sources, and strengthening the role of the private sector.

According to Sari, these measures aim to bolster economic stability and enhance the country’s capacity to deal with regional challenges.

Sari noted that the government is addressing the economic consequences of the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz by reprioritizing expenditures, increasing non-oil revenues, and maintaining the state’s essential obligations while pursuing structural reforms.

“Iraq Vision 2050” represents a strategic plan for reducing dependency on oil, broadening production, empowering the private sector, and achieving inclusive and sustainable economic growth, according to Sari.

The minister noted that the reform package includes enhancing public financial management, automating customs and tax operations, boosting the business and investment climate, upgrading the banking sector, and increasing electronic payment systems.

According to Sari, the partnership with the IMF and the World Bank Group supports the economic and financial reform program.

World.title: Chinese oilfield service firm markets Iraq’s oil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – China-based Anton Oilfield Services Group has sold its first Iraqi crude oil shipment as part of a new supply deal with the State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO).

According to Reuters, the unique arrangement with one of a few Chinese independent oil corporations expanding their activities in Iraq enables Baghdad to access cash to pay service suppliers.

Iraq is attempting to bolster oil exports impacted by the military conflict in the Middle East. In the past few months, greater discounts have enticed traders and refiners, leading to a resurgence in its oil shipments.

The Chinese firm said in a statement on Saturday that the agreement intends to improve Basra Oil Company’s (BOC) crude oil sales and cash flow, provide channels for engineering and services, and expedite payment collection for Anton and partners.

An official in the oil sector indicated that Anton struck an agreement with SOMO to market undetermined amounts of Iraqi crude oil, mostly from the Majnoon oilfield managed by BOC.

In late September, Anton marketed one million barrels of Basra Heavy crude to a trading company.

Anton mentioned that the agreement with SOMO allows it to sell oil from the Dhufriya oilfield in eastern Iraq, where it received a license in 2024 to develop the field.

World.title: Iraq inaugurates first satellite ground station
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Minister of Communications Mustafa Sanad inaugurated on Sunday Iraq’s first satellite ground station in Baghdad, a step aiming to bolster digital sovereignty and develop the country’s telecommunications infrastructure.

In a speech he delivered during the inauguration ceremony, Sanad said that Iraq’s acquisition of a satellite would be impossible without a ground station.

The new facility will serve as a cornerstone for the country’s upcoming national space program, with future expansions planned to establish additional ground stations across other Iraqi provinces depending on population density and administrative assessment.

The station also acts as a complete technological hub that includes a satellite communication gateway, a localized data center, and an internet exchange point.

Developed in partnership with the technology group Commercis, the station links incoming satellite communications directly into Iraq’s expanding domestic fiber-optic terrestrial network.

Iraq previously relied on international infrastructure located outside its borders to route satellite traffic. The government is now actively urging ministries, private companies, and security agencies to migrate their traffic to this local gateway to secure sensitive data.

The station is part of a broader economic vision to transform Iraq into a regional data corridor. By leveraging its geographic location, Iraq aims to serve as a high-speed data transit bridge connecting networks across Asia, Africa, and Europe.

The station provides high-speed enterprise internet, secure government communications, live television feeds, and commercial satellite broadcasting.

World.title: Competing narratives emerge over blast at PMF security compound in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Two days after a powerful blast ripped through a Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) security headquarters in eastern Baghdad, an investigative report published by Al Mada newspaper and monithas revealed sharp contradictions surrounding the incident, presenting four competing narratives ranging from a targeted foreign strike to sabotage and munitions mismanagement.

The explosion struck at approximately 6:00 PM on Saturday, October 17, 2026, inside a facility operated by the PMF Security Directorate located along Sadr Al-Qanat near the Saad Al-Watri Hospital.

While the PMF’s official communique attributed the incident to an internal fire that detonated obsolete, deteriorated munitions—resulting in minor injuries to five personnel—field sources cited by Al Mada report over twenty injuries among PMF security personnel and unidentified associates. Strict security cordons accompanied the medical evacuation via PMF ambulances, fueling speculation regarding the potential presence of Iranian technical personnel at the site.

The circumstances have ignited debate over the operational nature of the facility. As an intelligence and security installation, the complex is not designated to warehouse expired ordnance. Security sources cited in the report claimed that newly arrived military consignments from Iran had been transferred into the depot just a week prior to the detonation.

Preliminary forensic findings referenced in the investigation point to the possibility of an incoming projectile initiating the primary blast, though information sharing on the file remains tightly restricted by the PMF Chief of Staff’s office while a specialized investigative committee established by Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi conducts its inquiry.

Four Competing Accounts

World.title: Iraq opens public university admissions for international schools’ graduates
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research announced on Monday, October 19, 2026, that the electronic admissions portal for international school graduates applying to public universities will open within the coming days for the 2026–2027 academic year.

According to a ministerial press release obtained by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), admissions processing will be managed through the centralized digital application platform Qaddim.

Eligible candidates graduating from accredited international curricula within Iraq will access the admissions system using their standardized examination sequence number and confidential verification credentials issued directly by their respective school administrations.

The ministry advised prospective students and guardians to monitor its official web portal and recognized digital channels for forthcoming regulatory guidelines, grade-weighting criteria, and precise application submission schedules.

The upcoming portal launch represents an institutional mechanism to integrate international school diploma holders into national university admissions channels alongside graduates of the standard ministerial secondary baccalaureate examinations.

World.title: US dollar edges up to 169,500 IQD in Baghdad and provincial exchanges
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar edged upward across parallel retail and wholesale counters in Baghdad and major commercial hubs on Monday, October 19, 2026.

The capital recorded an increase of 500 dinars per $100 compared to prior trading sessions, while regional desks in Erbil and Basra registered fractional gains of 50 dinars per $100.

In Baghdad, licensed exchange shops and retail desks posted dollar cash selling quotes at 169,500 dinars per $100 against purchase bids of 168,500 dinars, reflecting persistent upward pressure in parallel liquidity channels.

In Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan Region, counters listed selling rates at 168,550 dinars per $100 with purchase transactions accepted at 168,000 dinars. Across the southern port province of Basra, foreign exchange desks closed the morning session at a selling price of 168,750 dinars per $100 against buying offers of 168,250 dinars.

The current parallel figures sustain a pronounced gap above the official statutory cash rate mandated by the Central Bank of Iraq, which remains benchmarked at 152,000 dinars per $100.

This continuous premium highlights elevated demand for physical banknotes among local commercial importers navigating foreign trade settlements outside the central electronic clearance window.

World.title: Young innovators impress juries with ideas to solve real-world challenges
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Three separate juries evaluated entries in the three categories for the award and the panel members acknowledged at the end of the day that the quality of applicants was excellent.

In each of the categories, bulk of those shortlisted for evaluation by the jury were very young, either still in college or just out of it, though there were some older innovators too.

Over 14,000 applications were received, which were filtered down by Techgig to 1,000 and Grant Thornton shortlisted it to 35 finalists that were split between three juries. While first was on sovereign technology for India handled 14 entries, second on Inclusive Innovation for Bharat met a dozen applications and third on Sustainable & Resilient India dealt with nine entries.

The juries followed a pattern of a short presentation by the applicants, followed by questions from jury members and then a brief discussion between the members before scoring the applicant. Several jury members admitted that they were pleasantly surprised by how well thought through the presentations were, especially given the age of most applicants.

Even where some aspect of the road to implementation may have not occurred to the applicants â say, a compliance issue or consent to be obtained â it was striking how eager the innovators were to learn from the experience of those who had worked in the real world for decades and knew what it takes to translate brilliant ideas into real solutions.





The maturity to take hard questions as essential inputs rather than as harsh criticism was quite remarkable.

Ideas For India

The diversity of the presentations was also a striking aspect. In the technology sovereignty category, for instance, the ideas ranged from closing a felt gap in middle sized drones to faster and more efficient identification and countering of cyberattacks to dealing with ships that go âdarkâ, which may not always be for innocent reasons.

But these were not just ideas. The drone entry had already done some testing in the field with army units, the dark ships idea had been explored with a port and so on.

Such was the overall quality of the applicants that at least in two categories some of the jury members voiced the opinion that perhaps the awards need not be restricted to two in each category. There was, after all, no compulsion to stick to a bell curve, they pointed out. Most left the venue feeling satisfied that they had done their bit to encourage a cohort whose innovative mindset was matched by its enthusiasm to do good for society and for India.

World.title: BJP invokes CPM's 1972 'rigged poll' charge to corner Congress
World.content:
BJP MP Nishikant Dubey shared the report and took a dig at Congress neta Rahul Gandhi

NEW DELHI: Accused by its rivals of "vote-chori", BJP Monday sought to embarrass the Opposition by highlighting CPM's allegation that Congress used state power to turn the 1972 Bengal election into a "complete farce", taking a swipe at the two parties over their joint campaign against it."In order to turn their sure defeat into an artificial victory, Congress has thrown overboard rules and turned the whole election into a mockery," a CPM report on the "rigged poll" had said.BJP MP Nishikant Dubey shared the report and took a dig at Congress neta Rahul Gandhi over his campaign against EC and BJP over their alleged collusion to influence polls. Even Jyoti Basu, who became CM in 1977 and served for 23 years, was roughed up during counting and made to lose, Dubey claimed.CPM had alleged that Congress disregarded elementary rules, including allowing voters to vote, protecting ballot boxes and ensuring proper counting. TNN

World.title: ‘Deliberately breached bonds’: Court extends Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka’s custody by 2 days
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A special executive magistrate (SEM) on Monday extended the judicial custody of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activists

and Ashutosh Ranka by two days, rejecting fresh sureties furnished by their counsel.

The hearing was held before the new magistrate, SEM Ritu Raj, after the previous magistrate recused citing a threatening message.

An FIR was registered to investigate that matter.

In the order, the SEM observed that the duo had âdeliberatelyâ breached the bonds furnished on Oct 11 and committed a breach of peace soon after. Their assurance that they would not repeat the offence did ânot inspire confidenceâ, the order said, citing material submitted by the investigating officer.

It also flagged their âhabitualness in calling protests at de-notified areasâ and said they had shown âno respect for lawâ.

The magistrate rejected the two fresh sureties after personally questioning them.

Duo made no fresh calls for protests after Oct 10: Lawyer

The magistrate rejected the two fresh sureties after personally questioning them. The order noted an âapparent mismatch between one suretyâs photograph on the bond and his Aadhaar card,â while, over second surety, the SEM noted, he could not provide basic details, including parentage and address, of Das, with the magistrate concluding that âneither surety had sufficient controlâ over the activists to ensure their presence before the authorities.





sought a further five to seven days of judicial custody, citing an âimminent threat to public orderâ following an anonymous WhatsApp message allegedly sent to the previous magistrate. The IO also accused the duo of mobilising people to assemble at âde-notifiedâ protest sites through social media and breaching their Oct 11 undertaking.

Advocate Abhik Chimni, representing the duo, contested the grounds for continued detention, arguing that the police application did not establish any specific apprehension that the activists would repeat the alleged offence.

He maintained that the duo had made no fresh calls for protests after Oct 10 and had gone to Jantar Mantar individually. The defence also assured the magistrate that they would not repeat the alleged conduct and sought their release.

âThe order will be challenged,â Chimni said.

They were released the same day after furnishing peace bonds of Rs 50,000 each, but were detained again on Oct 13 over their alleged attempt to stage a Tiranga protest at Jantar Mantar.

World.title: Ringleader Lawrence Bishnoi in jail, 'shadow cabinet' runs gang
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Who really controls the Lawrence Bishnoi network while its notorious kingpin is confined to a high-security cell inside Gujarat's Sabarmati jail? The answer, sources told TOI, is that the gang is being run by a 'shadow cabinet' of Lawrence's key lieutenants who orchestrate transnational operations from foreign safe havens.

The core group comprises Tyson Bishnoi, Anil Pandit, Hari Boxer, Harman Sandhu and Himanshu Sonipat. They coordinate recruitment, tasking and logistics, and share screenshots. A parallel group comprising Aarzoo Bishnoi, Shubam Lonkar and Randeep Malik handles planning, financing and target selection. Gangster Goldi Dhillon was also part of it but went underground after FBI launched Operation Hardball.

Operating from the US, Canada and parts of Europe, the command structure oversees digital intimidation and field executions, directing local recruits through Signal, Instagram and WhatsApp.

Also Read:

Sources said seasoned kingpins Rohit Godara and Goldy Brar retain control and have falsely projected a split with Lawrence to mislead investigators. "Operating from deep within international safe havens, these higher-tier masterminds provide the strategic oversight, financial backing and cross-border protection that shield the network's mid-level lieutenants," an investigator said.

Pandit, their main public mouthpiece, posts gang manifestos and extortion warnings on social media.





A native of Panipat, he travelled to US via Canada a year after Sidhu Moose Wala was killed. Himanshu recently claimed responsibility for a drive-by shooting targeting Haryanvi singer Diler Kharkiya's Range Rover in Sonipat and rival gangster Vinod Kana's killing outside Hisar court complex on Aug 20.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

While Tyson issues online warnings to public figures, Hari drives ground-level extortion, and Harman coordinates overseas logistics through local executioners.

This distributed chain of command explains why an intercontinental dragnet led by FBI and its global allies has failed to paralyse the syndicate. Barely weeks after Operation Hard Ball, Lawrence's network issued warnings to actor Aamir Khan and Rajasthan politicians over alleged cultural slights.

World.title: Congress snubbed delimitation talks: Government signals Parliament session
World.content:
It was not clear why the demand for consultation was being made repeatedly, Rijiju said

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Days after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge called for an all-party meeting to discuss any fresh delimitation proposal, govt on Monday said it had already consulted many opposition parties, including Samajwadi Party, DMK and NCP (SP), and could not hold talks with Congress because of its own unwillingness, refuelling the buzz that Parliament may be called for a short duration to take up the legislation.In a sharp response to Kharge's Oct 16 letter to PM Narendra Modi, parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said, "When after repeated requests Congress didn't give dates for discussion, govt's outreach extended to other political parties. Consultations were held with representatives of parties including SP, DMK, YSRCP, NCP (SP), Shiv Sena (UBT), AIMIM and BJD with a view to building a broader consensus in support of the proposed legislation. "In these circumstances, it was not clear why the demand for consultation was being made repeatedly, he added, rejecting Kharge's suggestion. Rijiju sought to give the impression of Congress's isolation over the issue by emphasising govt's consultations with other key members of the opposition in contrast to both Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha, not giving him any date for discussion when he had met them during the last session.Writing to Modi, Kharge had also questioned the "unprecedented" delay in proroguing the monsoon session, which was adjourned indefinitely on Aug 13. Dismissing his contention, Rijiju cited precedents and underlined that no constitutional requirement existed prescribing a specific period within which a House must be prorogued following its adjournment sine die."The mere fact that a House has not been prorogued does not, by itself, give rise to any constitutional or procedural impropriety or irregularity," Rijiju said. â Kumar Rakesh

World.title: Dushyant Kumar Gautam sworn in as Sikkim governor, Congress vows stir
World.content:
Newly sworn-in Sikkim Governor Dushyant Gautam during the swearing-in ceremony

GANGTOK/DELHI: Dushyant Kumar Gautam was sworn in as the 19th governor of Sikkim Monday, succeeding Om Prakash Mathur.Slamming the governing BJP for sticking with Gautam's appointment as governor despite the shadow of a murder case, Congress said its protest over the issue will intensify and it will gherao the Uttarakhand assembly on Oct 27.AICC's Uttarakhand in-charge Kumari Selja said it is shameful that a person whose name is linked to a massive scandal is being appointed to Raj Bhavan. "Every citizen in Uttarakhand feels that there is no justice in the state. The murder of the young woman in the hill state in 2022 had shaken the country, but justice has not been meted out to this day." Selja said the party will take out yatras all over the state to highlight the issue.Gautam was administered the oath of office and secrecy by Sikkim HC chief justice A Muhamed Mustaque in the presence of CM Prem Singh Tamang, judges and others.

World.title: 400-plus Indian-origin scholars, alumni from 27 countries warn against ‘anarchy’
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Days after competing groups of Harvard-linked Indians took opposing positions on protests against the Election Commission, more than 400 Indian-origin students, researchers and alumni associated with universities across 27 countries have issued a statement warning against efforts to erode public trust in constitutional institutions and attempts to replace democratic debate with street confrontation.

Titled âSpare India from Anarchyâ, the statement carries 402 names, including individuals linked to Harvard, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), Oxford, Cambridge, Stanford, Princeton, Yale and Columbia universities, as well as the London School of Economics, National University of Singapore and University of Toronto.

The signatories allege that âa frenzy of election denialâ and a preference for âstreet over Sansadâ have taken hold in some quarters.

They argue that unfavourable election results are being used to question electoral procedures, adverse court rulings to cast doubts on judicial independence and even the armed forces are being drawn into partisan debate.

âAn unconscionable and devious plan of sowing seeds of doubt in Indian democracy has been hatched,â the statement claims, accusing unspecified groups of turning matters before courts into campaigns on the streets.





The intervention follows a public disagreement among Harvard affiliates over the October 10 protests in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. A group of around 100 Harvard-linked signatories criticised alleged police excesses and detentions, while 44 others subsequently warned against attacks on the credibility of constitutional institutions.

The latest appeal widens that dispute beyond Harvard, though it does not name the Election Commission, the SIR exercise or the Delhi protests explicitly.

Invoking BR Ambedkarâs warning about the âgrammar of anarchyâ, the statement says dissent remains essential to democracy but should not become a cover for undermining its institutions. It calls for resolving differences through âdebate, discussion, dialogue and dissentâ within the constitutional framework.

World.title: Hours after custody extension, Delhi Police transfers CJP leaders' trespassing case to crime branch
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

on Monday transferred the trespassing case against Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das to the crime branch, news agency ANI reported, citing sources.

This came hours after a Delhi court extended the CJP leaders' judicial custody by two days for allegedly entering Jantar Mantar, which is no longer a designated protest venue, and obstructing police personnel on duty.

Along with other CJP workers, they waved the national flag at the site and raised slogans against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar before being detained and placed under preventive custody.

According to their lawyer, their bail sureties were rejected due to a reported mismatch in documents. They will now be produced before the court on Wednesday.

"Today, when we reached the court, the five-day custody period had ended. On the last date of hearing, the court had stated that it did not find the sureties legitimate enough to be accepted. Today, we produced fresh sureties and brought them to court. When our matter was taken up, the State filed a fresh application, which was served on us at that point.





In this application, they sought a further five to seven days of judicial custody," the CJP leaders' advocate said.

"The reasons they gave were absolutely shocking to us. They claimed there was an imminent threat to public order and public tranquillity and that, therefore, the accused needed to remain in judicial custody... It is very unfortunate, and everyone must remember that there is currently no FIR against my clients in connection with this issue.

This concerns preventive custody. They have been detained out of fear that they might go and protest.

There is no FIR, no pending case against them in this matter, and no investigation for which they need to be questioned. This is absolutely appalling and deeply disturbing. I cannot remember the last time people were kept in preventive custody under such circumstances. We will pursue the matter legally, but this has been hugely disappointing for all of us," he added.

The development came amid allegations by the CJP that the bail proceedings had been deliberately delayed to prevent the release of its two convenors, who were sent to five-day judicial custody on October 13 following a protest at Jantar Mantar.

On Sunday, the special executive magistrate hearing their bail matter claimed that unknown persons were threatening him, following which the police registered a non-cognisable report.

Meanwhile, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership and praised Das and Ranka for remaining defiant despite spending five days in judicial custody.

"You must be feeling very strong keeping a 26-year-old Saurav Das in jail. You must be feeling very strong beating children on the streets. You must be feeling very strong putting up barricades across Delhi and dragging students on the streets," he said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Dipke claimed that Das and Ranka had gone to Jantar Mantar to wave the national flag but were sent to judicial custody. He also alleged that their court hearings had been repeatedly postponed. "Is this strength? Hiding behind the police, hiding behind the courts, is this Narendra Modi's strength?" he asked.

World.title: India asks its nationals in Italy to exercise caution, avoid crowded areas amid protests
World.content:
The Indian Embassy in Rome on Monday (October 19, 2026) asked Indian nationals to exercise caution and avoid crowded areas due to protests and demonstrations across several cities in Italy.

The Embassy, in a social media post, said there were protests and demonstrations last week in some Italian cities.

“We advise Indian nationals to exercise caution, avoid crowded areas and locations where protests are taking place and follow local news about such events,” it said.

It further said that in case of an emergency, Indian nationals could contact the embassy office in Rome at +39 331 614 2085 and the Consulate General of India in Milan at +39 3881647527.

The protests against rising cost of living began peacefully across several cities on Sunday. In Milan, rioters clashed with police, looted stores and set property ablaze.

Condemning the violence, Italy’s Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni on Sunday said, “Demonstrating is a right. Setting our cities ablaze is not.”

“I have great respect for the thousands of people who today demonstrated peacefully... Whatever the ideas for which one demonstrates, participation is the foundation of any healthy democracy,” Ms. Meloni said in a post on X.

The Italian premier said stones were thrown at the law enforcement forces in Milan, which led to injuries to officers and forced the interruption of the procession.

She said people carrying cobblestones and hammers were stopped in Turin and a railway station was closed as a precautionary measure in Bologna.

Ms. Meloni requested the opposition to unequivocally condemn these acts of violence and issue a clear appeal for every mobilisation to be peaceful.

The protests in Italy coincided with nationwide protests in neighbouring France against rising living costs and in support of high school students’ grievances.

World.title: Migrants have taken over France, they must close the borders: Trump on France riots
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump used the protests roiling France to score some quick political points on Monday (October 19, 2026), as the upcoming midterm elections force his Republican party to face strong headwinds.

At a rally in Kansas, the U.S. President launched into a lengthy tirade about France, which he said was being “conquered, looted, and burned to the ground by migrants, jihadists, and communists.”

“And we’re not going to let that happen to this country,” he added.

While speaking with reporters previously in the day, Mr. Trump recalled an exchange with his French counterpart Emmanuel Macron: “I told him a long time ago, you’re making a big mistake in France. You’re letting everybody from the world come in...Paris is going to be a Muslim city very soon.”

Earlier on Monday (October 19, 2026), the 80-year-old President wrote on his Truth Social platform: “The migrants have taken over France. They must CLOSE THE BORDERS, FAST!”

Cost-of-living demonstrations broke out across France over the weekend, with many devolving into looting and violent conflict, prompting officials to institute partial curfews on Monday (October 19, 2026).

While the French protests were inspired by soaring inflation, Trump has molded the violent clashes with police into evidence in favor of the anti-immigration policies he used to successfully campaign for reelection in 2024.

“They’re taking this French crisis and turning it into a campaign argument,” J.C. Lintzenich, a senior fellow with the German Marshall Fund think tank, told AFP.

Conservative talking points

Opinion polls heavily favour Mr. Trump’s rival Democratic Party in the November 3 midterm elections, which will determine who will take control of Congress.

With just two weeks to go before Americans go to the polls, Mr. Trump has grasped any strategy he can to compel voters to support the Republican party and his Make America Great Again (MAGA) movement.

“Since the beginning of the MAGA movement, Europe has been an extension of the US political battlefield, so it’s not surprising that when there are events like the unrest from October 17, the political machine gets moving,” Justin Vaisse, a professor of U.S. foreign policy at Johns Hopkins University, told AFP.

As videos of France’s unrest began surfacing on social media, Vice President J.D. Vance wrote Saturday (October 17, 2026) on X: “Western liberals imported the third world into France...they ignored fundamental questions of assimilation and compatibility.”

Right-wing U.S. media personalities, including Glenn Beck, Benny Johnson, Nick Sortor and Jack Posobiec made similar points, blaming immigrants from Muslim-majority countries for causing a crisis in Western identity.

“The riots are viewed as validation of the warnings against immigration in general and Muslim immigration, if such a thing exists,” Vaisse said.

Celia Belin, a senior policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations and head of its Paris office, views the commentary as an “export of domestic policies” from a US administration that openly supports nationalist parties in Europe.

She told AFP that Mr. Trump and his allies “rushed into this argument, the same one that Vance had presented in Munich” in 2025, in a controversial speech described as a US culture war against Europe, with the goal of “fanning the flames.”

Polling priorities

Experts note that this rhetorical strategy, while it may have succeeded in 2024, is not necessarily what US voters want to hear these days.

“When you look at the campaign ads here — I’m in South Carolina right now -- it’s about healthcare, domestic issues,” Lintzenich said.

“The international element is a blip on the radar, and Ukraine, and Iran, and other ongoing national security issues rate higher than the current French instability,” he continued.

A Pew Research poll this month found the economy plays an important role in the choice of 82% of U.S. voters, a far higher number than immigration (59%) or race-related issues (36%).

Though Mr. Trump has followed through on his 2024 campaign promise to crack down on immigration, he has fared less successfully on his other promise to tamp down on inflation, with his tariff policies and war with Iran spiking prices across the economy, plunging his approval rating to record lows.

Vaisse said using linking U.S. identitarian rhetoric with the events in France “is not going to win a single vote” for Republicans, though it could “mobilize the base” to vote.

World.title: Gold mine collapse kills at least 14 in southwest Colombia
World.content:
At least 14 miners were killed when an open-pit gold mine operating with no permits collapsed in a remote corner of Colombia’s Nariño province, regional authorities said.

In a statement, Nariño’s government said an additional seven people were injured in the mining accident on Monday near the small town of Santa Barbara de Iscuande, adding that search efforts had ended Monday night.

“This emergency once again highlights the risks associated with informal mining,” the statement said. “In less than three months, two collapsed mines in Nariño have killed 27 people.”

Santa Barbara de Iscuande is surrounded by dense rainforest and can only be reached by boat or small aircraft, which makes it difficult for aid workers to reach the area.

“Entire families have been killed in this regrettable accident. It is very sad,” said Nariño’s governor, Luis Alfonso Escobar.

Hundreds of small mines in Colombia operate without government permits, and some are controlled by rebel groups.

Besides being difficult to reach, Santa Barbara de Iscuande also faces security problems.

Two rebel groups reportedly operate in the area, including the Jacobo Arenas Block, a group led by former members of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) who refused to join a 2016 peace deal with Colombia’s government.

In a statement, Colombia’s Ombudsman’s Office urged armed groups in the area to allow humanitarian aid to reach the small town.

“All of our efforts must go towards protecting lives and tending to this emergency,” the office said on X.

World.title: France protests: Paris police issue overnight curfew in two areas to try to prevent further disorder
World.content:
Paris police issued an overnight curfew in two areas of the French capital, after a weekend marred by France's worst rioting in years that targeted city halls, other public buildings and thousands of businesses across the country.

The order issued on Monday (October 19, 2026) aims to protect “people and property from the violence and looting”, the Paris police statement said.

The curfew prohibits anyone from entering or remaining on the Place de la République, where rioting took place Saturday (October 17, 2026), and the shopping neighbourhood of Les Halles, which has been subject to looting.

The curfew will be in effect from 11 pm on Monday until 6 am on Tuesday. In addition, gatherings and demonstrations are banned from 8 pm, the Paris police said.

Earlier Monday (October 19, 2026), Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu had called for “very limited” and “localised” curfews.

In northern France, local authorities imposed a curfew for children and teenagers under age 18 in several cities, including Lille, starting from Monday (October 19, 2026) and for the next two days from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Nice, on the French Riviera, also imposed an overnight curfew for minors from 9 p.m.

Mr. Lecornu defended police handling of the unrest, saying that “despite scenes of severe violence and extensive property damage, no one was killed, and that is a miracle”.

He said that details of the curfews would be announced later Monday (October 19, 2026) after consultations with mayors.

Mass protests in France are often tainted by violence on the fringes of otherwise peaceful marches, leading to clashes with police. Saturday's unrest recalled the riots that followed the fatal police shooting of a teenager in 2023, when authorities imposed local curfews, and violence during the yellow vest movement that began in 2018 over fuel prices and broader economic grievances.

World.title: Delhi protest: CJP leaders’ judicial custody extended by two days
World.content:
Cockroach Janta Party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were on Monday (October 19, 2026) sent to judicial remand for two more days after being produced before a newly appointed Special Executive Magistrate at Mandir Marg police station in New Delhi, an official said.

Also read | CJP alleges delay in release of leaders, four sureties rejected

The development came amid allegations by the CJP that the bail proceedings in the case were deliberately delayed to prevent the release of its two co-convenors, who were initially sent to five-day judicial custody on October 13 after they defied restrictions to protest at Jantar Mantar.

The two were taken into custody after they allegedly climbed over a locked gate to enter Jantar Mantar, which had earlier been denotified as a designated protest site.

Along with other CJP workers, they displayed the national flag at the site and shouted slogans against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar before being detained and placed under preventive arrest.

They were subsequently produced before a Special Executive Magistrate, who remanded them to judicial custody.

On Monday (October 19, 2026), the police sought an extension of the two leaders' judicial custody and the court sent them to jail for two more days, sources said.

They will now be produced on Wednesday (October 21), they said.

On Sunday (October 19), the Special Executive Magistrate, hearing their bail matter, had claimed that unknown persons were threatening him, following which the police registered a non-cognisable report.

In a post on X, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke had alleged, "The state is deliberately prolonging Ashu and Saurav's illegal arrest by using every dirty trick in the book to delay court proceedings and prevent their release.

"They have no legal grounds to keep them behind bars, so they are resorting to delaying tactics to keep them there."

The CJP also alleged that bail sureties for the release of its leaders had been rejected on "vague" grounds.

World.title: Political mercury rises in Punjab ahead of Amit Shah’s visit
World.content:
Political temperature rose on Monday (October 19, 2026) ahead of Union Home Minister Amit Shah’s slated visit to Punjab on October 20, during which he is set to meet the families of those who lost their lives after speaking out against the drug menace.

Editorial | Drugs and bullets: On narcotrafficking and targeted killings in Punjab

Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon said Mr. Shah would meet the family of Parminder Singh Jhotta, the anti-drug crusader, in Mansa; the family of Gulzar Singh in Toor Banjara village of Sangrur district and the family of Bikramjit Singh in Mari Panwan village of Gurdaspur district. Both Jhota and Gulzar Singh died in incidents linked to the State’s drug issue.

Mr. Dhillon said the people of Punjab and the affected families want concrete action against drugs and justice for the victims and Mr. Shah’s visit has sparked new hope for families affected by drugs.

While Mr. Shah, in a post on ‘X’ targeted the AAP government in Punjab, saying, “The AAP government has left no stone unturned in pushing Punjab into the pit of drugs, which caused many families to lose their children. Those people who recently had to lose their lives for raising their voices against the meth dealers thriving under AAP’s protection,” he said.

The AAP targeted the BJP over the Lawrence Bishnoi gang claiming responsibility for the attack on actor Tiger Shroff. AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal said that a party unable to manage law and order in its own states was coming to Punjab to lecture its people, while providing gangsters with facilities to operate.

“They cannot manage law and order in their own states, yet they are coming to Punjab to lecture others. They have treated the country’s biggest gangster like their ‘daamaad’ and provided him with every facility to commit crimes not just in India but across the world.”

He asserted, “On Tuesday [October 20], they will come to Punjab to lecture people on law and order. But the people of Punjab know that voting for them would be like inviting their ‘daamaad’ into Punjab,” he alleged.

Meanwhile, senior Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) leader Harsimrat Kaur Badal urged Mr. Shah to order a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into the murder of Mr. Jhota besides calling for a comprehensive investigation into the politician-police drug trade nexus in Punjab.

In a letter to the Home Minister, the Bathinda MP said that Mr. Jhota’s father — Bhim Singh had given a statement to the police which, she alleged was not being acted upon and demanded that all facets of the bereaved father’s statement be probed by the CBI.

World.title: Two Indian nationals among 28 charged with election fraud in California
World.content:
Two Indian nationals are among 28 green card holders charged with election fraud in California, the U.S. Department of Justice said in a statement on Monday.

According to the Justice Department, Amandeep Kaur (30) and Kamlesh Shah (67) have been charged with fraudulently registering as voters and casting their ballots in the November 2024 U.S. elections.

It said of the 28 persons charged with election fraud, 11 have been arrested in early morning raids across the state under ‘Operation Protect the Vote’ to combat and root out fraud in U.S. elections and uphold electoral integrity.

It was not immediately clear whether the two Indian nationals were among those arrested.

Mr. Shah is a resident of Sacramento and fraudulently registered to vote on the day of the November 2024 general election and voted that day, the Justice Department said.

Ms. Kaur, a resident of Rancho Palos Verdes, who is seeking to become a U.S. citizen, fraudulently registered to vote in December 2022 and voted in the November 2024 US election, it said.

“All 28 foreign nationals charged are lawful permanent residents (LPRs), or 'green card' holders. Although LPRs have legal immigration status in the United States, they are not US citizens and are not permitted to vote in US elections,” the Justice Department said.

The criminal charges include making false statements in a naturalisation application and some of the defendants also are charged with fraudulent voter registration. Both charges are felonies that carry a maximum penalty of five years in federal prison.

Today DOJ charged 28 noncitizens across California with federal election crimes. All were on the list of 20k we sent to California, which has refused to even look at the list. It's not too late for California to step up & protect the votes of American citizens. https://t.co/5QAlPwBBjm — Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter (@PADAGMcCotter) October 19, 2026

“Each of the 28 defendants charged today appears on the list of more than 20,000 likely noncitizen registrants we provided to California election officials last week,” Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter told reporters in Los Angeles.

Before Monday (October 19, 2026), the Justice Department had charged about 90 people for various types of election misconduct so far this year, including 50 who are alleged to have voted as noncitizens. There were more than 227 million registered voters in the United States during the 2024 presidential election.

World.title: Morning Digest: Jaishankar welcomes UAE’s Foreign Minister Al Nahyan in Mumbai; gunmen kill at least 40 civilians in Mali, and more
World.content:
Jaishankar welcomes UAE’s Foreign Minister Al Nahyan in Mumbai

External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar expressed his delight in welcoming UAE Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan at Mumbai airport on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) ahead of their upcoming bilateral talks .“Delighted to welcome DPM & FM UAE @ABZayed to Mumbai. Look forward to our talks,” said Mr. Jaishankar in his social media post

Gunmen kill at least 40 civilians in Mali: security and community sources

More than 40 civilians have been killed in weekend attacks by armed men on camps in Mali’s northeastern Menaka region, security and community sources told AFP on Monday (October 19, 2026). The assailants reportedly rode in on motorcycles, targeting camps mainly housing members of the Daoussahak community, whose executive bureau blamed the killings on the Islamic State group.

SKM joins agitation over SIR irregularities; movement to grow bigger: Actor Prakash Raj

Actor-activist Prakash Raj on Monday (October 19, 2026) said the protest over alleged SIR irregularities was snowballing into a nationwide movement, with the SKM joining the agitation. He also claimed that voters would oust the Narendra Modi-led government in centre if it continued to suppress dissent.

Allahabad High Court stays conviction of murder convict who wishes to contest 2027 U.P. polls

The Allahabad High Court has stayed the conviction and sentence of a man convicted in a 2017 murder case after noting that he wished to contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election either as an independent candidate or, if possible, on a BJP ticket.A two-judge bench comprising Justice Siddharth and Justice Vinai Kumar Dwivedi passed the order hearing a criminal appeal filed by Nandlal Rai alias Babloo Rai, who was convicted by the Varanasi Sessions Court in 2025 in connection with a 2017 murder case which was registered at Sigra police station.

RSS leader, W.B. Minister oppose attacks on book stalls set up by Left parties at Durga Puja pandals

As attacks on book stalls set up by Left parties near Durga Puja pandals continue in different parts of the State, a senior functionary of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh and a West Bengal Minister has come out openly criticising the move. Jishnu Basu, a prominent RSS leader from West Bengal, said that there is no valour in vandalising book stalls and those indulging in such acts are cowards. Mr. Basu, the Saha Khetra Prachar Pramukh of South Bengal, said that “those intoxicated by power and using the police to close down book Stalls” do not understand the country and cannot call themselves Hindu.

Japan successfully launches probe in historic Mars moon mission

Japanese scientists successfully launched a spacecraft Tuesday (October 20, 2026) that aims to be the first to retrieve samples from one of Mars’s moons, potentially helping unlock the origins of the Solar System and life on Earth. The flagship H3 rocket carrying the unmanned Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) probe blasted off into a pitch-black sky from the Tanegashima Space Center at 4:41 a.m. (1941 GMT Monday), according to a live stream broadcast by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency.

Saudi envoy meets Pakistan Army chief, discusses regional security dynamics

Saudi Arabia’s newly appointed envoy to Pakistan, Rajeh Tami Albugamy, met Army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir on Monday (October 19, 2026) and discussed matters of mutual interest and regional security dynamics, the army said. During the meeting at General Headquarters in Rawalpindi, both sides expressed satisfaction over the progress made under the framework of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and underscored the importance of strengthening defence collaboration, institutional linkages and strategic coordination, the army said in a statement.

Cyril Ramaphosa tells South Africa to prepare for loss of U.S.-Africa trade deal

South African President Cyril Ramaphosa said on Monday (October 19, 2026) the country should “prepare” for the possibility of being removed from Washington’s duty-free trade programme for Africa, as ties between the two nations continue to fray. The African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), which grants eligible sub-Saharan African countries preferential access to the U.S. market, has been renewed until the end of 2028.

World.title: GDP growth revised down to 3.65pc as country falls short of target
World.content:
• Industrial, services sector slowdown drags down economic growth in FY26

• Per capita income ‘lowest in region’; economy reaches $450.4bn

ISLAMABAD: The government on Monday revised the gross domestic product (GDP) growth slightly downward to 3.65 per cent for the outgoing fiscal year (FY26), attributing the adjustment to a mild slowdown in the industrial and services sectors.

The country’s GDP registered modest growth alongside an increase in per capita income in dollar terms, reflecting a sluggish pace of recovery in the country’s overall output compared with the previous year, the government said.

In May 2026, the government had projected the economy to grow by 3.70pc in FY26, revising its earlier estimate of 4pc. The downward adjustment now indicates that the country fell short of its GDP target.

The revised growth rates in agriculture, industry and services in FY26 are 3.50pc, 3.34pc and 3.81pc, respectively, compared with earlier growth rates of 2.89pc, 3.51pc and 4.09pc.

The revision came during the 118th meeting of the National Accounts Committee (NAC), which was held on Monday at the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics.

The NAC estimate places Pakistan broadly in line with the outlook of multilateral lenders, though with some variation.

The International Monetary Fund has projected GDP growth at 3.6pc for FY26, the World Bank at 3.7pc and the Asian Development Bank at 3.7pc, while the State Bank of Pakistan expects growth to remain close to 3.7pc.

The committee approved the incorporation of revised imports data in the national accounts estimates from FY21 to FY25, quarterly GDP growth rates for Q1 (revised), Q2 (revised), Q3 (revised), and Q4 during FY26 and updated annual growth rates for FY25 and FY26.

The size of the economy rose to $450.4 billion in FY26 from $410.96bn in FY25, mainly driven by growth in the services sector, followed by industry and livestock.

Per capita income slightly increased to $1,896 in FY26, the lowest in the region, up from $1,824 in FY25. The projection is based on the 2023 census. However, it was $1,551 in FY23, $1,766 in FY22 and $1,677 in FY21.

This suggests a deterioration in the standard of living and well-being acro­ss almost all segments of society, with no tangible increase in personal incomes due to unprecedented inflationary pressures, which reduce disposable income and limit individuals’ ability to afford goods and services, save, or invest.

Updated growth rates

Meanwhile, the NAC also approved the updated growth rates for Q1, Q2 and Q3 of 2025-26 at 3.89pc, 4.31pc and 4.42pc, respectively, compared with 3.92pc, 4.05pc and 3.99pc, presented at the 117th meeting of the NAC. The fourth quarter of FY26 recorded a 2pc growth in GDP. The committee approved the updated annual growth of 3.11pc for FY25, which was estimated at 3.18pc in the previous meeting.

In agriculture, important crops improved from 0.65pc to 1.59pc due to wheat and maize, other crops have witnessed significant improvement from 2.43pc to 4.28pc due to higher production of pulses (6.3pc), fruits (1.3pc), tomato (44pc), oilseed (5.4pc), and green fodder (2.4pc). Livestock decreased slightly from 3.75pc to 3.71pc because of increased fodder inputs. Updated growth rates in forestry and fishing are 10.80pc and 1.39pc, respectively.

The committee revised growth in industry during FY26 to 3.34pc from 3.51pc estimated previously. The mining & quarrying industry has improved from 0.38pc to 1.52pc due to improvement in gas (2.84pc), crude oil (5.12pc), and coal (2.73pc). Large-scale manufacturing (LSM), which is measured through the Quantum Index of Manufacturing (QIM), has declined from 6.11pc to 5.01pc.

The major LSM groups with positive contributions are food (7.03pc), tobacco (12.61pc), petroleum products (9.7pc), rubber products (14.19­pc), electrical equi­pment (14.25pc), automobiles (57.77­pc), transport equipment (42.36pc), furniture (22.69pc), and other manufacturing (foot­ball) (16.62pc). The construction industry has improved from 5.73pc to 6.30pc because of increased construction-related expenditure in the public sector.

However, some LSM groups posted negative growth, e.g., pharmaceuticals (-8.87pc), iron & steel products (-7.84pc), chemicals (-2.53pc), and leather products (-1.95pc), electricity (-10.24pc) in FY26.

The services industry has declined from 4.09pc to 3.81pc in FY26, with positive contributions from all the constituents. The growth in wholesale and retail trade posted at 2.37pc as against the previous growth of 3.71pc due to decrease in manufacturing and imports.

Transport and storage industry growth improved to 3.23pc from 2.31pc due to upward revisions reported in railways, water transport, and air transport. Similarly, information & communication growth increased from 7.52pc to 9.53pc, the finance & insurance also improved from 0.32pc to 4.23pc in FY26 due to improvement in the insurance industry.

The slowdown was also reported in public administration and social security to 5.67pc from 8.54pc, education 4.17pc from 5.23pc, and human health and social work 5.52pc from 6.85pc.

Published in Dawn, October 20th, 2026

World.title: Govt slashes petrol price by Rs5.16 per litre, high-speed diesel rate by Rs7.69
World.content:
The government on Monday cut the price of petrol by Rs5.16 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs7.69.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs381.14 per litre while HSD will cost Rs389.27 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 20 (Tuesday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: CDF Munir, new Saudi envoy express satisfaction at progress made under Makkah defence pact: ISPR
World.content:
The new Saudi envoy in Pakistan, Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy, met with Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir on Monday, with both sides expressing satisfaction over the progress made under the trilateral Makkah defence agreement, according to the military’s media wing.

Albugamy assumed his diplomatic responsibilities in Islamabad last Thursday, reaffirming the commitment to strengthening the strategic and fraternal ties between the two countries.

Inter-Service Public Relations (ISPR) said in a statement on Monday that the ambassador called on CDF Munir at General Headquarters (GHQ) in Rawalpindi. According to the statement, matters of mutual interest and regional security dynamics were discussed.

“Both the dignitaries expressed satisfaction over the progress made under the framework of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and underscored the importance of strengthening defence collaboration, institutional linkages and strategic coordination,” the statement read.

CDF Munir congratulated the ambassador on his appointment and expressed confidence that his tenure would further strengthen the longstanding fraternal ties between Islamabad and Riyadh, which are “rooted in shared faith, mutual trust and strategic partnership”.

Last week, Albugamy met Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar.

PM Shehbaz reaffirmed Pakistan’s support for Saudi Arabia in safeguarding its “sovereignty, security and territorial integrity” amid a recent escalation in Houthi attacks during their meeting.

DPM Dar, meanwhile, underscored longstanding fraternal and strategic ties between Islamabad and Riyadh when he met Albugamy. He also reaffirmed Islamabad and Riyadh’s “shared commitment to further strengthen bilateral cooperation for mutual progress and prosperity”.

Islamabad and Riyadh have signed two defence pacts aimed at collective deterrence, the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement between the two and the Makkah Joint Defence Alliance that also includes Turkiye.

Earlier this month, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye convened an emergency meeting under the Makkah alliance and agreed to deploy military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom.

While the statement did not specifically name any threat, the development came against the backdrop of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

The Makkah defence pact , signed on Aug 7, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

In an interview aired on Sunday, the military’s spokesman said Pakistan is providing “whatever support is needed” to defend Saudi Arabia amid attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels against the kingdom.

World.title: Senate approves bill seeking blue passports for ex-lawmakers with incomplete term
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Senate on Monday passed a bill that sought to allow former lawmakers to have blue passports even if they had not served a full term in the National Assembly (NA) or Senate.

In the same sitting, the House withdrew a bill seeking to allow the issuance of blue passports to dependent children under the age of 28 of ex-members of Parliament.

Official blue passports are issued to key constitutional, government and judicial office holders, senior bureaucrats and their eligible dependents, allowing them visa-free entry to 55 countries, including 22 European countries.

The bills pertaining to the blue passport were moved by Senator Abdul Qadir today.

Of them, the House passed the amendment inserting a new Section 3-A in the Passports Act, 1974, which states that “a retired parliamentarian who has taken oath as a Member of the National Assembly (MNA) or the Senate, whether for a full term or for the remainder of the term of another member, shall, on such terms and conditions as may be prescribed, be entitled to retain and use the gratis official (blue) passport issued to him or her after ceasing to hold office”.

The amendment also covers lawmakers who leave office before completing five years as an MNA or six years as a senator.

At present, blue passports are issued to those ex-parliamentarians who remained a member of either House for at least one term, according to the Passport Rules 2021.

The statement of objects and reasons of the bill approved by the Senate states that the amendment “brings parity with the privileges available to other high-ranking officials and ensures uniform treatment of persons who have served the state at the highest level”.

The bill has yet to be passed by the NA.

The second bill, which sought to amend Section 12 of the Members of Parliament (Salaries and Allowances) Act, 1974 to provide that “an ex-member, the spouse of the ex-member and the dependent children of the ex-member below the age of 28 years shall be entitled to a gratis official (blue) passport”, was withdrawn after opposition by treasury members in the Senate.

In July, the bill had been approved by the relevant Senate committee, with the government drawing backlash. After criticism of the bill, Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry had assured that measures would be taken to ensure that the travel document was used for “only official duties” abroad and issued for a limited time in most cases.

Speaking on blue passports in the Senate, Chaudhry said the number of these official passports issued in the country had been reduced from 75,000 to 45,000 after European countries and Canada raised reservations. Around 30,000 unnecessary and inactive blue passports had been cancelled, he said.

“Security and dignity of passport is a matter of the dignity of people of Pakistan,” he remarked, noting that Pakistan also had agreements with other countries regarding blue and red passports.

He said the government had no issue with parliamentarians themselves getting blue passports but had concerns over extending the facility to their families, explaining that a large number of blue passports resulted in other countries hesitating to offer visa-free access.

He added that a bill would soon be moved to withdraw the blue passport facility available for the children of retired bureaucrats.

Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar emphasised that blue passports should be regulated as they are meant for official business.

“Let children make their own careers; respect is not built through blue passports,” he said.

He also called for ending the six-year service requirement for Senate members to obtain official passports, saying the rules should be the same for members of the Senate and the NA.

NA members became eligible for official passports after taking the oath, while senators had to complete their six-year term, he said, adding that a senator who resigned a few months before completing their term could lose eligibility for the passport.

PML-N Senator Abid Sher Ali strongly criticised the requirement of a no-objection certificate (NOC) from the interior ministry for the issuance of blue passports to parliamentarians, saying it did not exist earlier.

“Are we dacoits or terrorists that we need NOCs?” he said, terming the requirement a breach of privilege. He announced that he would move a privilege motion in this regard.

‘Assault on people’s mandate’

The Senate also witnessed a debate between the opposition and the treasury over the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Leader of the Opposition in the Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas termed the move an “assault on the people’s mandate”.

“You robbed the people’s votes. Your own minister said the system has collapsed,” he said, referring to comments made by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi about the governance system in the country requiring a reset.

Speaking at the Pakistan Economic Summit in July, the interior minister had said the current “system” of governance had “collapsed”, and was fundamentally incapable of resolving the country’s problems.

The opposition leader said what happened in KP was “sheer oppression” and could have been avoided.

He also urged the government not to push people to the wall, saying, “You snatched the mandate from Bengalis and they separated. You have still not learned.”

Abbas also sought a briefing on Yemen, noting that Parliament in 2015 had passed a resolution not to be part of the conflict in the Middle Eastern country. He said he had written to the prime minister and foreign minister asking them to mediate, instead of becoming part of the conflict.

“This is a sensitive issue. Countries are economically devastated and we are going to be part of another war,” he said.

In response, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said that emergency and governor’s rule were imposed in KP via a presidential order under Articles 233 and 234 of the Constitution, and were ratified by the Senate and National Assembly.

“All steps have been taken in the interest of peace, stability and national interest,” he said.

Additional input from APP

World.title: In NA, Achakzai demands to know Sohail Afridi’s whereabouts
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly (NA) Mehmood Khan Achakzai on Monday demanded on the floor of the House that details about Sohail Afridi’s whereabouts be shared.

Afridi, who has become non-functional as the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister, has not been seen since the imposition of governor’s rule and emergency in his province on Oct 11. His whereabouts remained unknown on the day governor’s rule was imposed and federal minister said a day later that he and some of his cabinet members are in preventative custody.

The PTI has also alleged the detention and arrests of several of its other members, including lawmakers and ministers.

“Afridi and six to seven other MNAs of the opposition party are missing since the proclamation of emergency and governor’s rule in KP. At least we and their families should know where they are,” Achakzai said, after he reached the NA some time after the session began.

Deputy Speaker Syed Ghulam Mustafa Shah was presiding over the proceedings and was asked by Achakzai to give him the floor.

Continuing his criticism of governor’s rule, Achakzai said, “You have attacked the assembly of a province”. He called for the issuance of production orders for missing MNAs.

The chief whip of the opposition in the NA, MNA Amir Dogar, also submitted an adjournment motion in the House, seeking production orders for six “missing” PTI MNAs: Amjad Ali Khan (NA-02), Junaid Akbar (NA-09), Fazal Muhammad Khan (NA-25), Zubair Khan (NA-42), Haji Imtiaz Ahmad Choudhry (NA-68) and Nasim Ali Shah (NA-39).
